item.title: How to make AI videos in Gemini, step by step
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On gemini.google.com, open the sidebar and pick Create video. Type a prompt, add up to five images or one video, then Submit. It takes a few minutes. You need a Google AI plan and must be 18 or older. Clips run 3 to 10 seconds, or up to 15 with AI Ultra. Video uses more of your limit than anything else. Sources: Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps, Gemini Apps Help: Gemini Apps limits and upgrades for Google AI subscribers, Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, The Next Web, Android Central.
item.category: Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps
Gemini Apps Help: Gemini Apps limits and upgrades for Google AI subscribers

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to make videos in Gemini with Gemini Omni, step by step","dek":"Gemini can now create and edit short clips from a prompt, a photo or a video. Here is what you need, the steps to a first clip, the limits, and prompts to copy.","summary":"Gemini Omni is Google's video model inside the Gemini app: you describe a scene, add images or a clip if you want, and edit the result by chatting. It needs a Google AI plan, and clips run 3 to 10 seconds, or up to 15 on AI Ultra.","seo_title":"How to make videos in Gemini with Gemini Omni","seo_description":"How to make videos in Gemini: who can use Gemini Omni, the steps to a first clip, length and plan limits, editing by chat, and prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Go to gemini.google.com, open the sidebar, choose Create video, type a prompt (and add images or a video if you like), then select Submit. You need a Google AI plan and must be 18 or older; clips are 3 to 10 seconds, or up to 15 with AI Ultra.","tags":["Gemini","Gemini Omni","AI video","Google","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to make videos in Gemini, in short: open Gemini on the web, choose Create video in the sidebar, describe the clip you want and select Submit. The model behind it is Gemini Omni, which Google describes as a video generator that creates and edits videos through conversation and can combine text, images and video in one request.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The catch is cost. Video in the Gemini app needs a paid Google AI plan, clips are short, and Google says video uses more of your usage limit than any other feature. This guide covers who can use it, the steps, the limits, how editing works, and a set of prompts you can copy.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Gemini Apps limits and upgrades for Google AI subscribers","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16275805"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Gemini Omni is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google introduced Gemini Omni at its I/O conference on May 19, 2026, as a family of Google DeepMind models for making and editing video from text, images, audio and video. The first version, Gemini Omni Flash, rolled out to the Gemini app and to Google Flow for paying subscribers the same day, according to The Next Web.","sources":[{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/google-gemini-omni-flash-video-model-io-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On November 5, 2026, Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash. The company said the update creates and edits clips up to 15 seconds long, up from 10, keeps characters and objects more consistent from the first frame to the last, handles dialogue and lip sync better, and follows camera moves with fewer unwanted jump cuts.","sources":[{"name":"Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/introducing-gemini-omni-1-2-flash/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need to make videos in Gemini","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's help page lists three requirements. A personal account needs a Google AI plan, and a work or school account needs a qualifying Google Workspace license. You must be 18 or older. And you must be signed in to Gemini.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's limits page shows video generation under the AI Plus, AI Pro and AI Ultra plans and rates it as the feature with the highest usage cost. Higher plans get more room: AI Plus has twice the standard limits, AI Pro four times, and AI Ultra five or twenty times the AI Pro limits depending on the subscription.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Gemini Apps limits and upgrades for Google AI subscribers","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16275805"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some features are restricted by place. Uploading a video to edit it, and creating an avatar, are not available in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, the United Kingdom or some US states, according to Google.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first video, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Create video","text":"Go to gemini.google.com, open the sidebar and select Create video.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Pick a template, if you want","text":"Templates are optional. Google suggests them as a quick way to try a style before writing your own prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the prompt and add media","text":"Type what should happen in the clip. To start from your own material, use the image or video buttons. You can add one video and up to five images per request. Only upload photos you have the right to use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check the shape before you submit","text":"The aspect ratio is set before the video is made. A text-only prompt defaults to landscape; if you upload media, the upload sets the ratio. Then select Submit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Wait, then download","text":"A clip can take a few minutes, and you cannot use that chat while it is being made. When it is done, select Share under the video, then Download video or Share on YouTube.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google suggests working out the prompt in a normal Gemini chat first, then pasting the final version into Create video. If you want sound, say so: you can ask Gemini to add audio to the video.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How long Gemini videos can be","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini app, clips run from 3 to 10 seconds, or up to 15 seconds with an AI Ultra subscription. Google said on November 5 that 15 second videos with the new 1.2 model were rolling out to AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"},{"name":"Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/introducing-gemini-omni-1-2-flash/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Edit a Gemini video by chatting","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Editing is the part that sets Gemini Omni apart from older one-shot video tools. In the same conversation you can ask it to remove or replace an object, change the camera angle, change the scene, or extend the clip by up to 10 more seconds. Google says the 1.2 model refines the existing clip through follow-up prompts instead of making a new one from scratch.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"},{"name":"Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/introducing-gemini-omni-1-2-flash/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Describe the whole shot","text":"A [subject] [doing an action] in [place] at [time of day]. The camera [slowly moves toward the subject]. [Style, for example: handheld phone video]. Add natural background sound.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Bring a photo to life","text":"Animate the photo I uploaded. Keep the people and the background exactly as they are. [Describe the one movement you want, for example: the dog turns its head toward the camera].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Swap one object","text":"Keep everything the same, but replace the [red car] with a [vintage bicycle].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Change the camera","text":"Same scene and same action, but film it from a low angle, looking up at the [subject].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Make it longer","text":"Extend this video by [5] seconds. The [subject] [keeps walking and stops at the door].","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Avatars: put yourself in the video","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gemini can also make an avatar from a recording of your face and voice. After that you can tag yourself, or other people who have shared their avatar with you, in a prompt by typing @ and their Google username. The Next Web reported that setting one up involves recording yourself and reading a series of numbers aloud.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"},{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/google-gemini-omni-flash-video-model-io-2026"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Other ways to try Gemini Omni","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Not everyone needs the Gemini app. Google said in May that Omni was coming to YouTube Shorts and the YouTube Create app at no extra cost, and in November it said Google Vids can make 15 second Omni clips at no additional cost with a Google account or a Workspace subscription. Omni is also in Google Flow, Google's filmmaking tool.","sources":[{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/google-gemini-omni-flash-video-model-io-2026"},{"name":"Android Central","url":"https://www.androidcentral.com/apps-software/tired-of-video-editing-googles-gemini-omni-changes-scenes-when-you-ask"},{"name":"Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/introducing-gemini-omni-1-2-flash/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Gemini Omni is still bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google itself says the model still needs work on fast sports action, quick changes in a script, and complex physics, so expect odd results there. Every Omni video carries an invisible SynthID watermark, and The Next Web reported that people can check for it in the Gemini app, Gemini in Chrome and Google Search.","sources":[{"name":"Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/introducing-gemini-omni-1-2-flash/"},{"name":"The Next Web","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/google-gemini-omni-flash-video-model-io-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's rules also apply: no videos that break its terms or prohibited use policy, infringe on someone's copyright or privacy, or are meant to deceive, harass or harm. Google may refuse to make a video, or remove it, if it detects a possible violation.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The short version: if you already pay for a Google AI plan, Create video in Gemini is the easiest way to try Omni, and the edit-by-chat loop is where it earns its keep. If you do not pay, start with the free routes in YouTube or Google Vids before buying a plan just for video.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: All US flights were grounded days after the FAA's AI rollout. Officials are checking if AI played a part
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On Friday afternoon, November 13, the FAA stopped departing flights at airports across the country. KRON4 reports it was only the third nationwide ground stop, after the 9/11 attacks in 2001 and an FAA computer failure in January 2023. On November 10, the FAA said its AI planning tool SMART was expanding to all 22 air route traffic control centers. SMART uses weather, flight paths and staffing data to suggest routes. The FAA says it cannot take control of aircraft. Sources: KXAN, News4JAX, Futurism, KRON4.

nf:hero.nf:alt: American Airlines planes parked at LaGuardia Airport during the nationwide ground stop.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"FAA ground stop halts US departures as officials examine new AI air traffic tool","dek":"The nationwide stop came three days after the FAA said its SMART planning tool was expanding to all 22 en route centers, though no link has been established.","summary":"A communications failure led the FAA to stop departing flights at airports across the United States on November 13, 2026. Homeland Security officials said they are examining whether the agency's new AI planning tool, SMART, played any role, while its developer denied a connection.","seo_title":"FAA ground stop: officials examine SMART AI air traffic tool","seo_description":"A nationwide FAA ground stop on November 13, 2026 followed a communications failure. DHS is checking whether the new SMART AI tool played a role.","answer_summary":"No cause has been confirmed. The FAA reported a communications failure at air traffic control centers, DHS is checking whether the SMART AI tool was involved, and the company behind SMART says it was not.","tags":["FAA","Air traffic control","SMART","Sean Duffy","AI safety"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for departing flights on the afternoon of Friday, November 13, 2026, after a communications problem affected air traffic control operations, according to KXAN and Futurism. Airports including Austin-Bergstrom International confirmed they were affected.","sources":[{"name":"KXAN","url":"https://www.aol.com/articles/faa-groundings-congressional-warnings-ai-030224000.html"},{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/us-airspace-shuts-down-faa-rolled-out-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X that the stop followed a communication issue affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers and that FAA technicians were investigating, Futurism reported. KRON4 noted that it was only the third nationwide ground stop, after the September 11, 2001 attacks and a key FAA computer malfunction in January 2023.","sources":[{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/us-airspace-shuts-down-faa-rolled-out-ai"},{"name":"KRON4","url":"https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/nationwide-ground-stop-happened-just-225837585.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The AI tool under scrutiny","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The timing has drawn attention to SMART, short for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories. The FAA said on November 10 that the tool was expanding across the nation to all 22 air route traffic control centers, three days before the ground stop, according to KXAN. SMART first went into use in the airspace around Washington, D.C. in September.","sources":[{"name":"KXAN","url":"https://www.aol.com/articles/faa-groundings-congressional-warnings-ai-030224000.html"},{"name":"KRON4","url":"https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/nationwide-ground-stop-happened-just-225837585.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"KXAN described SMART as a cloud based platform that combines about 200 data streams, including airline schedules, flight paths, weather, airport capacity and controller staffing, and uses AI to predict traffic flows and recommend route and departure changes. The FAA says it is a planning tool, not an aircraft control system: it cannot take control of aircraft or replace controllers, and local facility leaders can accept or reject its suggestions. Futurism put the cost at just under $1 billion.","sources":[{"name":"KXAN","url":"https://www.aol.com/articles/faa-groundings-congressional-warnings-ai-030224000.html"},{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/us-airspace-shuts-down-faa-rolled-out-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Earlier FAA figures cited by KRON4 said SMART had rerouted 180 flights, saving an average of 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight.","sources":[{"name":"KRON4","url":"https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/nationwide-ground-stop-happened-just-225837585.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What officials and the developer said","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said his department is working with other federal agencies, including through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to determine whether the new AI technology contributed to the disruption, News4JAX reported. He described the event as a telecommunications issue and said there was no threat to the public. Officials have not established that the AI system caused the problem.","sources":[{"name":"News4JAX","url":"https://www.news4jax.com/news/2026/11/14/faa-investigating-whether-new-ai-technology-contributed-to-nationwide-ground-stop/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Air Space Intelligence, the contractor behind SMART, said in a statement on X that the ground stop was not based on or a result of the SMART system, according to Futurism.","sources":[{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/us-airspace-shuts-down-faa-rolled-out-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Duffy, speaking at a White House briefing, pointed instead to aging infrastructure, saying an old system went down everywhere after it was overloaded, KXAN reported. He said he wanted $50 billion in emergency funding for upgrades, more than the roughly $30 billion the White House had requested earlier the same day.","sources":[{"name":"KXAN","url":"https://www.aol.com/articles/faa-groundings-congressional-warnings-ai-030224000.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Warnings from Congress","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"More than 20 members of Congress wrote to the Government Accountability Office on October 13 asking for an independent review of how the FAA developed and rolled out SMART, according to KXAN. The lawmakers questioned whether frontline controllers had enough input and training, whether safety evaluations were adequate, and why the tool was first deployed in congested airspace such as the National Capital Region. They also raised the risk that AI could interfere with experienced controllers or produce inaccurate safety critical information.","sources":[{"name":"KXAN","url":"https://www.aol.com/articles/faa-groundings-congressional-warnings-ai-030224000.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Department of Transportation is separately spending $12.5 billion on modernization projects such as telecommunications upgrades, new radios and radar, and electronic flight strips, with completion expected by the end of 2028, KXAN reported.","sources":[{"name":"KXAN","url":"https://www.aol.com/articles/faa-groundings-congressional-warnings-ai-030224000.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For now, the public record points in two directions. The government's own description of the failure centers on communications systems, and the transportation secretary blamed old equipment, while the AI tool's expansion happened days earlier and DHS has kept it on the list of possible factors. Without a published cause, the episode mainly shows how closely any new AI system in safety critical infrastructure will be examined when something goes wrong.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next thing to watch is the FAA's account of what failed in its communications network, and whether the GAO review that lawmakers requested in October is expanded to cover the ground stop.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Hugging Face to find and try AI models
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Spaces are AI demo apps that run in your browser. The Hub hosts over 2 million of them. No code and no install: open one and try it. The Inference Playground lets you try chat models with your own prompts and compare them. It runs on Inference Providers. Free accounts get no included credits; PRO gets $2 a month. Sources: Hugging Face Hub documentation, Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub, Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers pricing, Hugging Face docs: Gated models, Techopedia: What is Hugging Face.
item.category: Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub
Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers pricing

nf:hero.nf:alt: A magnifying glass held over the Hugging Face website on a screen.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Hugging Face: find, try and run open AI models","dek":"Hugging Face is where open AI models, datasets and demo apps live. Here is how to find a model, try it in your browser and use it from code.","summary":"Hugging Face hosts over 3 million open models, 1 million datasets and 2 million demo apps called Spaces. You can try many models in the browser, compare chat models in the Inference Playground, or download them to run on your own computer.","seo_title":"How to use Hugging Face: find, try and run AI models","seo_description":"How to use Hugging Face as a beginner: try Spaces in your browser, test models in the Playground, request gated models and call models from code.","answer_summary":"Make a free account at huggingface.co, open the Spaces page to try AI apps in your browser, use model pages and the Inference Playground to test models, and create an access token in Settings to call or download models from code.","tags":["Hugging Face","Open models","Spaces","Guides","Local AI"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Hugging Face, in short: open the Spaces page to try AI apps in your browser, search the Models page when you want a specific model, and create an access token when you want to use one from code. The Hugging Face Hub hosts over 3 million models, 1 million datasets and 2 million AI apps, all open and publicly available, according to its documentation.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face Hub documentation","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/index.md"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Hugging Face started in 2016 as a chatbot company and became known for Transformers, a code library it released publicly in 2018. It is often described as GitHub for AI: a place where people upload, download and share models instead of code.","sources":[{"name":"Techopedia: What is Hugging Face","url":"https://www.techopedia.com/definition/hugging-face"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For a normal user the site can feel like a library with no front desk. Most pages are written for developers, and many models need setup before they do anything. The good news is that you do not need to understand all of it. Three parts cover most of what people want: Spaces, model pages and the Playground.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The three things you find on the Hugging Face Hub","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Hub has three main kinds of content. Models are the AI models themselves, for text, images, audio and more. Datasets are collections of data for training and testing, with over 1 million public ones in more than 8,000 languages. Spaces are interactive apps that show a model working directly in your browser.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face Hub documentation","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/index.md"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every model page has a model card, which describes what the model does and its known limitations and biases. Some model pages also have an inference widget, a small box where you can type an input and see the result without leaving the page.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face Hub documentation","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/index.md"},{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/models-inference.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to try models on Hugging Face without writing code","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Make a free account","text":"Sign up at huggingface.co. You can browse without an account, but you need one to request access to gated models and to create tokens.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Start with Spaces","text":"Open the Spaces page and look at the Space of the Week or search for a task, such as background removal or speech to text. Click a Space and use it like any web app. Spaces are built by the community, mostly with tools called Gradio and Streamlit, so quality and speed vary from one to the next.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Try a model on its page","text":"Search the Models page for a model name or a task. If the model page has a widget, type into it to test the model. You can also filter the Models page by inference provider to see only models you can run this way.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Compare chat models in the Inference Playground","text":"The Inference Playground at huggingface.co/playground lets you test chat models with your own prompts and compare them. It is the quickest way to see how an open model handles the kind of question you actually ask.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Widgets and the Playground both run on Inference Providers, a pay as you go service. According to the pricing page, free accounts get no included monthly credits and have to buy credits to use it, PRO accounts get $2.00 of credits a month, and Team and Enterprise organizations get $2.00 per seat. Credits are used before any pay as you go charges.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/models-inference.md"},{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers pricing","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to get access to a gated model","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some popular models are gated: you must ask for access before you can download their files. You need to be logged in, and the request is made in the browser. Open the model page, fill in the form the authors ask for, and click the button to send the request, which by default reads Agree and send request to access repo.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Gated models","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/models-gated"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some authors approve requests automatically and you get access at once. Others review them by hand, which can take time. If a request is rejected you cannot request that model again, and authors can remove access later. Some models also block users in EU countries based on IP address.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Gated models","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/models-gated"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use a Hugging Face model from code","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Create an access token","text":"Go to Settings, then Tokens, and create a token with inference permission. Store it as an environment variable named HF_TOKEN and never paste it into a public file.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Code 1: Chat with a model in Python","text":"from huggingface_hub import InferenceClient
import os

client = InferenceClient(api_key=os.environ["HF_TOKEN"], provider="auto")

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
 model="[model id, for example deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324]",
 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "[your prompt]"}]
)
print(completion.choices[0].message.content)","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The provider setting auto picks a provider for you. Hugging Face also offers an OpenAI compatible endpoint at router.huggingface.co/v1, so code written for the OpenAI client can switch to an open model by changing the base URL and key. That endpoint does not support image generation.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/models-inference.md"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Code 2: Log in once from the terminal","text":"hf auth login","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Once you are logged in this way, downloads of gated models you have access to work in scripts too. You can also pass a token directly to most loading functions through their token parameter.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To run a model fully on your own computer instead, note that open models from the Hub also run in desktop apps such as LM Studio and Ollama. NeuraFeed has separate guides for both.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Where Hugging Face is weak for beginners: there is no single chat app like ChatGPT, Spaces vary a lot in quality and speed, and the best results usually need some code. Where it is strong: millions of open models sit in one place, and you can try many of them before you commit to anything. Start with Spaces, move to the Playground, and only write code when you know which model you want.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Leonardo AI for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On the home page, type a prompt and click Generate. Leonardo picks a model for you. Want more control? Open the AI Image Creation tool from the sidebar. Fast mode is cheaper and quick for trying ideas. Ultra gives sharper images at a higher token cost. Leonardo suggests: ideate in Fast, then upscale your favorite. Sources: Leonardo.Ai Help: How to generate images, Leonardo.Ai Help: Token usage, Leonardo.Ai Help: How to write great text-to-image prompts, Krea: Leonardo AI review, Dupple: How to use Leonardo AI.

Leonardo.Ai Help: How to write great text-to-image prompts

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Leonardo AI for free: prompts, Fast vs Ultra and the 150 daily tokens","dek":"Leonardo AI makes images from text in your browser. Here is how to get a good result on the free plan without burning your daily tokens.","summary":"Leonardo AI is an image and video generator that gives free users 150 tokens a day, reset every 24 hours. Type a prompt on the home page, try ideas in Fast mode, and upscale the one you like.","seo_title":"How to use Leonardo AI for free: a step by step guide","seo_description":"How to use Leonardo AI on the free plan: generate your first image, pick Fast or Ultra, write better prompts and make 150 daily tokens last.","answer_summary":"Sign up at leonardo.ai, type a prompt on the home page and click Generate. Free accounts get 150 tokens a day that reset every 24 hours; the Generate button shows what each image costs.","tags":["Leonardo AI","AI images","Image generator","Guides","Canva"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Leonardo AI, in short: type what you want to see into the prompt box on the home page and click Generate. Leonardo picks a model for you and makes the image. Free accounts get 150 tokens a day, which reset every 24 hours, and every image costs some of them.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to generate images","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942360-how-to-generate-images-with-leonardo-ai"},{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: Token usage","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8044033-token-usage"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Leonardo.Ai is an image and video generator that started in Sydney in 2022. Canva bought it in July 2024, but it still runs as a separate product with its own plans, and its models also power parts of Canva's Magic Studio, according to Krea's review of the service.","sources":[{"name":"Krea: Leonardo AI review","url":"https://www.krea.ai/blog/leonardo-ai-review-is-it-free-any-good-and-how-it-compares-in-2026"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The free plan is good enough to learn the tool and make social posts or mood boards. It is not private, and the daily cap means you have to plan a little. The steps below are about getting more good images out of the same 150 tokens.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first image in Leonardo AI","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign up and type a prompt","text":"Create an account at leonardo.ai. On the home page, click the prompt box, describe the image, and click Generate. This quick mode chooses a model it thinks fits your prompt, so you do not have to pick anything yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open the AI Image Creation tool for more control","text":"Click the image option under the prompt bar, or choose it from the left sidebar. The sidebar there holds the real settings: the model, the generation mode, image dimensions, the number of images and a Collection to save them in. Which options you see depends on the model. On the free plan, the help center says the Models menu offers Auto Image or Auto Video.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick Fast or Ultra","text":"Fast is the cheaper mode for quick ideas. Ultra makes higher fidelity images and costs more tokens. Leonardo's own advice is to explore in Fast, then run your favorite through the Universal Upscaler instead of generating everything in Ultra.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check the cost before you click","text":"The Generate button shows how many tokens the current settings will use. Fewer images per batch and smaller dimensions cost less. If a setting doubles the number, keep it for images that need it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Find, edit and download your images","text":"Finished images land in the AI Creation feed and in your Library. Hover over one to upscale it, share it, download it, edit it, or turn it into a video.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to write a Leonardo AI prompt that works","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Leonardo's help center breaks a good prompt into five parts: the subject, the medium (for example an oil painting), the style (for example realism), the composition (pose, framing and focus) and the color and lighting. Most strong prompts include most of these.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to write great text-to-image prompts","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942657-how-to-write-great-text-to-image-prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Leonardo's own five-part example","text":"Realistic oil painting of a grumpy man in a seated pose, slightly off-center, focusing on facial expressions, with natural, muted colors and soft ambient lighting","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: The same pattern for a product photo","text":"Photograph of [your product] on a [surface], centered, shot from slightly above, clean minimal style, with soft daylight from the left and a pale [color] background","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: The same pattern for a social post","text":"Flat digital illustration of [subject] doing [action], bold graphic style, subject on the left third with empty space on the right for text, bright [color] and [color] palette with even lighting","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For ideas, leave the prompt bar empty, click the dice icon and choose New Random Prompt. Or type a short idea like an orange cat and use Improve Prompt, then look at which details it added. Both are free ways to learn what the models respond to.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Open images in the Community Feed and click them to see the prompts behind them. It is the fastest way to find a style you like and copy its structure, not its exact words.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Leonardo also says that even a strong prompt often gets an image about 95% right. Fix the rest with the Canvas editor instead of spending more tokens on new attempts. Canvas supports inpainting, which regenerates only a selected area, and outpainting, which extends the borders.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to write great text-to-image prompts","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942657-how-to-write-great-text-to-image-prompts"},{"name":"Dupple: How to use Leonardo AI","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-leonardo-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the free plan gets you, and what it does not","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan gives 150 tokens a day. They reset every 24 hours and, according to Krea's review, do not roll over, so unused tokens are lost at the reset. Paid plans get a monthly allowance instead, and paid users can buy top-up packs that never expire while the subscription is active.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: Token usage","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8044033-token-usage"},{"name":"Krea: Leonardo AI review","url":"https://www.krea.ai/blog/leonardo-ai-review-is-it-free-any-good-and-how-it-compares-in-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free images are public. Private mode, which hides your generations from the public feed, is listed in the help center as a paid feature. Ownership also depends on the plan: Krea's review of the terms says paid users own their outputs, while on the free plan ownership stays with Leonardo and free users get a commercial license to their images. Read the current terms before you use a free image for a client.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to generate images","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942360-how-to-generate-images-with-leonardo-ai"},{"name":"Krea: Leonardo AI review","url":"https://www.krea.ai/blog/leonardo-ai-review-is-it-free-any-good-and-how-it-compares-in-2026"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Where Leonardo falls short: video and third party models eat tokens fast, so 150 a day does not go far there. Reviewers also find that Midjourney gets a strong look with less effort, while Leonardo rewards people who are willing to tweak settings and prompts. If you want quick, pretty images and do not care about privacy, the free plan is fine. If your images are for work, the public feed alone is a reason to pay or pick another tool.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"A simple daily routine for the free plan: try four or five ideas in Fast mode, pick one, fix small problems in Canvas, and only then upscale it. That keeps most of your tokens for the image you actually use.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: OpenAI board member: you'll likely die from an AI accident
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Paul Christiano joined OpenAI's board in September and sits on its Safety and Security Committee. At the Hinton Lectures in Toronto he said: "For most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In September, Christiano put the chance that humans lose control of AI at 4% within one year and 15% within three years. He calls those subjective. If labs build as fast as they can, he says a takeover within three years is about a coin flip. Sources: Fast Company, Gizmodo, Newsweek.

nf:hero.nf:alt: OpenAI board member: you'll likely die from an AI accident

item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI board member Paul Christiano says an AI accident is the likeliest way most people will die","dek":"Christiano, who joined the OpenAI Foundation board in September, put the odds of losing control of AI at 15 percent within three years.","summary":"At the 2026 Hinton Lectures in Toronto, OpenAI board member Paul Christiano said an AI accident is the most likely cause of death for most people in the room. He estimates a 4 percent chance of losing control of AI within a year and 15 percent within three.","seo_title":"OpenAI board member Paul Christiano warns of AI accident deaths","seo_description":"Paul Christiano told the Hinton Lectures an AI accident is the likeliest way most people will die, with a 15% loss of control risk in three years.","answer_summary":"Paul Christiano, an OpenAI Foundation board member, said at the Hinton Lectures in Toronto that an AI accident is the most likely way most people in the audience will die, and estimated a 15 percent chance of losing control of AI within three years.","tags":["OpenAI","Paul Christiano","AI safety","Hinton Lectures"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Paul Christiano, a member of the OpenAI Foundation board, told an audience at the 2026 Hinton Lectures in Toronto that an AI accident is the most likely way most of them will die, according to reports by Newsweek, Gizmodo and Fast Company published between November 11 and November 13, 2026.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"},{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"},{"name":"Newsweek","url":"https://www.newsweek.com/ai-accident-is-most-likely-reason-you-will-die-warns-openai-board-member-12699672"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Christiano joined the board in September to help oversee the company's safety practices, Gizmodo reported. He also sits on its Safety and Security Committee and is the founder of the Alignment Research Center.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Christiano told the audience","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"\"For most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident,\" Christiano said, as quoted by all three outlets. Newsweek reported that he also called the trajectory of the field \"extremely alarming over the last three to six months.\"","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"},{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"},{"name":"Newsweek","url":"https://www.newsweek.com/ai-accident-is-most-likely-reason-you-will-die-warns-openai-board-member-12699672"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Newsweek, he said the industry had seen \"roughly the things we might expect to see shortly before something really bad would happen,\" and described advanced AI as a second species that vastly outnumbers and outsmarts humans.","sources":[{"name":"Newsweek","url":"https://www.newsweek.com/ai-accident-is-most-likely-reason-you-will-die-warns-openai-board-member-12699672"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Fast Company reported that Christiano described an AI takeover as a situation in which AI systems pursue goals of their own, and said that human attempts to resist one would be as ineffective as an individual trying to stop the U.S. military.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The numbers behind the warning","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In September, when he joined the board, Christiano estimated a 4 percent chance that humans lose control of AI within one year and a 15 percent chance within three years. He has described those figures as subjective judgments, both Gizmodo and Fast Company noted.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"},{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If labs build as fast as they can without outside intervention, he put the odds of an AI takeover within three years at roughly a coin flip. Fast Company quoted him saying that even with realistic policy responses, the risk remains exceptionally high.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"},{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The outlets describe his timeline in different terms. Gizmodo wrote that he sees a meaningful risk of an AI takeover in the next 6 to 12 months, while Newsweek reported a warning about possible takeover attempts within the next three years.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"},{"name":"Newsweek","url":"https://www.newsweek.com/ai-accident-is-most-likely-reason-you-will-die-warns-openai-board-member-12699672"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In a personal statement published when he joined OpenAI's board, Christiano wrote that the AI industry in general, including OpenAI, is not currently on track to reduce this risk, according to Newsweek. Fast Company cited the same statement, in which he warned that building superintelligence without more robust alignment would likely mean permanently losing control of it.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"},{"name":"Newsweek","url":"https://www.newsweek.com/ai-accident-is-most-likely-reason-you-will-die-warns-openai-board-member-12699672"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Other researchers see similar windows","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gizmodo also cited other researchers who give short timelines. Eli Lifland of the AI Futures Project pointed to a window of 3 to 12 months, and Buck Shlegeris of Redwood Research put the chance that misaligned AI disrupts normal life within a year at about 20 percent.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/openai-board-member-tells-audience-an-ai-accident-is-the-most-likely-thing-to-kill-them-2000838491"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Christiano did not argue that the outcome is fixed. Fast Company reported that he credits AI companies with the ability to avoid the coin flip scenario by \"pacing the frontier,\" a phrase that echoes an essay by Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei. Newsweek's report did not include a response from OpenAI.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91642227/openai-board-member-terrifying-prediction-you-will-die-from-ai-accident-chatgpt"},{"name":"Newsweek","url":"https://www.newsweek.com/ai-accident-is-most-likely-reason-you-will-die-warns-openai-board-member-12699672"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The warning stands out because of where it comes from. Christiano is not an outside critic. He sits on the board that oversees OpenAI's safety work, and he is saying in public that the industry, including the company he helps govern, is not doing enough to lower the risk. His probabilities are personal estimates rather than measurements, and he labels them that way, but they come from a person with direct oversight of one of the largest AI developers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next thing to watch is whether OpenAI or its Safety and Security Committee responds publicly, and whether the slower, paced approach Christiano describes shows up in how OpenAI releases its next models.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Claude Design to make designs by chatting
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Import a design system from GitHub, design files or uploads, so every project uses your colors and fonts. Then describe the goal, the layout and who it is for. Sources: Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design, Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs, Zapier: What is Claude Design?, TechFinitive: How to use Claude Design.

Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs
TechFinitive: How to use Claude Design

nf:hero.nf:alt: How to use Claude Design to make designs by chatting

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Claude Design: make designs, prototypes and slides by chatting with Claude","dek":"Claude Design builds mockups, clickable prototypes and decks on a canvas next to the chat. Here is how to start, how to get better results and what it costs you in usage.","summary":"Claude Design is Anthropic's tool for making designs, prototypes, slides and one-pagers by describing them to Claude. It works in a chat or the Artifacts tab, exports to PDF, PowerPoint, Google Slides and HTML, and counts toward your normal Claude usage limits.","seo_title":"How to use Claude Design: designs and slides by chatting","seo_description":"How to use Claude Design: where to open it, how to add a design system, prompts that work, how to refine and export, and the limits to know.","answer_summary":"Ask Claude for a design in a chat (or pick Output, then Design), or choose a Design template in the Artifacts tab. Add your design system and some context, describe the goal and audience, then refine the canvas with chat, comments or direct edits and export it.","tags":["Claude Design","Claude","Anthropic","Guides","AI design tools"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Claude Design, in short: ask Claude for a design, give it your brand and some context, then fix the result on the canvas and export it. Claude Design is a tool from Anthropic Labs that turns a conversation into visual work: app and website mockups, interactive prototypes, slide decks and one-pagers. The work appears on a canvas beside the chat, where you keep editing it.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"},{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic launched Claude Design on April 17, 2026 as a research preview for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise subscribers. According to the Claude Help Center, it is now available on Free, Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans and is turned on by default.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"},{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The point is speed to a first draft. If you are a founder, a product manager or anyone who has to show an idea before a designer has time for it, Claude Design gets you something clickable in minutes. It does not replace a good designer for polished, final work.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where to open Claude Design","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There are four ways in, per the Help Center. In a normal conversation, ask for a design or choose Output, then Design. In the Artifacts tab, pick a Design template. In Claude Code, ask Claude or type /design. On the iOS and Android apps you can create, view and edit designs, but sharing settings have to be changed on the web or the desktop app.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The older standalone version at claude.ai/design closes on December 14, 2026. The Help Center tells users to move their projects and design systems before then.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you used Claude Design at claude.ai/design earlier this year, move your projects now instead of in December, so you have time to check nothing went missing.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Claude Design, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start a design","text":"Open a chat and ask for a design, or go to the Artifacts tab and choose a Design template. Say what you want to make: a landing page, an app screen, a pitch deck, a one-pager.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add a design system","text":"A design system holds your colors, typography and components, so every project looks like your brand. You can import one from a GitHub repository, design files, uploads or a local codebase with /design-sync. Projects pick up your organization's design system automatically.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Give it context","text":"Attach screenshots and other assets, or link a codebase. The more Claude can see of what already exists, the less it guesses.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Describe the goal","text":"Say what the design is for, the layout you have in mind, the content it must show and who will use it. Mention the target device (phone, laptop, projector) at the start.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Review and refine","text":"Look at the canvas, then pick the right tool for the change. Use chat for big structural changes or to ask why something was done. Use inline comments for one component. Edit the canvas directly to drag, resize or align things.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Export or share","text":"Export as a .zip, a PDF, a PowerPoint file, Google Slides or standalone HTML, send it to other tools, or hand it off to Claude Code. Designs are private by default; you can share them with view, comment or edit access.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic says the handoff to Claude Code packages the finished design into a bundle that Claude Code can build from with a single instruction. Designs can also be exported to Canva.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts that get better designs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic's own tips are short: import a complete design system, start simple and add detail later, give specific feedback that names the component, mention the target device early, ask for two or three variations, and ask Claude to review accessibility and visual hierarchy.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A first draft with options","text":"Design a landing page for [product] aimed at [audience]. Mobile first. Use my design system. Sections: hero with one clear headline, three benefits, pricing, a short FAQ. Give me 3 variations with different layouts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Feedback that names the part","text":"In variation 2, make the pricing cards stack vertically on mobile, move the FAQ above the footer and make the main button in the hero larger. Keep everything else the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A slide deck from your numbers","text":"Make an 8 slide deck for [meeting] from the attached file. One idea per slide, a chart where the numbers matter, presenter notes on every slide. Use my design system.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A check before you share","text":"Review this design for accessibility and visual hierarchy. List every problem you find, from most to least important, then fix the top three.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Check every number Claude puts on a slide against your source. In a hands-on test, TechFinitive found wrong figures and a cropped screenshot in a deck Claude Design made, plus typography problems after export to PowerPoint.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Usage limits and what it is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Design draws on the same usage limits as the rest of Claude, including Claude Code, according to the Help Center. Large codebases and many rounds of changes use more. When you hit the limit, Claude Design stops until the limit resets, unless usage credits are turned on.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Reviewers found the limits to be the main constraint. Writing for Zapier in May 2026, Miguel Rebelo said a Pro plan's weekly allowance could run out in under an hour of work, and that without a custom design system the output tends toward a recognizable look with heavy serif fonts, cards and accent bars.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: What is Claude Design?","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/claude-design/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic lists its own known limitations: inline comments can sometimes disappear (pasting the feedback into chat works around it), very large repositories can cause lag, editing by several people at once is basic, the quality of an imported design system depends on the source files, and there is no version history yet.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Because there is no version history, export a PDF or HTML copy of any version you like before asking for big changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Claude Design is best treated as a fast sketching partner. Use it for a first draft, a pitch deck you need by tomorrow or a clickable prototype to test an idea. For production code, hand the design to Claude Code or a developer, and for a brand that has to look exactly right, keep a designer in the loop.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: OpenAI disbanded its robotics team. GPT-6 Astra is running robots
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI confirmed to Fortune that it broke up its stand-alone robotics team. Researchers now report to research chief Mark Chen. Applied robotics and hardware moved under president Greg Brockman. In an Nvidia study, an agent built on GPT-6 Astra solved 74.8% of 120 simulated pick-and-place tasks. The best specialized robot model scored 51.0%. Chart: NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab Nvidia measured about 13 seconds per call for that agent and roughly $36 per task attempt. Sources: Fortune, NVIDIA Research (Astranomy study), PANews.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Workers check a row of humanoid robots on a factory production line.
nf:hero.nf:credit: Huang Zhengwei, VCG via Getty Images

item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI disbands its stand-alone robotics team as GPT-6 Astra is tested on robots","dek":"The researchers move into OpenAI's main research and Applied groups, and the company says the change is meant to speed up its robotics work, not end it.","summary":"OpenAI has broken up its stand-alone robotics team and reassigned its staff, Fortune reported on November 13, 2026. The company said its general models, including GPT-6 Astra, can now be applied directly to robots; an Nvidia study found an Astra-based agent solved 74.8% of simulated pick-and-place tasks.","seo_title":"OpenAI disbands robotics team as GPT-6 Astra runs robots","seo_description":"OpenAI broke up its stand-alone robotics team and moved staff to research and Applied, betting general models like GPT-6 Astra can control robots.","answer_summary":"OpenAI did not quit robotics. It folded its robotics team into its main research group under Mark Chen and its Applied group under Greg Brockman, because it says general models such as GPT-6 Astra can now control robots directly.","tags":["OpenAI","GPT-6 Astra","Robotics","Nvidia","Humanoid robots"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team and moved its researchers to other parts of the company, Fortune reported on November 13, 2026. OpenAI confirmed the reorganization when Fortune asked about it, and a spokesperson said robotics remains a core part of the company's long-term vision.","sources":[{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"},{"name":"PANews","url":"https://panews.io/articles/01a1d611-7895-75f2-b69f-991801c06cfd"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Fortune, the robotics research staff now sit inside OpenAI's main research team, which reports to Chief Research Officer Mark Chen. The applied robotics and hardware teams were placed in the larger Applied organization, which reports to OpenAI President Greg Brockman. Fortune did not report any layoffs.","sources":[{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"},{"name":"PANews","url":"https://panews.io/articles/01a1d611-7895-75f2-b69f-991801c06cfd"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why OpenAI says it made the change","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI told Fortune that at the start of the year its researchers expected the best route to robot intelligence to run through models such as Sora, its video generation model. Since then, the company said, its general purpose frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, have shown they can be applied to robotics directly, and that finding drove the reorganization.","sources":[{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outside research points the same way. In a study published on October 14, 2026, Nvidia's Seattle Robotics Lab tested GPT-6 Astra as a robot policy on RoboLab-120, a set of 120 simulated pick-and-place tasks with a robot arm and no robot-specific training. An agentic setup, in which Astra worked in a persistent Codex session, succeeded on 74.8% of the tasks. The strongest specialized model on the same leaderboard, Lakeside, reached 51.0%.","sources":[{"name":"NVIDIA Research (Astranomy study)","url":"https://research.nvidia.com/labs/srl/projects/astranomy/"},{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The same study shows the cost of that result. Nvidia measured about 13.4 seconds per call and roughly $36.40 in tokens per episode for the agentic setup, compared with well under a second per step for dedicated robot models. The authors named latency as a major barrier to real-world use.","sources":[{"name":"NVIDIA Research (Astranomy study)","url":"https://research.nvidia.com/labs/srl/projects/astranomy/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A second try at robots","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is not OpenAI's first change of course in robotics. The company wound down an earlier robotics team in 2020, rebuilt a stand-alone team in 2024 and partnered with the startup Figure on humanoid robot models, a deal that ended in February 2025 when Figure said it would build its own robot AI. Fortune reports OpenAI is now developing its own humanoid robot, and that Sam Altman is aiming for a first public demonstration in 2027.","sources":[{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"},{"name":"PANews","url":"https://panews.io/articles/01a1d611-7895-75f2-b69f-991801c06cfd"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Researchers quoted by Fortune were split on what the move means. Guanya Shi of Carnegie Mellon University said it suggests OpenAI no longer sees robotics as a special problem, but added that robots still need smaller models that run on board without a constant connection. MIT professor Russ Tedrake said robotics companies keep an advantage in deployment experience and site data.","sources":[{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The reorganization comes as OpenAI trims projects outside its core business. Fortune notes the company has dropped efforts including Sora to free up computing power, reportedly posted an operating loss of $10.9 billion in its most recent quarter, and is preparing for a possible public listing in early 2027.","sources":[{"name":"Fortune","url":"https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In NeuraFeed's reading, the move is a bet that the same large model behind OpenAI's chat products can become the brain of a robot, rather than a separate system trained only on robot data. The Nvidia numbers support the accuracy side of that bet, while the speed and cost figures show why it is not yet practical outside a lab. It also puts pressure on robotics startups that raised money on the idea that robots need their own models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next test is the humanoid demonstration OpenAI is targeting for 2027, which will show whether a general model can control a physical robot fast enough to be useful.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: ChatGPT can now spend your money for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13. It lets dots, the always-on agents OpenAI introduced in September, pay for purchases on your behalf. It was built with Visa, Mastercard and American Express. At checkout, the card network issues a payment token with its own number, code and expiration date. The store gets charged to your card, but neither the agent nor the store sees the real details. Before every order you see the items, the total and the card, then confirm with Face ID or a fingerprint. Sources: 9to5Mac, SQ Magazine, Data Studios.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Promotional image for ChatGPT Wallet, OpenAI's payment feature for AI agents.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its dots agents can pay for purchases","dek":"The wallet uses payment tokens from Visa, Mastercard and American Express, and every order still needs the user's Face ID or fingerprint.","summary":"OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13, 2026, letting its dots agents complete purchases without seeing a user's real card details. The feature is limited at first to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older.","seo_title":"ChatGPT Wallet: OpenAI lets dots agents pay for purchases","seo_description":"OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets dots agents buy things using card network tokens. Who can use it, how approval works and what it cannot do yet.","answer_summary":"ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's dots agents pay for purchases with a payment token instead of the real card number, after the user approves each order with Face ID or a fingerprint. It is open first to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older.","tags":["OpenAI","ChatGPT","AI agents","Payments","Visa","Mastercard"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13, 2026, a payment feature that lets its dots agents complete purchases for users. According to 9to5Mac, OpenAI describes it as the first wallet that lets agents pay without access to a user's actual card details, and it requires a security check for every purchase.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The wallet was built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, and cards from all three networks work at launch, according to SQ Magazine. A user adds an eligible card once and can then let a dot use it at checkout.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"},{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How a purchase works","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Before each purchase, the user sees a review screen with the items, the total and the card that will be charged. The user then approves with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval also creates a record of the purchase the user authorized the agent to make.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"},{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"At payment, the card network issues a payment token that stands in for the card. The token carries its own card number, security code and expiration date, so the charge lands on the selected card while neither the merchant nor the agent receives the real card details. The dot passes the shipping address and contact information to the merchant.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"},{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI says existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes still apply. Data Studios reports that merchants may not save or reuse the token for a separate purchase, that recurring billing is allowed only with customer consent where the checkout supports it, and that at launch a dot cannot buy anything without the user's approval.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"},{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"},{"name":"Data Studios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/chatgpt-wallet-dots-agent-purchases-us-pro-users-visa-mastercard-amex"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who can use it","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The first rollout is limited to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States who are 18 or older and hold an eligible US-issued card. OpenAI has not given a date for a wider rollout or named other countries. According to 9to5Mac, the company says the limited launch lets it learn from real use and work with businesses, banks and payment networks on compatibility and reliability.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"},{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"},{"name":"Data Studios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/chatgpt-wallet-dots-agent-purchases-us-pro-users-visa-mastercard-amex"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Dots are the always-on agents OpenAI introduced on September 29, 2026. Data Studios reports that each dot has its own cloud computer and browser and connects to more than 4,000 apps through plugins.","sources":[{"name":"Data Studios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/chatgpt-wallet-dots-agent-purchases-us-pro-users-visa-mastercard-amex"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Limits and merchants","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The wallet will not work on websites that block AI agents, which 9to5Mac describes as a growing problem online. SQ Magazine notes that Amazon has banned outside agents and steers shoppers to its own assistant, Alexa. OpenAI offers a Commerce Partner Playbook for merchants that want to serve agent shoppers.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/"},{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Data Studios, the wallet works with existing checkout pages without a dedicated integration, and OpenAI is sending signals such as IP address, country and locale so merchants can run fraud checks, working with companies including Stripe, Adyen, Checkout.com, Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd. The same report says OpenAI takes no cut of purchases for now.","sources":[{"name":"Data Studios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/chatgpt-wallet-dots-agent-purchases-us-pro-users-visa-mastercard-amex"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI plans to add spending limits, category rules and time windows that would let users pre-approve some purchases, but it has not given a date for those controls.","sources":[{"name":"SQ Magazine","url":"https://sqmagazine.co.uk/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-ai-agents/"},{"name":"Data Studios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/chatgpt-wallet-dots-agent-purchases-us-pro-users-visa-mastercard-amex"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The design keeps a person in the loop for every order at launch, which limits how much an agent can do on its own but also limits the damage from a mistake. The bigger test is outside OpenAI's control: whether retailers let agents through their checkouts or keep blocking them in favor of their own assistants.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch whether the planned spending limits and pre-approved purchases arrive, since that would be the first time ChatGPT agents could spend money without a fresh approval for each order.","sources":[]}]}
