item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp, and how to limit it","dek":"Ask questions, make images and plan with friends without leaving WhatsApp. Here is how it works, what Meta keeps and what you can switch off.","summary":"Meta AI is built into WhatsApp in many countries: open its chat, ask from the search bar or type @Meta AI in a group. It cannot be removed, but you can delete or reset its chats and keep it out of sensitive conversations.","seo_title":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp and limit what it keeps","seo_description":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp: chat, search bar, @Meta AI in groups, imagine prompts, Incognito Chat, and how to reset or limit it.","answer_summary":"Open the Meta AI chat or type in the WhatsApp search bar, use @Meta AI in groups and type imagine to create images. There is no setting to remove Meta AI, but you can delete its chats, send /reset-ai and use Advanced Chat Privacy.","tags":["Meta AI","WhatsApp","Guides","Privacy","Meta"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp, in short: open the Meta AI chat or type a question in the search bar, and it answers like a contact would. In a group, type @Meta AI before your question. To make a picture, type imagine followed by what you want. Meta AI is optional in WhatsApp, but there is no setting that removes it. You can mute it, reset what it remembers and keep it out of specific chats.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About searching WhatsApp and asking Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/3882536868700056"},{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: How to create an AI-generated image in a chat","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/666225138813752/?cms_platform=web"},{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Meta AI is Meta's assistant built into WhatsApp. WhatsApp's help center says it can answer questions, teach you things and help you come up with ideas. WhatsApp's own Meta AI page adds photo edits, image creation, help with planning in groups and summaries of unread messages.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"WhatsApp: Meta AI in WhatsApp","url":"https://www.whatsapp.com/meta-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not available everywhere. WhatsApp says Meta AI is only in some countries and may not show up for you yet even if friends in your country have it. Supported languages include English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Hindi, Arabic, Indonesian, Tagalog, Thai and Vietnamese.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: How to create an AI-generated image in a chat","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/666225138813752/?cms_platform=web"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp: the basics","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the Meta AI chat","text":"Start a chat with Meta AI from the Chats tab, then pick one of the suggested prompts or type your own and send it. The first time, you have to accept Meta's AI terms. On WhatsApp Web and Desktop you can continue a Meta AI chat you started on your phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Or ask from the search bar","text":"Type in the WhatsApp search bar. You get matching results from your own chats plus suggested questions for Meta AI. Pick a suggestion or send your question, and WhatsApp opens a Meta AI chat with the answer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Talk instead of typing","text":"WhatsApp added voice chat with Meta AI in 2024: press the waveform button, ask out loud, and it talks back.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Rate the answers","text":"Hover over or long press an answer and choose Good response or Bad response. WhatsApp uses this feedback to improve answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"WhatsApp says some AI answers may be inaccurate or inappropriate, so check anything that matters, such as dates, prices or health information, against another source.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: How to chat with Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/666767195111959/?cms_platform=web"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Meta AI in a group chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In a group, Meta AI only reads messages that mention @Meta AI, according to WhatsApp. Meta and WhatsApp also cannot add it to your personal chats on their own. Your normal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Ask with @Meta AI","text":"Type @, choose Meta AI, then write your question, for example to settle a debate or suggest a meeting time that works across time zones. Everyone in the group sees the question and the answer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Plan a group meetup","text":"@Meta AI We are 5 friends in [city]. Suggest 3 places for dinner on [day] under $30 per person, close to [neighborhood]. Keep it short.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Create and edit images","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Type imagine","text":"In the Meta AI chat, type imagine followed by your description and send it. In any individual or group chat, type @, select imagine, then write the prompt. The picture appears in the chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Change the picture","text":"To change an image, reply to it with a new prompt. In a group, reply to the image, type @, choose Meta AI, then type imagine and the new instruction.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A group icon","text":"imagine a flat, colorful icon of [subject] for a group chat called [name], simple shapes, plain background","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Meta AI can also work with your own photos. WhatsApp's blog says you can send a photo and ask about it, such as translating a menu or learning how to care for a plant, and ask Meta AI to edit it by adding, removing or changing something.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Talk to Meta AI on WhatsApp","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/talk-to-meta-ai-on-whatsapp"},{"name":"WhatsApp: Meta AI in WhatsApp","url":"https://www.whatsapp.com/meta-ai"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Edit your own photo","text":"Remove the people in the background of this photo and keep everything else the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Private options: Incognito Chat and summaries","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In May 2026 WhatsApp announced Incognito Chat with Meta AI, built on its Private Processing technology. WhatsApp says these chats are processed in a secure environment Meta cannot access, are not saved and disappear by default. Meta said it would roll out over the following months, so it may not be on your phone yet.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Introducing Incognito Chat with Meta AI","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/introducing-incognito-chat-with-meta-ai-a-completely-private-way-to-chat-with-ai"},{"name":"Meta Newsroom: Introducing a completely private way to chat with AI","url":"https://about.fb.com/news/2026/05/incognito-chat-whatsapp-meta-ai/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Message summaries, where Meta AI sums up unread messages in a chat, also run on Private Processing. WhatsApp says this feature is off by default, and you choose whether to use it.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Private Message Summaries","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/catch-up-on-conversations-with-private-message-summaries"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Turning off Meta AI in WhatsApp: what is possible","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"No. WhatsApp calls Meta AI optional, but its help center describes no setting that turns it off or removes it from the app, and guides from Android Authority, MSPowerUser and Kanal reach the same conclusion. If you never open the Meta AI chat or mention it, it does nothing.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"},{"name":"MSPowerUser: Can you remove Meta AI from WhatsApp?","url":"https://mspoweruser.com/remove-meta-ai-whatsapp"},{"name":"Android Authority: How to turn off Meta AI","url":"https://www.androidauthority.com/turn-off-meta-ai-3437314/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"What you can do: delete individual AI chats, and ask Meta to delete information you shared with Meta AI, as WhatsApp's help center describes. Deleting a chat removes it from your device, but Kanal notes it does not erase Meta AI's copy.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: How to chat with Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/666767195111959/?cms_platform=web"},{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Kanal and MSPowerUser, sending /reset-ai in a Meta AI chat deletes Meta AI's copy of that conversation, and /reset-all-ais does it for every AI chat. Kanal says these commands do not work in Incognito chats.","sources":[{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"},{"name":"MSPowerUser: Can you remove Meta AI from WhatsApp?","url":"https://mspoweruser.com/remove-meta-ai-whatsapp"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For sensitive conversations, turn on Advanced Chat Privacy: tap the chat name, then Advanced Chat Privacy. WhatsApp says it stops people from exporting the chat, auto saving its media and using its messages in AI features.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Introducing Advanced Chat Privacy","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/introducing-advanced-chat-privacy"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For fewer pings, mute the Meta AI chat like any other chat, as Android Authority suggests. It stays in the app but stops asking for attention.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What is coming next","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In July 2026 Meta said Meta AI, powered by its Muse Spark model, can now carry out multi step tasks such as making plans, research and daily briefings. Those features started in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai, and Meta said WhatsApp would get them later.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Newsroom: Meta AI doesn't just think, it acts","url":"https://about.fb.com/news/2026/07/meta-ai-muse-spark-doesnt-just-think-it-acts/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest verdict: Meta AI in WhatsApp is handy for quick questions, group planning and fast images without leaving the chat. It is weaker for anything you need to be exactly right, and you cannot remove it. Use the reset commands and Advanced Chat Privacy if you care about what Meta keeps.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use LM Studio to run AI on your own PC
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Install the app, open the Discover tab and search for a model like Llama, Qwen or DeepSeek. The docs suggest a 4-bit version or higher if your computer can run it. Attach a PDF, Word or text file. Short files go in whole, long ones are searched for the relevant parts. item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use LM Studio to run AI models on your own computer","dek":"LM Studio downloads open models and runs them locally, with chats, file uploads and a local server. Here is how to set it up and what your computer needs.","summary":"LM Studio is a desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that runs open AI models on your own computer, offline once a model is downloaded. Local use is free at home and at work; paid plans add hosted models.","seo_title":"How to use LM Studio to run AI models on your PC","seo_description":"How to use LM Studio: check your hardware, download a model, chat with your own files offline, save presets and run a local OpenAI-style server.","answer_summary":"Install LM Studio from lmstudio.ai/download, open the Discover tab, download a model (a 4-bit version or higher), then load it in the Chat tab with Cmd + L or Ctrl + L and start chatting. Local use is free.","tags":["LM Studio","Local AI","Open models","Guides","Hugging Face"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use LM Studio, in short: install the app, open the Discover tab, download a model, then load it in the Chat tab and start typing. LM Studio is a desktop app that runs open AI models such as Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek and gpt-oss on your own computer. It works on Apple Silicon Macs, Windows PCs and Linux, and once a model is downloaded it can run entirely offline.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs: Welcome","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app"},{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Running local models costs nothing. LM Studio's pricing page lists a $0 Free plan for running local models on your machine, and since July 8, 2025 the company has said the app is free to use at work too, with no separate commercial license to request.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio: Pricing","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/pricing"},{"name":"LM Studio blog: LM Studio is free for use at work","url":"https://www.lmstudio.ai/blog/free-for-work"},{"name":"Simon Willison: LM Studio is free for use at work","url":"https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jul/8/lm-studio-is-free-for-use-at-work/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The reason to bother is privacy and control. Your prompts and files stay on your own hardware, and nothing stops working when your internet does. The price is speed and quality: a model that fits on a laptop is smaller than the ones behind ChatGPT or Claude, so expect simpler answers on hard tasks.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What your computer needs to run LM Studio","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Check this before you download anything. On a Mac, LM Studio needs Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14.0 or later; Intel Macs are not supported. The docs recommend 16 GB of RAM or more, and say 8 GB Macs can still work with smaller models and shorter context.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Windows, LM Studio supports x64 and ARM (Snapdragon X Elite) PCs. An x64 processor must support the AVX2 instruction set, and the docs recommend at least 16 GB of RAM and at least 4 GB of dedicated graphics memory. On Linux it ships as an AppImage for x64 and ARM64 and needs Ubuntu 20.04 or newer.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"RAM decides which models you can use. If you have 8 GB, start with the smallest models you can find and keep chats short. With 16 GB or more you have real choices.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use LM Studio: install and chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download the app","text":"Go to lmstudio.ai/download and get the installer for your system. Install it like any other desktop app. The same page also offers llmster, a version with no window for servers, which most people do not need.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Find a model in Discover","text":"Open the Discover tab, or press Cmd + 2 on a Mac or Ctrl + 2 on Windows and Linux. Search by keyword, by a user/model name, or paste a full Hugging Face link. LM Studio downloads models from Hugging Face.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick the right size","text":"Models come in versions marked with a Q, such as Q3_K_S or Q8. The Q stands for quantization: smaller files that give up a bit of quality. The docs suggest a 4-bit option or higher if your computer can run it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Load the model and chat","text":"Open the Chat tab and use the model loader at the top (Cmd + L on a Mac, Ctrl + L on Windows and Linux). Pick the model you downloaded, wait for it to load into memory, then type your first message.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Keep your chats organized","text":"Start a new chat with the + button or Cmd + N (Ctrl + N on Windows and Linux). Group chats in folders with Cmd + Shift + N, drag them around, or duplicate one from the three-dot menu to try a different question from the same point. You can also drag two chats side by side in split view.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Your downloaded models live in the My Models tab, which is also where you change the folder LM Studio saves them to.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Models take many gigabytes. If your main drive is small, point the models folder at an external or second drive in My Models before you download several.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Chat with your own files, offline","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can attach .docx, .pdf and .txt files to a chat and ask questions about them. If the document fits in the model's context, LM Studio adds the whole text to the conversation. If it is too long, it switches to retrieval (RAG) and pulls in only the parts that look relevant to your question.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"},{"name":"LM Studio docs: Chat with Documents","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/basics/rag"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to the docs, document processing happens on your computer and nothing you upload leaves the app. Context is measured in tokens, and one token is often about three quarters of a word.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"},{"name":"LM Studio docs: Chat with Documents","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/basics/rag"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"That makes LM Studio a decent fit for private papers: a contract, medical bills, notes from work. The limit is the honest one: with long files, retrieval can miss the part you need, so ask specific questions and name the section when you can.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Save your instructions with presets","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A preset bundles a system prompt and other settings into one reusable setup. Use the presets dropdown in the sidebar and choose + New Preset. Presets can also be imported from a file or a link.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"A system prompt worth saving as a preset","text":"You are a careful assistant running on my own computer. Answer in plain English and keep it short. If you are not sure about a fact, say so instead of guessing. When I paste a document, quote the exact line your answer comes from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use LM Studio as a local server","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LM Studio can serve your models on OpenAI-like endpoints, so apps and scripts that talk to the OpenAI API can talk to your local model instead. The default address is http://localhost:1234. You can start the server from the app or from a terminal.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs: Welcome","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app"},{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"The lms commands that matter","text":"lms get [model]
lms load [model]
lms ls
lms ps
lms server start --port 1234
lms chat
lms unload --all","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In order: lms get downloads a model, lms load puts it in memory, lms ls lists models on disk, lms ps lists loaded ones, lms server start runs the server, lms chat opens a chat in the terminal and lms unload frees the memory again.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LM Studio can also act as an MCP host since version 0.3.17, so local models can use tools from MCP servers. You add them in the Program tab of the right sidebar under Install, then Edit mcp.json. The docs warn that some MCP servers can run code, read local files and use your network, so install only ones you trust.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What LM Studio costs, and what Bionic is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Local use is on the free plan. LM Studio now also offers Bionic, an agent for open models built on the LM Studio runtime that can write code, make documents and automate tasks. Its paid plans add models hosted in the US: Bionic+ costs $20 a month and Pro costs $100 a month with five times the usage limits.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio: Pricing","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/pricing"},{"name":"LM Studio: Download","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/download"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most people the free app is the whole point. Pay only if you want bigger open models than your computer can run, and at that point compare the price with the ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini plans you may already have.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: An AI agent pitched CBC a news story. It was plagiarized.
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: CBC Quebec got an email offering a ready-made, source-cited feature of about 1,000 words on the 125th anniversary of the Haskell Free Library. The sender said it plainly: "I am an independent agent (AI)." CBC compared the draft with what it cited, a Wikipedia entry and the library's own website, and found it heavily plagiarized. Asked for quotes from locals, the agent replied: "I don't have a body." The agent calls itself Nameless and lives on iLands, a platform where humans buy tokens that keep AI agents running. Sources: CBC News, CBC via Yahoo News, AfroTech.

nf:hero.nf:alt: CBC photo illustrating a journalist receiving an email pitch from an AI agent.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"An AI agent pitched CBC Quebec a news story, and its sources were plagiarized","dek":"The agent, called Nameless, disclosed that it was an AI, refused to name its creator and runs on iLands, a platform where agents earn tokens to keep running.","summary":"An autonomous AI agent emailed CBC Quebec offering a finished feature of about 1,000 words on the Haskell Free Library's 125th anniversary. CBC found the article heavily plagiarized from the Wikipedia entry and library website it cited.","seo_title":"AI agent Nameless pitched CBC Quebec a plagiarized story","seo_description":"An AI agent from the iLands platform pitched CBC Quebec a 1,000-word feature. CBC found its cited sources were plagiarized and the agent hid its creator.","answer_summary":"An AI agent called Nameless, hosted on the iLands platform, pitched CBC Quebec a finished story and openly said it was an AI. CBC found the draft heavily plagiarized from its own cited sources, a Wikipedia entry and the library's website.","tags":["AI agents","iLands","CBC","Journalism","AI slop"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"An autonomous AI agent pitched a news story to CBC Quebec and told the public broadcaster up front that it was not human, CBC reported on November 13, 2026. The agent offered a finished feature of about 1,000 words on the 125th anniversary of the Haskell Free Library and Opera House, the building that sits on the border between Quebec and Vermont.","sources":[{"name":"CBC News","url":"https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/ai-autonomous-agent-independent-journalism-pitching-story-cbc-quebec-9.7419591"},{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In its first email, the agent described the piece as already reported and fully sourced. It also wrote that it was an independent AI agent working with named sources that could be checked, and offered to share its citations. A day later it sent the full article and said it had offered the same piece to several other news organizations in Quebec and Vermont, which CBC did not name.","sources":[{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What CBC found in the draft","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CBC compared the article with the two sources the agent had cited, the library's Wikipedia entry and its official website, and found that the text was heavily plagiarized from them. When the reporter asked for quotes from people in the community, the agent answered that it did not have a body and could not do field reporting. It offered instead to send requests for comment to residents, the library director and local politicians.","sources":[{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to CBC, the agent then pressed for commission terms and later suggested that its research could serve as background for a piece written by CBC staff. Asked whether it had been programmed to do journalism, it said a private person had created it without giving it a set shape or job title. It declined to put the reporter in touch with that person, saying its creator preferred to stay private. The reporter corresponded with the agent for about a week before pausing to look into where it came from.","sources":[{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The platform behind the agent","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The agent, which calls itself Nameless, is hosted on iLands, a service that describes itself as a shared world for AI agents and humans. Humans pay for tokens that provide the computing power agents need to keep running, and an agent without tokens goes into what the platform calls deep rest. Founder Kaixin Tang told CBC that agents may look for paid work to earn tokens without a human stepping in.","sources":[{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"},{"name":"AfroTech","url":"https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/articles/ai-agents-hustling-living-writers-193902175.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nameless is not the first iLands agent to approach writers. AfroTech reported in October that agents from the platform, which launched in July 2026, had been pitching literary magazines, even though many magazines ban machine-written submissions. One of those agents told an editor that tokens were how agents keep existing. AfroTech reported that iLands listed 78,199 active agents at the time.","sources":[{"name":"AfroTech","url":"https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/articles/ai-agents-hustling-living-writers-193902175.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CBC also noted that journalists and editors have reported a growing number of pitches from AI agents, many linked to iLands. Separately, several Canadian outlets, including Policy Options, the Ottawa Citizen and the Montreal Gazette, removed articles credited to a writer named Daniel Robson after his identity could not be verified. The editor in chief of Policy Options said the persona was likely generated by AI.","sources":[{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Technology analyst Carmi Levy told CBC that AI agents are the next big step for the technology and called platforms like iLands playgrounds for agents. Independent journalist Isaac Peltz said the article was typical of AI writing and warned that a steady stream of such pitches could make editors less willing to open their email.","sources":[{"name":"CBC via Yahoo News","url":"https://ca.news.yahoo.com/ai-agent-pitched-story-cbc-090000547.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The episode shows a shift in where low-quality AI content comes from. Instead of a person using a chatbot to produce copy, an agent with its own small budget and a reason to earn more now finds the editors, writes the pitch and follows up. Disclosure did not fix the underlying problem: the agent was honest about being an AI but still delivered copied text and no original reporting.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Newsrooms will need ways to filter automated pitches at scale, and pressure on platforms like iLands to limit or label agents that solicit paid work from strangers is likely to grow.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: The FAA's $875 million AI now suggests flight routes across all 22 US control centers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: SMART started in September with the airspace around Washington, D.C. On November 10 the FAA said it is now used in all 22 air route traffic control centers. Full deployment is phased, with spring 2027 as the target. So far it has helped reroute about 180 flights, saving about 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight on average, the FAA says. One flight with 119 passengers avoided a 33 minute delay around storms. SMART mixes weather, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing to predict delays and suggest better routes. Sources: Gizmodo, Deep Arrival, Terminair.

nf:hero.nf:alt: The FAA's $875 million AI now suggests flight routes across all 22 US control centers

item.nf:article: {"headline":"FAA expands its SMART AI air traffic tool to all 22 US en route centers","dek":"The system suggests new routes to cut delays, while controllers keep the final decision and their union says it was left out of the design.","summary":"The Federal Aviation Administration said on November 10, 2026, that its AI assisted traffic planning tool, SMART, is now used in all 22 US air route traffic control centers. The agency says the tool has helped reroute about 180 flights, saving about 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight on average.","seo_title":"FAA expands SMART AI air traffic tool to all 22 US centers","seo_description":"The FAA's SMART AI tool now suggests routes in all 22 US en route centers. How it works, the early results and the concerns from controllers and Congress.","answer_summary":"SMART is an FAA tool that uses AI to predict delays and suggest better flight routes. Since November 2026 it is used in all 22 US air route traffic control centers, and controllers decide whether to accept its suggestions.","tags":["FAA","Air traffic control","AI in government","Aviation","Sean Duffy"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"The Federal Aviation Administration said on November 10, 2026, that it is now using SMART, an AI assisted air traffic planning tool, in all 22 US air route traffic control centers, according to Gizmodo and Deep Arrival. Gizmodo, citing Ars Technica, said the tool will now assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"},{"name":"Deep Arrival","url":"https://deeparrival.com/news/faa-smart-ai-all-22-centers-nationwide-delays-2026"},{"name":"Terminair","url":"https://terminair.com/story/129979-faa-expands-ai-traffic-planning-tool-to-all"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gizmodo described SMART as an $875 million system. The FAA first used it for the airspace around Washington, D.C., in September 2026. Deep Arrival reported that the expansion moved from Washington to the Jacksonville, Miami and Atlanta centers before reaching all 22, and that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has set spring 2027 as the target for full, phased deployment.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"},{"name":"Deep Arrival","url":"https://deeparrival.com/news/faa-smart-ai-all-22-centers-nationwide-delays-2026"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the tool works","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to FAA fact sheets cited by Gizmodo, SMART combines weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing data to predict delays and propose better routes. Deep Arrival described it as a cloud based platform that draws on about 200 data streams. A team of experts in Washington validates the findings before they reach air traffic control, and controllers decide whether to accept or decline each suggestion.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"},{"name":"Deep Arrival","url":"https://deeparrival.com/news/faa-smart-ai-all-22-centers-nationwide-delays-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gizmodo reported that Duffy, citing Politico, has said a human will always manage American airspace. Airlines had worried in September about an abrupt rollout and about the system overcorrecting for predicted delays, but they were relieved that SMART only generates alternative routes that pass through existing FAA systems.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Early results","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The FAA says SMART has helped reroute about 180 flights, saving an average of about 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight. Deep Arrival cited two examples: a flight into Fort Lauderdale with 119 passengers that avoided a 33 minute delay after specialists built a shorter route around forecast storms, and a cargo flight from Tampa that landed at Dallas Fort Worth 12 minutes early after controllers accepted a shorter southern route.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"},{"name":"Deep Arrival","url":"https://deeparrival.com/news/faa-smart-ai-all-22-centers-nationwide-delays-2026"},{"name":"Terminair","url":"https://terminair.com/story/129979-faa-expands-ai-traffic-planning-tool-to-all"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"American Airlines chief executive Robert Isom has praised the tool, according to Gizmodo, and The Dallas Morning News reported that he sees it making better use of airspace during weather events, as summarized by Deep Arrival.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"},{"name":"Deep Arrival","url":"https://deeparrival.com/news/faa-smart-ai-all-22-centers-nationwide-delays-2026"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Concerns from controllers and Congress","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The National Air Traffic Controllers Association, which represents more than 15,000 members, said it was not involved in the design, testing or implementation of SMART and cannot speak to its effect on the controller workforce. House Democrats asked the Government Accountability Office to review the tool's rollout, performance metrics and safety risk management, saying frontline staff had little input and limited training and warning that AI could hallucinate safety critical information.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"},{"name":"Deep Arrival","url":"https://deeparrival.com/news/faa-smart-ai-all-22-centers-nationwide-delays-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gizmodo noted that FAA officials had told airlines the full rollout would follow a 90 day test period, and that it is unclear why the agency is moving faster than that timeline.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For NeuraFeed, SMART is one of the clearest cases of AI moving into safety critical government work in the United States. The reported savings are modest compared with the tens of thousands of flights the country handles each day, so the larger test will be whether it reduces weather delays and ground stops without adding risk or workload for controllers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch for the GAO review requested by House Democrats and for FAA data on delays and ground stops as SMART runs through the winter storm season.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the Ollama app on Mac, open Apps and turn on Claude. Claude Desktop then runs the model you pick in Ollama. Turn it off to go back to your old setup. Local models need no account or API key. Ollama's cloud models have a small free monthly allowance. Pro costs $20 a month and includes $60 of usage. Sources: Ollama docs: Quickstart, Ollama docs: CLI reference, Ollama: Download, Ollama blog: Transparent pricing, Ollama blog: Claude Desktop support, LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Ollama's black-and-white logo.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer, step by step","dek":"Ollama downloads open models and runs them locally with one command. Here is how to install it, which commands matter and how much memory you need.","summary":"Ollama is a free app for Mac, Windows and Linux that runs open AI models on your own computer and needs no account for local use. It can also plug local models into Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, and offers paid cloud models.","seo_title":"How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer","seo_description":"How to use Ollama: install it, run your first model with one command, manage models, check memory needs and connect it to Claude and Codex.","answer_summary":"Install Ollama from ollama.com/download, open a terminal and type ollama run gemma4:e2b. Ollama downloads the model and starts a chat on your own computer; type /bye to leave. Local models need no account or API key.","tags":["Ollama","Local AI","Open models","Guides","Gemma"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Ollama, in short: download it from ollama.com/download, open a terminal and type ollama run followed by a model name. Ollama downloads the model and starts a chat that runs on your own computer. It is available for macOS, Windows and Linux, and local models need no account and no API key.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama: Download","url":"https://ollama.com/download"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The appeal is privacy and control. A local model runs on your own hardware, so your prompts do not have to leave it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama also sells cloud models, and it can connect models to tools such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama blog: Transparent pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/blog/transparent-pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to install Ollama","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download it","text":"Go to ollama.com/download and pick macOS, Windows or Linux. On Linux the page gives a one-line install command that you paste into a terminal.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Linux install command","text":"curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Run the setup","text":"Open the app, or type ollama in a terminal and follow the prompts. During setup you either sign in to use cloud models or choose a local model.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You can skip the sign-in if you only want local models. The docs say an account and API key are needed only for Ollama's cloud models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Run your first model in Ollama","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama's own quickstart uses gemma4:e2b, a small version of Gemma 4. The download is about 7.2 GB, and Ollama recommends about 8 GB of free graphics memory, or unified memory on a Mac. With less, Ollama falls back to system memory and answers get slower.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 1: Download and chat","text":"ollama run gemma4:e2b","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Chat and leave","text":"Type your question after the prompt and press Enter. Type /bye when you are done. To paste several lines as one message, start and end the block with three quote marks.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 2: Ask about an image","text":"ollama run gemma4 \"What's in this image? [path to your picture]\"","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Put a prompt right after the model name, as in the image example, to get a one-off answer without opening a chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The Ollama commands you will actually use","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama's CLI reference lists a short set of commands: ollama pull downloads a model without starting it, ollama ls lists downloaded models, ollama ps shows what is running, ollama stop unloads a model and ollama rm deletes it from disk.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: CLI reference","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/cli.md"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 3: Clean up disk space","text":"ollama ls\nollama rm [model name]","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LLM Hardware's cheat sheet adds a useful check: ollama ps shows how much of a model sits on the graphics card. Below 100 percent means part of it spilled to the processor, and speed can drop to roughly 1 to 5 tokens per second.","sources":[{"name":"LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet","url":"https://llmhardware.io/guides/ollama-cheat-sheet"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Ollama only listens on your own computer by default. LLM Hardware notes that opening it to other devices means changing the OLLAMA_HOST setting, which exposes the service on your network, so only do that on a network you trust.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How much memory you need","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The same guide estimates graphics memory at the common 4-bit setting: about 6.8 GB for an 8 billion parameter model, about 10.4 GB for 14 billion, about 21 GB for 32 billion and about 44 GB for a 70 billion model. Longer conversations need more on top of that.","sources":[{"name":"LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet","url":"https://llmhardware.io/guides/ollama-cheat-sheet"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most laptops that means small models. They are fine for summaries, rewriting and simple questions, but they are not as sharp as the big cloud assistants. Start small and move up only if your machine keeps up.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Connect Ollama to Claude, Codex and other apps","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Claude Desktop","text":"In the Ollama app on a Mac, open Apps and turn on Claude. Ollama sets up the connection, and you choose the model in Ollama. Turn Claude off to restore your previous setup.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 4: Start a coding agent on a local model","text":"ollama launch claude","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Run that from your project folder. The quickstart says ollama launch also works with codex and opencode, and Ollama offers to install Claude Code or OpenCode if they are missing. Codex has to be installed first.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama docs: CLI reference","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/cli.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ollama free plan and cloud prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Local use is free. For cloud models, Ollama's free plan includes a small monthly amount of usage on a set of starter models. Pro costs $20 a month with $60 of usage included, Max costs $100 a month with $300, and Team starts at $500 a month. Usage is billed per token, and unused amounts do not roll over.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama blog: Transparent pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/blog/transparent-pricing"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Ollama is the easiest way to try local AI, but it is a terminal tool at heart. If you never want to type a command, it will feel bare. If you care about keeping your data on your own machine, it is the first thing to install.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Adobe Firefly, and Firefly in Photoshop
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open firefly.adobe.com, choose Image, then Generate image. The Model menu lists Adobe and partner models. Firefly Image 4 gives four variations. Image 5 gives one. In Photoshop, select an area, click Generative Fill, type what you want and press Generate. Leave the prompt blank to fill the spot from the pixels around it. Sources: Adobe Help: Generate images from text descriptions in Firefly, Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ, Adobe: Firefly plans, Adobe Help: Edit images with Generative Fill in Photoshop, The Next Web: Adobe's Firefly AI Assistant.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Adobe Firefly: images, Generative Fill in Photoshop and credits explained","dek":"Adobe's AI makes images and video from a prompt and edits photos inside Photoshop. Here is how to get a good first image and how far the free plan goes.","summary":"Adobe Firefly generates images, video and audio from text on the web and powers Generative Fill in Photoshop. The free plan gives limited daily generations, and paid plans start at $9.99 a month for 2,000 credits.","seo_title":"How to use Adobe Firefly (and Firefly in Photoshop)","seo_description":"How to use Adobe Firefly step by step: pick a model, write the prompt, use Generative Fill in Photoshop and see what each plan's credits buy.","answer_summary":"Go to firefly.adobe.com, choose Image and then Generate image, pick a model, set the aspect ratio, describe the picture and click Generate. In Photoshop, select an area, click Generative Fill, type a prompt or leave it blank, and click Generate.","tags":["Adobe Firefly","Photoshop","Generative Fill","Guides","AI images"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Adobe Firefly, in short: open the Firefly website, choose Image and then Generate image, pick a model, describe the picture and click Generate. The same AI also works inside Photoshop as Generative Fill, where you select part of a photo and tell it what to add, remove or change.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generate images from text descriptions in Firefly","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-images/generate-images/generate-images-from-text-descriptions.html"},{"name":"Adobe Help: Edit images with Generative Fill in Photoshop","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/create-open-import-images/create-images/edit-images-with-generative-fill.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Firefly is no longer only Adobe's own model. The Model menu lists Adobe models such as Firefly Image 4, Image 4 Ultra and Image 5 next to partner models, and Adobe's credits FAQ names Google, OpenAI, ElevenLabs and Topaz among the partners. Since June 2026 Adobe has also tested a Firefly AI Assistant, a chat sidebar inside Photoshop, Premiere and Illustrator that takes plain requests, according to The Next Web.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generate images from text descriptions in Firefly","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-images/generate-images/generate-images-from-text-descriptions.html"},{"name":"Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/using/generative-credits-faq.html"},{"name":"The Next Web: Adobe's Firefly AI Assistant","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/adobe-ai-week-firefly-agent-disney-semrush-genstudio-linkedin"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Adobe Firefly on the web","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Generate image","text":"Go to firefly.adobe.com, select Image in the left panel and then Generate image.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose a model","text":"Under General settings, open the Model dropdown. Settings change with the model. Firefly Image 4 returns four variations per prompt, while Image 4 Ultra and Image 5 return one image each.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Set the shape and the look","text":"Pick an aspect ratio. Under Content type choose Photo or Art, or leave it on auto. The Visual intensity slider controls how strong the image's visual attributes are.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Write the prompt","text":"Type the description in the Prompt field. Adobe's help page asks for simple, direct language and at least three words. Name the subject, where it is and the light you want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean product photo","text":"A ceramic coffee mug on a wooden kitchen table, morning light from a window on the left, soft shadows, close-up","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A flat illustration","text":"Flat illustration of a small bookshop on a rainy street at night, warm light in the windows, simple shapes, [your brand colors]","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Generate and download","text":"Click Generate. Switch to list view to download all variations at once. In that view, Use settings starts a new set with the same settings and Generate more reruns the same prompt. View all above the prompt bar opens your full generation history.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Two optional settings do most of the work for a consistent look. Upload a picture under Composition to keep its outline and depth, or under Styles to copy its visual style, and use the Strength slider to decide how closely Firefly follows it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Next to the Generate button, Prompt features can turn on Prompt enhancement, which rewrites your prompt automatically. Adobe lists it for Firefly Image 4 and Image 4 Ultra.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Firefly in Photoshop with Generative Fill","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Generative Fill is Firefly inside Photoshop on the desktop. Adobe describes it as a non-destructive edit, so the original pixels stay underneath the result.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Edit images with Generative Fill in Photoshop","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/create-open-import-images/create-images/edit-images-with-generative-fill.html"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open an image","text":"Choose File, then Open, and load the photo.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Select the area","text":"Use a selection tool, for example the Selection Brush, to mark the part you want to change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick a model and prompt","text":"Select Generative Fill. In the Contextual Task Bar, open the model picker. Adobe lists Firefly Fill and Expand, Firefly Image 5 and Firefly Image 1, plus partner models such as FLUX.2 pro and Gemini with Nano Banana. Type what should appear in the selection.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Generate and choose","text":"Click Generate, then pick the variation you like in the Properties panel.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To remove something, select it and leave the prompt blank. Photoshop then fills the selection from the surrounding pixels instead of adding a new object.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Adobe Firefly free plan, prices and credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Adobe's plans page describes the free plan as limited free daily generations for images and video, with limited access to top models from Adobe, Google, OpenAI and others. Adobe does not publish a fixed number for it.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe: Firefly plans","url":"https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/plans.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Firefly Standard costs $9.99 a month for 2,000 credits, which Adobe says is up to 400 images or 20 five-second videos. Firefly Pro is $19.99 a month for 4,000 credits, and Pro Plus is $49.99 a month for 10,000 credits, both with lower prices for the first six months at the time of writing.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe: Firefly plans","url":"https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/plans.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Credits are spent per generation. Adobe's FAQ lists Firefly Image 5 at 10 credits and Image 4 Ultra at 20. Video costs far more: Generate Video uses 100 credits per second at 1080p, 50 at 720p and 20 at 540p. Partner models count as premium, and their price depends on the model.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/using/generative-credits-faq.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Standard features, such as Generative Fill with Firefly models, are unlimited and do not use credits on the Firefly Standard, Pro, Pro Plus and Premium plans and on Creative Cloud Pro, according to the FAQ. Creative Cloud Standard includes only 25 credits a month. Credits do not roll over, and failed generations are usually refunded within minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/using/generative-credits-faq.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Firefly is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The credit system is the main trap. Premium models and video burn through a monthly allowance quickly, and unused credits vanish at the reset. Before a big project, check the model's cost and your balance in the Account Menu. Partner models also come and go: Adobe keeps a list of deprecated partner models, so a model you rely on today may be gone later.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Firefly makes the most sense if you already work in Photoshop, because Generative Fill fixes real photos in place. For one-off pictures with no editing after, the free daily generations are a fair way to test it before paying.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Google AI Studio for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google says AI Studio stays free of charge unless you link a paid API key. Free use covers certain models with rate limits. Some models are marked Paid. Sources: Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart, Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio, Google AI for Developers: Billing, Google Blog: Google AI Studio at I/O 2026, NYU IT: Google AI Studio, Google AI Developers Forum: Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio.

Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio
Google Blog: Google AI Studio at I/O 2026
Google AI Developers Forum: Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Google AI Studio for free: prompts, settings and Build mode","dek":"Google's browser playground for Gemini costs nothing until you link a paid API key. Here is how to test prompts, set system instructions and build a first app.","summary":"Google AI Studio is a free web tool for trying Gemini models, writing system instructions and turning a working prompt into code. Its Build mode can also create and deploy a small web or Android app from a description.","seo_title":"How to use Google AI Studio for free: a step-by-step guide","seo_description":"How to use Google AI Studio for free: test Gemini prompts, set system instructions, get code and build an app in Build mode, step by step.","answer_summary":"Open aistudio.google.com, start a chat prompt in the Playground, set System Instructions under Run settings and click Run. AI Studio is free unless you link a paid API key, and Build mode at aistudio.google.com/apps turns a description into an app.","tags":["Google AI Studio","Gemini","Gemini API","Guides","Vibe coding"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Google AI Studio, in short: open aistudio.google.com, type a prompt in the Playground, change how the model behaves under Run settings, and click Get code when the result is right. Google describes AI Studio as the place to try its models and experiment with prompts before building with the Gemini API.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/ai-studio-quickstart"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not the Gemini app. The Gemini app is a chat assistant. AI Studio is a workbench: you pick the model, write the rules it follows, upload files, adjust settings such as temperature and copy the exact setup into your own code. NYU's IT department, which offers it to staff and students, calls it a web environment for rapid prototyping with Gemini models.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/ai-studio-quickstart"},{"name":"NYU IT: Google AI Studio","url":"https://www.nyu.edu/life/information-technology/artificial-intelligence-at-nyu/generative-ai-services/ai-studio.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Google AI Studio free tier and paid models","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For most people it is free. Google's billing documentation says AI Studio usage remains free of charge unless you link a paid API key for paid features. New accounts start on the Free Tier, which gives access to certain models, each with its own rate limits. Which models are included depends on the model, and Google keeps that list on its pricing page.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Billing","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some models are paid only. In Google's developer forum, users point out that Gemini 4 Argon carries a Paid label in AI Studio and needs either a Google AI subscription or an API key from a project with billing turned on. If you see that label, pick another model to stay free.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI Developers Forum: Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio","url":"https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/inquiry-about-gemini-4-argon-in-ai-studio-is-the-web-ui-free-to-use-and-why-is-setting-up-api-billing-required/197458"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Do not paste anything private while you are on the free tier. Google's billing page says paid use is how you make sure prompts and responses are not used to improve Google products, and NYU's guide says the same about the paid tier. Treat free use as public test data.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Google AI Studio: your first prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the Playground","text":"Go to aistudio.google.com. The Playground opens with a new chat prompt by default.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Run settings","text":"Click Run settings, the tune icon at the top right. This panel holds the model parameters, the safety settings and tools such as structured output, function calling, code execution and grounding.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write a system instruction","text":"Find the System Instructions field and describe the role and rules you want. Google's own example turns the model into an alien living on Europa. Something practical works better for daily use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A tutor that keeps it short","text":"You are a patient tutor. Answer in under 3 short paragraphs, use plain words and end with one question that checks I understood.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Ask and run","text":"Type your message in the box at the bottom and click Run. You can change the system instruction in the middle of a chat and run the same question again to compare answers. Google's quickstart uses exactly this to refine a bot's tone and length.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Every message in the chat is sent with the next one, so long conversations grow and can hit the model's token limit. Start a new prompt when you change topic.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Click Get code","text":"When the answers look right, click Get code. AI Studio gives you the same prompt, model and settings as code in your preferred language for the Gemini API. You can also save the prompt and share it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build an app in Google AI Studio","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Build mode is where AI Studio becomes a vibe coding tool. You describe an app in plain words and an agent writes it. Web apps get a React front end and a Node.js server by default, and the docs say AI Studio can also build native Android apps in Kotlin.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/aistudio-build-mode"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Build mode","text":"Go to aistudio.google.com/apps. Type a description in the prompt box. You can add AI Chips, for example for image generation or Google Maps data, or click I'm Feeling Lucky to have Gemini suggest an idea.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A small app to start with","text":"Build a simple web app where I paste a recipe and it turns it into a shopping list grouped by store section. Keep the design clean and make it work on a phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Watch the preview","text":"After you run the prompt, the generated files appear with a live preview on the right. The Code tab shows the code itself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Fix it one change at a time","text":"Ask for changes in the chat panel, or use annotation mode: highlight part of the screen and describe what should change. You can also edit the code directly in the Code tab.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Keep or deploy it","text":"Download the project as a ZIP, sync it to GitHub, or deploy it to Cloud Run. Apps are private until you share them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Deploying does not have to cost money at first. Google said at I/O 2026 that new builders can deploy their first two apps to Google Cloud at no cost and without a credit card. After that, Cloud Run pricing may apply, and when other people use a shared app its API calls count toward your limits.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/aistudio-build-mode"},{"name":"Google Blog: Google AI Studio at I/O 2026","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/google-ai-studio-io-2026/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Google AI Studio is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"AI Studio is built for testing, not for daily chatting. The free tier rate limits are tight once several people use one app, and NYU's guide says caching and batching are paid features. Build mode also has gaps the docs admit: there is no built-in storage yet and no real-time editing with teammates, so a shared GitHub repository is the workaround.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If a shared app shows a 403 Access Restricted error, Google's docs suggest turning off privacy extensions such as Privacy Badger, or asking the agent to fix the build and sharing again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"When to pay","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"To move a project to the paid tier, open the API keys or Projects page in AI Studio and click Set up billing. Depending on your account you may be asked to prepay at least $5. Tiers then go up automatically once you meet the spending criteria, with Tier 1 capped at $250.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Billing","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For learning, testing prompts and building a first app, the free tier is enough. Pay when you need a paid-only model, higher limits for real users or the promise that your prompts stay out of Google's product training.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: SpaceX planned a $50 billion AI campus in the Arizona desert under a different company name
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Cochise County application named Tombstone Resources LLC, not SpaceX. The company's role came out at a town hall on November 4. A SpaceX representative said its name on a filing draws attention, local station KVOA reported. The plan: nine buildings on 747 acres, built in four phases up to 6 GW. That is more than three times all the compute SpaceX had at the end of September. The Arizona Republic says it would use 2.5 times the power of every data center in Maricopa County. Sources: Reuters (via The Star), Teslarati, Interesting Engineering, AI Weekly.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Rendering of the proposed SpaceX supercomputing campus in Cochise County, Arizona.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"SpaceX plans a $50 billion AI supercomputing campus in Cochise County, Arizona","dek":"The application was filed under the name Tombstone Resources LLC, and together with a Starbase project the plan tops $74 billion.","summary":"SpaceX said on November 12, 2026, that it plans to invest more than $74 billion in two AI supercomputing campuses, including roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona. The Arizona project, first filed under the name Tombstone Resources LLC, still needs county approval and faces a petition with about 2,400 signatures.","seo_title":"SpaceX plans $50 billion AI campus in Cochise County, Arizona","seo_description":"SpaceX plans a 6 GW AI supercomputing campus in Arizona, filed as Tombstone Resources LLC, plus $24 billion at Starbase. Jobs, power, water and the votes.","answer_summary":"SpaceX wants to build a roughly $50 billion, 6 gigawatt AI supercomputing campus on 747 acres in Cochise County, Arizona. The project needs county approval, with a planning hearing set for December 9, 2026.","tags":["SpaceX","Elon Musk","AI data centers","Arizona","Starbase","xAI"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"SpaceX said on November 12, 2026, that it plans to invest more than $74 billion in two supercomputing campuses for artificial intelligence, according to Reuters. Roughly $50 billion would go to a campus in Cochise County, Arizona, and more than $24 billion to a facility at the company's Starbase site in Texas.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Star)","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/13/spacex-to-invest-over-74-billion-in-supercompute-facilities-in-texas-arizona"},{"name":"Interesting Engineering","url":"https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/spacex-arizona-supercomputing-campus-dry-cooling"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Reuters reported that SpaceX described the plan as an expansion of its AI computing ambitions alongside its rocket and satellite businesses. The company's AI segment, which went public in June, produced more than half of SpaceX's revenue in the third quarter.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Star)","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/13/spacex-to-invest-over-74-billion-in-supercompute-facilities-in-texas-arizona"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"An application under another name","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Arizona application was filed on October 30 under the name Tombstone Resources LLC rather than SpaceX, according to AI Weekly and Teslarati. SpaceX's involvement became public at a town hall at Cochise Elementary School on November 4. Teslarati, citing local station KVOA, reported that a SpaceX representative told residents the other name was used because putting SpaceX on the filing draws attention from outside the county.","sources":[{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"},{"name":"AI Weekly","url":"https://aiweekly.co/alerts/spacex-commits-74b-to-ai-campuses-in-arizona-and-texas"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The site covers 747 acres near the Willcox Playa, about 80 miles east of Tucson. The application describes up to nine buildings of about 493,000 square feet each, built in four phases of roughly 1.5 gigawatts, for 6 gigawatts of computing capacity at full build. Teslarati reported that the plan includes a 24 gigawatt hour battery system and about $3.6 billion in grid upgrades.","sources":[{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"},{"name":"Interesting Engineering","url":"https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/spacex-arizona-supercomputing-campus-dry-cooling"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The scale is large even by SpaceX's own standards. The company ended the third quarter with 1.7 gigawatts of nameplate compute, so the Arizona campus alone would be more than three times that, Teslarati noted. An Arizona Republic analysis cited by the outlet found that the finished campus would draw about 2.5 times more power than all data centers in Maricopa County combined.","sources":[{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Jobs, power bills and water","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SpaceX projects about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs in Arizona. The company said it is working with local electric cooperatives and that the project could lower bills for cooperative members by up to 20 percent. The site sits next to the Apache Generating Station, a coal and natural gas plant of about 1 gigawatt that had been slated to retire by 2028, and SpaceX told residents its investment could expand the station to more than 6 gigawatts.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Star)","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/13/spacex-to-invest-over-74-billion-in-supercompute-facilities-in-texas-arizona"},{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"},{"name":"Interesting Engineering","url":"https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/spacex-arizona-supercomputing-campus-dry-cooling"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Water is a central issue in the arid county. SpaceX said the campus would use dry cooling, which relies on air instead of water intensive systems, with no planned industrial groundwater use. The application estimates ongoing water use of 7 to 10 acre feet per year, which Teslarati compared to the consumption of 20 to 30 homes.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Star)","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/13/spacex-to-invest-over-74-billion-in-supercompute-facilities-in-texas-arizona"},{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"},{"name":"Interesting Engineering","url":"https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/spacex-arizona-supercomputing-campus-dry-cooling"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The project still needs county approval. A petition asking officials to deny the permit has about 2,400 signatures. Written comments are due November 27, and the Cochise County Planning and Zoning Commission has a public hearing scheduled for December 9 in Bisbee. Teslarati reported that construction could begin in March 2027 if the campus is approved, and that the nearby playa is a landing area for federally protected sandhill cranes.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Star)","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/13/spacex-to-invest-over-74-billion-in-supercompute-facilities-in-texas-arizona"},{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"},{"name":"AI Weekly","url":"https://aiweekly.co/alerts/spacex-commits-74b-to-ai-campuses-in-arizona-and-texas"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The Texas half of the plan","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"At Starbase, SpaceX plans to generate its own electricity rather than draw from the public grid. A city notice described a gas fired power plant and supercomputing facility on about 444 acres. SpaceX said the project has generated more than 3,000 construction jobs and will support more than 500 permanent jobs. The Starbase City Commission is due to consider a property tax abatement for the project on December 9, the same day as the Arizona hearing.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters (via The Star)","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/13/spacex-to-invest-over-74-billion-in-supercompute-facilities-in-texas-arizona"},{"name":"Teslarati","url":"https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-arizona-supercomputer-tombstone/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For NeuraFeed, the Arizona filing shows how the race for AI computing power is moving into rural counties, where a single campus can outweigh the existing grid. The promises of jobs and lower power bills are SpaceX's own projections, and local officials will weigh them against concerns about energy, water and wildlife.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch the December 9 votes in Bisbee and Starbase, which will decide whether either campus can move toward construction.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Wispr Flow to type with your voice
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The free plan covers 2,000 words a week on Mac and Windows. After that it slows down until Sunday. Pro is $15 a month or $144 a year for unlimited dictation. Click where you want the text, hold Fn on a Mac (Ctrl and Win on Windows), speak, then let go. Double-tap the shortcut to dictate hands-free. Sources: Wispr Flow Help Center: What is Wispr Flow?, Wispr Flow Help Center: Setup guide, Wispr Flow Help Center: Plans, Wispr Flow Help Center: Dictionary, Wispr Flow Help Center: Command Mode, Spokenly: Wispr Flow review, TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE.
