nf:hero.nf:alt: How to use Wispr Flow to type with your voice

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Wispr Flow on Mac and Windows: voice typing with AI, step by step","dek":"Wispr Flow turns speech into clean text in any app. Here is how to set it up, the shortcuts that matter, what the free plan covers and where it falls short.","summary":"Wispr Flow is an AI dictation app that types what you say into any text field on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, removing filler words and adding punctuation. The free plan gives 2,000 words a week on desktop; Pro costs $15 a month or $144 a year.","seo_title":"How to use Wispr Flow on Mac and Windows (free plan explained)","seo_description":"How to use Wispr Flow: setup, the Fn and Ctrl+Win shortcuts, hands-free mode, Dictionary, Command Mode, and what the free 2,000 words a week get you.","answer_summary":"Install Wispr Flow, sign in, allow the microphone (and Accessibility on Mac), then click into any text box, hold Fn on a Mac or your chosen shortcut on Windows, speak and release. The text appears where your cursor is.","tags":["Wispr Flow","Voice typing","Dictation","AI tools","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Wispr Flow, in short: put your cursor where you want text, hold one shortcut key, talk, and let go. Flow turns what you said into cleaned up text and drops it into whatever app you are in, according to Wispr's help center. It removes filler words, adds punctuation and handles it when you correct yourself mid-sentence. It runs on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, and it needs an internet connection because transcription happens in the cloud.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: What is Wispr Flow?","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2772472373-what-is-flow"},{"name":"Spokenly: Wispr Flow review","url":"https://spokenly.app/blog/wispr-flow-review"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not a niche tool anymore. Wispr AI raised $280 million in August 2026 at a $2 billion valuation, and the company says users have written more than 60 billion words with Flow, according to SiliconANGLE. This guide covers setup, the shortcuts worth learning, the free plan and the honest downsides.","sources":[{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/17/wispr-raises-280m-to-power-up-natural-speech-to-text-using-ai/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Wispr Flow free plan and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan gives you 2,000 words a week on Mac and Windows, with a hard cap of 5,000. Past 2,000, Flow slows down; at the cap, dictation stops until the weekly reset at midnight Pacific time on Sunday. iPhone and Android share a separate weekly allowance, according to Wispr's plans page.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Plans","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/9559327591"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pro costs $15 a month or $144 a year, which works out to about $12 a month, and removes the word limit. A default trial lasts 14 days, and students with a recognized .edu address can get longer trials. Team plans start at $23 per user per month. Prices outside the US are set in local currency, so they may differ.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Plans","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/9559327591"},{"name":"Spokenly: Wispr Flow review","url":"https://spokenly.app/blog/wispr-flow-review"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Two thousand words is roughly a handful of long emails. Use the free week to test whether you actually dictate every day before you pay for unlimited.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to set up Wispr Flow on Mac and Windows","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download and open Flow","text":"Get the app from wisprflow.ai/download. On a Mac, move it to Applications and open it; a menu bar icon shows it is running. On Windows, run the installer and open Flow from the Start menu; it lives in the system tray.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Sign in","text":"Click Sign in via browser and use Google, Apple, Microsoft, SSO or email. If your company uses SSO, check with IT first instead of making a separate account.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Allow the microphone","text":"Flow asks for microphone access on both systems, plus Accessibility on a Mac so it can type into other apps. If you clicked deny, turn it on under System Settings, Privacy and Security on a Mac, or Settings, Privacy and Security, Microphone on Windows. Use Test your microphone to check that it hears you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Pick your shortcut and languages","text":"On a Mac with an fn key, the default is fn. On a Mac without one, it is Ctrl and Option. On Windows the help center lists Ctrl and Win as the default, and you can change it with Edit shortcut. Pick your languages or leave automatic detection on; Flow supports more than 100 languages and you can mix them in one sentence.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Do your first dictation","text":"Click into any text box, an email, a chat, a doc. Press and hold your shortcut, speak normally, then release. On desktop the text appears after you let go, not word by word as you talk.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Go hands-free for long text","text":"Double-tap your shortcut to start hands-free dictation, so you do not have to hold the key for a long message.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Make Wispr Flow spell your words right","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Dictionary is where you teach Flow names, product terms and jargon. On Mac or Windows, open Dictionary in the left sidebar, click Add new, type the word and click Add word. Then dictate a sentence with it to check. If Flow keeps writing the same wrong spelling, add a correction: turn on Correct a misspelling and enter the wrong version Flow produces.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Dictionary","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4052411709"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On desktop Flow can also learn words by itself when the auto-learn setting is on and you fix dictated text. It skips everyday words, numbers, web addresses and very famous names. You can import up to 1,000 entries from a file on Mac and Windows.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Dictionary","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4052411709"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Edit text by voice with Command Mode","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Command Mode lets you speak an instruction instead of text: edit what you wrote, draft a reply or run a web search. It is off by default; turn it on under Settings, Experimental. The default shortcut is Fn and Ctrl on a Mac and Ctrl, Win and Alt on Windows. The help center ties it to Pro, active trials and enterprise plans.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Command Mode","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4816967992-how-to-use-command-mode"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 1: Tighten a message","text":"Make this shorter and friendlier, and keep the dates.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 2: Fix the tone","text":"Rewrite this so it sounds professional, not annoyed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 3: Draft a reply","text":"Write a short reply that says yes to Thursday and asks for the agenda.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Hold the Command Mode shortcut, say the instruction with no wake word, and release. Press Esc to cancel. Asking it to build a website or an app only gives you drafted text, not a working app, the help center notes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Wispr Flow is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is no offline mode: everything goes through the cloud, so a bad connection means no dictation. A May 2026 review by Spokenly, which makes a rival app, also says the AI cleanup sometimes over-edits what you said, real-world delay is about one to two seconds, and data sharing for model training is on unless you opt out. Wispr's onboarding asks for your data preference, so read that screen instead of clicking through.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: What is Wispr Flow?","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2772472373-what-is-flow"},{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Setup guide","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/3152211871-setup-guide"},{"name":"Spokenly: Wispr Flow review","url":"https://spokenly.app/blog/wispr-flow-review"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Flow is worth it if you write a lot of email, chat and notes and talk faster than you type. If you mostly write code, numbers or work offline, the free week will show you quickly that it is not your tool.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen is here, and free users get it
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12 as the replacement for Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google says it finishes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Flash and calls it the daily driver of the Gemini 4 family. Hydrogen now powers Google Search for all users worldwide, at no cost. Google says it handles typos and multi-part questions better. In the Gemini app, free users get it automatically when a prompt fits. Google says Hydrogen makes more than 5 times fewer fabricated claims than Gemini 3.8 Flash. Sources: VentureBeat, MakeUseOf, Digital Trends, Chrome Unboxed.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Google's promotional artwork announcing the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen and puts it in Search for all users","dek":"The faster model replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash in Search and the Gemini app, with a higher API price for developers.","summary":"Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026, as the successor to Gemini 3.8 Flash and made it the model behind Google Search for all users. Google says it completes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Flash, and developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.","seo_title":"Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Flash successor, price and access","seo_description":"Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash. Who gets it in Search and the Gemini app, what it costs developers and what Google claims.","answer_summary":"Gemini 4 Hydrogen is free in Google Search for all users and reaches free Gemini app users automatically when a prompt fits; developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.","tags":["Google","Gemini","Gemini 4 Hydrogen","Google Search","AI models"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026, a faster model in the Gemini 4 family that takes over from Gemini 3.8 Flash. According to VentureBeat and Digital Trends, the model is rolling out at once across Google Search, the Gemini app, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and Google's business products.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Digital Trends reported that Google describes Hydrogen as its daily driver for agent work, built for speed and efficiency, while the heavier Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models handle long, deep reasoning. Hydrogen arrives a few weeks after those two models.","sources":[{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who gets it","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Hydrogen now powers Google Search for all users worldwide, according to Digital Trends and Chrome Unboxed, and MakeUseOf noted that it is free to use there. Google says the model understands multi-part questions, typos and very specific requests better, gives answers that are easier to scan and shows a wider range of links in results.","sources":[{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini app, Hydrogen appears in the model picker. Free users are routed to it automatically when the app judges that a prompt calls for it. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers also get it in Google Sheets, where Google says financial models are built more than 30 percent faster, and in the Antigravity coding tool.","sources":[{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Developers can use it in Google AI Studio, Android Studio and the Gemini API, and Google Cloud lists the model as generally available, according to VentureBeat. The context window is about 1 million tokens, and the model accepts text, images, audio and video as input.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Google claims","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Gemini 3.8 Flash. At its default high reasoning setting, it scored 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, VentureBeat reported, compared with 31 for Flash and one point above Gemini 4 Argon. At the new xhigh setting it reached 54.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Google's own comparison shows Hydrogen completing 57 percent of tasks, against 18.2 percent for Flash and 63.9 percent for Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5. Digital Trends reported that Google places Hydrogen ahead of OpenAI's GPT 6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on knowledge tests, but slightly behind in science, math and computer use.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google also made safety claims. According to Digital Trends and MakeUseOf, the company says Hydrogen makes more than five times fewer fabricated claims than Flash, reduces overreach in agent tasks by up to 81 percent and is up to twice as unlikely to get around permission limits when a task is blocked. These figures come from Google and have not been checked independently.","sources":[{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What developers pay","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The standard API price is $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, including reasoning tokens. VentureBeat reported that this matches the standard Flash pricing scheduled from January 1, 2027, and is twice the introductory Flash rate that runs through December 31, 2026. Batch and Flex requests cost half the standard rate.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Box, which tested the model early, reported that accuracy on its complex work evaluation rose from 74 percent with Flash to 79 percent with Hydrogen, VentureBeat said, with tasks taking less than half as long.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most people the change is invisible but large: the model answering their Google searches has been replaced without any action on their part. The higher developer price suggests Google is betting that speed and fewer errors matter more to businesses than the cheapest possible rate.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next thing to watch is whether independent testers confirm Google's claims about fewer fabricated answers, since Hydrogen now writes the AI answers in Google Search for all users.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Lovable to build an app without writing code
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The free plan gives 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. A color change costs about 0.50 credits. A landing page with images costs about 2. Type your idea in the prompt box with Build selected. The first version takes a few minutes. Chat sits on the left, a live preview on the right. Use the preview toolbar to pick one element and describe the change. It is cheaper than a new full prompt. Sources: Lovable Docs: Quick start, Lovable Docs: Plans and credits, Lovable Docs: Subscription plans, Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices, AppLaunchpad: Lovable review, TechCrunch.

nf:hero.nf:alt: How to use Lovable to build an app without writing code

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Lovable to build an app without coding, and what the free plan gets you","dek":"Lovable turns a written description into a working web app. Here is how credits work, the steps to a first published app, and prompts to copy.","summary":"Lovable is an AI app builder that writes a working web app from a plain description, and the free plan includes 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. This guide covers credits and plans, the steps from first prompt to a published app, Plan mode, and prompts that waste fewer credits.","seo_title":"How to use Lovable to build an app without coding (free plan)","seo_description":"How to use Lovable: free credits and plans, the steps from first prompt to a published app, Plan mode, and prompts to copy that save credits.","answer_summary":"Sign up at Lovable, type what you want in the prompt box with Build mode selected, check the preview, ask for one change at a time and click Publish. The free plan gives 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month.","tags":["Lovable","AI app builder","Vibe coding","No code","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Lovable, in short: describe the app you want in plain words, let it build a first version, fix it one change at a time and click Publish. Lovable is an AI app builder from Stockholm that grew out of GPT Engineer, an open source tool built by its CEO Anton Osika. Lovable says a first app takes about ten minutes and needs nothing installed.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Quick start","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/getting-started"},{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/10/lovable-says-its-nearing-8-million-users-as-the-year-old-ai-coding-startup-eyes-more-corporate-employees"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The catch is credits. Every build costs some, the free plan gets only a few a day, and an October 2026 review says vague prompts and repeated fixes burn through them quickly. This guide covers what you get for free, the steps to a first published app, and prompts that keep the cost down.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/plans-and-credits"},{"name":"AppLaunchpad: Lovable review","url":"https://theapplaunchpad.com/blog/lovable-review/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Lovable free plan, credits and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan includes 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. Once you hit 30, daily credits stop for the rest of the calendar month and come back on the 1st. Daily credits refresh at midnight UTC and do not roll over. Free users also get small monthly grants for Lovable Cloud, its backend, and for AI features inside the apps they build.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/plans-and-credits"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Subscription plans","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Build mode is priced by the work done. Lovable's own examples: a color change costs about 0.50 credits, removing a footer about 0.90, adding user login about 1.20 and a landing page with images about 2.00. Plan mode, where Lovable thinks with you before writing code, costs 1 credit per message. If you stop a build, you pay only for the work it finished.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/plans-and-credits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pro starts at $25 a month for 100 credits, plus the 5 daily build credits with no monthly cap. It adds code editing and download, custom domains, removal of the Edit with Lovable badge and rollover of unused monthly credits. Business starts at $50 a month and adds team features such as single sign-on and role-based access. Students and teachers can get 50 percent off Pro for up to 12 months.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Subscription plans","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On the free plan you cannot edit or download the code and cannot use your own domain, but Git sync with GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket is included. Publishing is free on every plan.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Subscription plans","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Quick start","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/getting-started"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Lovable: your first app, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create an account","text":"Sign up with email, Google, GitHub or Apple. You can also type your idea on the homepage first; Lovable keeps the prompt and asks you to sign up when you submit it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe your app in Build mode","text":"Type in the prompt box with Build selected in the mode picker. Any language works. Be concrete: what the app is, who it is for and which sections or screens it needs. You can also attach a sketch, a design or a screenshot as a visual reference, start from a template, or build from a link.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Watch the first version appear","text":"The first build takes a few minutes. The editor has the project chat on the left and a live preview on the right.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Change one thing at a time","text":"Ask for a single change, then check the preview before the next one. Every change is saved as a version you can restore, so a bad edit does not break the app for good.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Point at what you want changed","text":"For small fixes, use the preview toolbar to select an element and describe the change. For text, use Edit text inline and type straight onto the page. Lovable's own docs recommend this over writing a new prompt for small fixes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Test it on a phone screen","text":"Click every button and link, then use the device toggle to switch to Mobile view. Most people will open your link on a phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Publish","text":"Click Publish in the top right. Lovable suggests a lovable.app address that you can edit. The live site is a snapshot: later edits show up in the preview right away, but reach the live site only when you click Publish again and choose Publish changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Lovable prompts that save credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting guide suggests building in a fixed order: the foundation (the product, the audience and the one key action), then the design direction, then one component at a time with real text, and finally a clear limit on what each change may touch. It also suggests saving your design rules in the project instructions so they carry across prompts.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The foundation","text":"Build a one-page website for [product], made for [audience]. The one thing visitors should do is [key action, for example book a table]. Sections: [list of sections]. No login or database yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Plan before building (use Plan mode)","text":"I want to add [feature] to this app. [Describe how it should work in two or three sentences.] Ask me any questions you need in order to fully understand what I want from this feature and how I envision it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A scoped change","text":"Only change the [page or section name]. [Describe the change.] Keep the existing styling and leave the rest of the app unchanged.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A clear design direction","text":"Use a [calm, bold or premium] design: [colors], [type of fonts], rounded corners and generous spacing. Apply it to the whole site without changing any text or layout.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use real headlines and button text instead of placeholder text. The docs say placeholder copy hides layout problems that real words reveal. Specific words work better than vague ones: \"bold, saturated colors\" beats \"colorful\", and \"replace\" or \"adjust\" beats \"make this better\".","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Lovable is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An AppLaunchpad review published on October 20, 2026 called Lovable one of the strongest tools for turning an idea into a working first version quickly. It also named credit burn as a major weakness, said some users need several prompts to fix a single bug, and said bigger, more complex projects still need manual fixing. Its advice: for a real production app, knowledge of React and backend code becomes much more valuable.","sources":[{"name":"AppLaunchpad: Lovable review","url":"https://theapplaunchpad.com/blog/lovable-review/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"That matches how the credit system works. Each round of fixes costs credits, so a loop of failed fixes is expensive on any plan. If a fix does not work after one or two tries, describe the problem more precisely, or restore an earlier version, instead of repeating the same request.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Lovable's docs suggest bookmarking milestones in version history and previewing the current version before a risky redesign, so you know which version to return to.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"When to pay for Lovable","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The free plan is enough to test an idea, build a simple landing page or a small internal tool and publish it on a lovable.app address. Pay for Pro when you need your own domain, want to edit or download the code, or keep running out of daily credits halfway through a project. Teams that need sign-in controls and shared workspaces are who Business is for.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google just opened preorders for its Gemini glasses. They start at $395 and ship December 10
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Warby Parker's three frames start at $395. Gentle Monster's six frames start at $449. Samsung builds the hardware. Preorders opened on November 12. Stores and shipping start December 10, in the US and South Korea. Ask Gemini about what you are looking at, get Google Maps directions or live translation in over 70 languages. There is no screen. A 12MP camera and open-ear speakers do the work. A light shows when the camera records. If it is covered, recording stops. Sources: 9to5Google, Unite.AI, Android Headlines.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A pair of Warby Parker smart glasses made with Google, shown in a lifestyle product photo.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Google opens preorders for Gemini smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, starting at $395","dek":"The display-free glasses, built by Samsung, have a camera, open-ear speakers and a Hey Gemini wake word, and reach stores on December 10.","summary":"Google opened preorders on November 12, 2026 for its first Gemini-powered Intelligent Eyewear, designed with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster and engineered by Samsung. Prices start at $395, and shipping and in-store sales begin December 10 in the US and South Korea.","seo_title":"Google Gemini glasses: price, release date and features","seo_description":"Google's Gemini smart glasses with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster start at $395 and ship December 10. Prices, features, privacy rules and compatible phones.","answer_summary":"Google's Gemini glasses start at $395 for Warby Parker frames and $449 for Gentle Monster frames. Preorders opened November 12, 2026, and they ship and reach stores on December 10.","tags":["Google","Gemini","Smart glasses","Samsung","Warby Parker","Gentle Monster"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Google opened preorders on November 12, 2026 for its Gemini-powered Intelligent Eyewear, a line of smart glasses designed with the eyewear brands Warby Parker and Gentle Monster and engineered by Samsung, according to 9to5Google and Unite.AI. Shipping and in-store availability begin on December 10.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Warby Parker's frames start at $395 and Gentle Monster's at $449, with Android Headlines putting the top Gentle Monster models at $489. Android Headlines counted 30 designs in total: 14 Warby Parker variations across three frames and 16 Gentle Monster variations across six frames.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The frames and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Warby Parker's three styles are called Alden, Reid and Wren, offered in optical and sun versions in Pine, Saddle and Jet Black, 9to5Google reported. Gentle Monster's six frames come in colors that include dark red, pink, gray and yellow, with clear, tinted, blue or brown lenses, and prescriptions are available for most designs. Unite.AI reported that more than 360 Warby Parker stores will offer guided demos, along with selected partner and Google Store locations.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The glasses have no display. They rely on a 12 megapixel ultra-wide camera that records video at up to 3K, four microphones and two open-ear speakers, running on a Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chip, according to 9to5Google. The frames weigh 40 to 44 grams, the battery is rated at nine hours, and the charging case holds seven full charges.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Gemini does on the glasses","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Wearers can wake the assistant with a new Hey Gemini phrase, a tap on the frame or, with a Pixel Watch, a hand gesture. Google lists questions about objects in view, turn-by-turn directions from Google Maps and real-time speech translation through Google Translate in more than 70 languages. The speakers also work as headphones for music, calls and spoken message summaries.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Unite.AI reported that Google's accessibility feature Guided Vision, which gives spoken descriptions of surroundings to blind and low-vision users, will also run on the glasses with a compatible Android phone. Google says the feature can make mistakes and is not a mobility aid.","sources":[{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Privacy rules","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An outward-facing light turns on when the camera captures a photo or video, and recording stops if the light is covered or disabled, 9to5Google reported. Google says faces of bystanders are automatically redacted before Gemini processes what the camera sees, and that those camera visuals are not saved to Gemini History or used for AI training or ad targeting. A physical switch turns off the camera, microphones and Gemini.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google Play rules bar apps on the glasses from using the camera for real-time facial identification, according to Unite.AI. Android Headlines reported that buyers must be 18 or older and pass age verification to activate the glasses.","sources":[{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The glasses work with Pixel 7 phones and newer, Galaxy S, Z Fold and Z Flip models on One UI 9.0 or later, and iPhone 13 Pro and newer, according to 9to5Google and Android Headlines.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The launch puts Google in direct competition with Meta's Ray-Ban glasses in the same form: a camera, speakers and an assistant inside frames that look like ordinary eyewear. Supporting iPhones from day one and leading with privacy controls suggests Google wants to reach buyers beyond its own phone users and answer the camera concerns that followed earlier smart glasses.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The first reviews after the December 10 release should show whether the nine hour battery claim and the bystander face redaction hold up in daily use.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Google Flow to make AI videos, and what 50 free credits really buy
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Every account gets 50 Flow credits a day. Unused ones do not roll over. Free users may not get video between about 2 PM and 5 PM UTC. Omni Flash 1.2 costs 3 credits a second at 720p, so 10 seconds is 30 credits. Sources: Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow, Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features, Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits, Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes, Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow, Google: New creative controls in Google Flow, Fello AI: Google Flow credits, prices and limits.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Google Flow: make AI videos step by step, and what 50 free credits get you","dek":"Google's AI filmmaking tool gives everyone 50 credits a day. Here is how to spend them, the steps to a first clip, and four prompts to copy.","summary":"Google Flow turns prompts, frames and reference images into short AI video clips, and every account gets 50 free credits a day. This guide covers credit costs, plans, the steps to a first video, frames, ingredients, the Flow Agent and Scenebuilder.","seo_title":"How to use Google Flow: AI video step by step (free credits)","seo_description":"How to use Google Flow: the 50 free daily credits, what each clip costs, steps to your first video, frames, ingredients, and four prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Open Google Flow in Chrome or Edge, start a project, click the model name, choose Video, set the length and model, write a detailed prompt and click Generate. Everyone gets 50 credits a day; Omni Flash 1.2 costs 3 credits per second at 720p.","tags":["Google Flow","Gemini Omni","Veo","AI video","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Google Flow, in short: open it in Chrome or Edge, type a detailed prompt, pick a video model and length, and click Generate. Flow is Google's AI filmmaking tool for making clips, scenes and short stories with consistent characters, and every account gets 50 free credits a day.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The catch: free credits buy only a few seconds of video at full quality, video generation can be unavailable to free users at peak hours, and the best editing features need a paid Google AI plan. This guide covers what you get for free, what each clip costs, the steps to a first video, and prompts to copy.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need to use Google Flow","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You must be 18 or older, verify your age, and live in a supported region. Google says a VPN does not unlock Flow in an unsupported country, and Flow is not offered everywhere Google AI Pro is sold, so check the region list before you pay for a plan. Google recommends a computer for the strongest editing tools, and there is also a mobile app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Fello AI reported on November 10, 2026 that the Android app is in beta and the iPhone app is listed as coming soon. It also reports that Flow now lives at flow.google.com and that the old Google Labs address redirects there.","sources":[{"name":"Fello AI: Google Flow credits, prices and limits","url":"https://felloai.com/google-flow/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Google Flow free credits and plans","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Everyone gets 50 Flow credits per day, with or without a subscription. The daily credits refresh after your first generation of the day, and unused ones do not roll over. Without a subscription you may not be able to generate video between roughly 2 PM and 5 PM UTC, though images and the Flow Agent still work.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid Google AI plans add monthly credits on top of the daily 50: 200 with Google AI Plus, 1,000 with Pro, 10,000 with the $100 Ultra plan and 25,000 with the $200 Ultra plan. Monthly credits reset at the start of the billing cycle and do not roll over either. Fello AI lists the US prices as $4.99 for Plus, $19.99 for Pro and $99.99 and $199.99 for the two Ultra tiers.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Fello AI: Google Flow credits, prices and limits","url":"https://felloai.com/google-flow/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Credits are taken when a generation starts. If a generation fails or is blocked by a safety filter, Google says the credits come back within one hour.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What a Google Flow video costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Omni Flash 1.2, the main video model, costs 1 credit per second at 360p and 3 credits per second at 720p for clips up to 10 seconds. So a 10 second 720p clip uses 30 of your 50 daily credits. Free users can make clips of 3 to 10 seconds; Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers can go up to 15 seconds, at double the rate for seconds 11 to 15.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Veo 3.1 Lite makes 720p clips of 4, 6 or 8 seconds for 10 credits each, or 5 for Ultra subscribers. Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Quality and Omni Flash 1.1 will be retired on December 5, 2026, and Google recommends Omni Flash 1.2 or Veo 3.1 Lite for new projects. Image generation runs on Nano Banana models.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Draft at 360p, which costs a third of 720p, and only make the 720p version of the shot you like. Fello AI gives the same advice, and Google's own August update pitched 360p as the cheap way to test ideas.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first video in Google Flow","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Flow and start a project","text":"Go to Google Flow in a Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge, sign in, and open an existing project or start a new one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Video","text":"Click the model name in the prompt box (it starts on the image model Nano Banana Pro), then click Video.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Set the options","text":"Choose the aspect ratio, the number of outputs, the model and the length. Video is billed per second, so shorter clips cost less.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Write the prompt and generate","text":"Be specific about the subject, the action, the place, the lighting and the style, then click Generate.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A first clip","text":"[Subject] [doing an action] in [place], [time of day] light, [style, for example handheld documentary or warm film look]. The camera [moves slowly toward the subject / stays still].","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Frames, ingredients and the Flow Agent","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Frames to video lets you set a start frame, an end frame or both. Click the model name, then Video, then Frames, drag in your images, and describe the action between them. This mode works only on the web version of Flow.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353334?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Connect a start and end frame","text":"The camera moves from the first image to the second in one smooth shot. [Describe what happens in between, for example: the door opens and the dog runs out into the snow.]","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ingredients are reference images or videos for a character, a product or a place. Click the model name, then Video, then Ingredients, and add references by dragging them in, typing @ to search your project, or clicking Add. Then say how each one should appear. Google suggests plain backgrounds for subject and product references and a prompt that matches the references.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353334?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Use your ingredients","text":"The [character from @ingredient] walks into [place] holding [product from @ingredient]. Keep the face and clothes exactly as in the reference. [Lighting and mood].","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Flow Agent is a switch in the prompt box. Turn on Agent, describe the scene, and you can ask for several versions at once; Google's own example is a request for 5 variations of a video with different lighting. You can also drag a finished clip into the prompt box with Agent on and describe a change, and the edit is saved to that clip's stack.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353334?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Ask the Agent for options","text":"Give me 4 variations of this video with different lighting: early morning, noon, sunset and night. Keep the subject and camera move the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Extend clips and build a scene","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Extending a clip needs a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra plan and Omni Flash 1.2. Click the clip, click Extend, pick the extra length, describe how the action continues and click Generate. You can add up to 3 reference images. Veo Extend was retired on November 5, 2026.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Scenebuilder puts several clips in order. Hover over a clip, click More, then Add to Scene. From there you can drag clips into order, trim the start and end of each one, preview the sequence and download the scene. To keep a single frame, pause the video, hover over it and click Save frame, then use it as an ingredient or a start or end frame.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Subscribers can upscale Omni 360p videos to 1080p, and Ultra subscribers to 4K. Every Flow output carries an invisible SynthID watermark, and a visible watermark can be switched on in the profile menu.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Google Flow falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The free plan is fine for learning the tool, not for a project. Fifty credits are less than two 10 second clips at 720p, they reset daily rather than piling up, and the peak hour block lands in the US morning. Region limits are strict, and features such as frames to video and extending are web only or paid only. If you want to test Flow seriously, Google AI Plus is the cheapest way to get longer clips, extending and free 1080p upscaling.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before a bigger project, check your balance: click your profile picture at the top right in Flow. Google notes that limits and credit costs can change, and the current cost shows in the prompt box settings.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Anthropic is saving up to 20% of its IPO for regular investors, at $70 to $78 a share
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at an expected $70 to $78 each. At the top of the range that is up to $64.35 billion. An updated filing on November 10 says up to 20% could go to retail investors. Fidelity, Robinhood, Charles Schwab, SoFi and ETRADE are taking requests from eligible customers, CoinCentral reports. A request is not a guarantee. If demand is higher than supply, many will get fewer shares or none. Sources: Yahoo Finance, CoinCentral, Anthropic on X, MarsBit via KuCoin.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Portrait photo of a smiling man.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Anthropic reserves up to 20% of its IPO for retail investors","dek":"The Claude maker expects to price its shares at $70 to $78, with trading on Nasdaq possible as early as November 19.","summary":"Anthropic said in an updated filing that up to 20% of its initial public offering could go to retail investors. The company plans to sell 825 million shares at an expected $70 to $78 each.","seo_title":"Anthropic IPO: up to 20% for retail investors, $70 to $78","seo_description":"Anthropic may give retail investors up to 20% of its IPO at $70 to $78 a share. Brokers, key dates and what happened after SpaceX did the same.","answer_summary":"Anthropic says up to 20% of its IPO shares could be allocated to retail investors, at an expected price of $70 to $78 a share. Trading under the ticker ANT could begin on Nasdaq as early as November 19, 2026.","tags":["Anthropic","IPO","Claude","Nasdaq","Retail investors"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, said in an updated regulatory filing on November 10, 2026, that up to 20% of the shares in its initial public offering could be allocated to retail investors, according to Yahoo Finance. The company plans to offer 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an expected price of $70 to $78 per share. At the top of that range the offering would be worth up to $64.35 billion.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic also shared a link to a dedicated IPO website, ipo.anthropic.com, in a post on X, along with a notice that it has filed a registration statement and prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission and that investors should read the prospectus before investing.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic on X","url":"https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2120841731302154708"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How retail investors can request shares","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Eligible customers of Fidelity, Robinhood, Charles Schwab, SoFi and ETRADE can request shares through those brokers, CoinCentral reported on November 12, 2026. Fidelity customers must submit an indication of interest before an expected deadline of November 17. A request does not guarantee an allocation if demand is higher than the number of shares available, and access varies by country, the outlet said.","sources":[{"name":"CoinCentral","url":"https://coincentral.com/how-to-invest-in-the-anthropic-ipo-share-price-date-and-risks-explained"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outside the United States, a report by MarsBit republished by KuCoin said the IPO website has regional paths for the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, and named Interactive Brokers, Revolut and SBI as participating institutions. That report cites unnamed filings and has not been confirmed by Anthropic.","sources":[{"name":"MarsBit via KuCoin","url":"https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/anthropic-ipo-website-launched-retail-investors-in-multiple-countries-can-apply"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Key dates and numbers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pricing is expected on November 18, and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT could begin as early as November 19, according to CoinCentral, which noted that the dates can change and that the opening price could land above or below the expected range. Yahoo Finance estimated the retail portion at about $12.2 billion at the $74 midpoint.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"},{"name":"CoinCentral","url":"https://coincentral.com/how-to-invest-in-the-anthropic-ipo-share-price-date-and-risks-explained"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The filing shows third quarter revenue of $17 billion, more than 12 times the figure a year earlier, and more than 11,900 customers that spend at least $100,000 a year, Yahoo Finance reported. It also lists about $900.9 billion in committed spending, most of it for computing infrastructure, with about $451.6 billion expected before the end of 2030.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What happened in earlier offerings","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Retail investors received about 20% of SpaceX's offering as well, Yahoo Finance said, citing The Wall Street Journal. That stock priced at $135, opened at $150 and passed $200 by its third day, and was later trading below $150. Facebook opened at $38 on May 17, 2012, and was under $18 by early September of that year.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In NeuraFeed's reading, a large retail allocation does two things at once. It lets the people who use Claude every day own a piece of the company on the same terms as institutions, and it moves part of the first-day price risk onto buyers who have the least information. The SpaceX and Facebook examples show that a strong opening and a lower price a few weeks later can both happen to the same stock. The size of Anthropic's spending commitments, more than fifty times its latest quarterly revenue, is the number in the filing that deserves the most attention from anyone weighing a request.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch the final price set on November 18 and how many shares retail investors actually receive, since both will show how much demand exists outside the large funds before trading begins.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Russian pranksters fooled OpenAI's national security team with a fake Ukrainian official on a 17-minute call
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Russian prank duo Vovan and Lexus posed as Rustem Umerov, a top Ukrainian security official, on a 17-minute video call with OpenAI. The fake Umerov kept his camera off. The duo later posted the recording online. Three senior OpenAI staff joined, including Sasha Baker, its head of national security policy. They discussed helping Ukraine's military, even offensive uses. One of them said many senior people at OpenAI were reluctant about offensive uses. Sources: The Intercept, Business Today, Digit.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A speaker on stage at a Semafor conference in New York.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Russian pranksters posed as a Ukrainian official on a call with OpenAI security staff","dek":"Three OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes discussing military AI with an impostor before the company concluded it was a prank.","summary":"Russian comedy duo Vovan and Lexus impersonated Ukrainian security official Rustem Umerov on a 17-minute video call with three OpenAI national security officials, The Intercept reported on November 11, 2026. OpenAI said it investigated, concluded the call was a prank and changed its procedures.","seo_title":"Russian pranksters fooled OpenAI national security officials","seo_description":"Vovan and Lexus posed as Ukraine's Rustem Umerov on a 17-minute video call with three OpenAI officials about military AI. OpenAI calls it a prank.","answer_summary":"Three OpenAI national security officials held a 17-minute video call with Russian pranksters posing as Ukrainian official Rustem Umerov. OpenAI says it investigated, concluded it was a prank and took steps to prevent a repeat.","tags":["OpenAI","Ukraine","Vovan and Lexus","AI security","Military AI"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Three senior OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes on a video call with a man they believed was Rustem Umerov, a senior Ukrainian security official, according to a report The Intercept published on November 11, 2026. The caller was in fact part of Vovan and Lexus, a Russian comedy duo known for prank calls, and the pair later posted a recording of the conversation online.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans told The Intercept that the company had opened an investigation into the call's authenticity weeks earlier, worked internally and with the relevant authorities, and concluded that it was a prank. He said OpenAI had taken action to prevent similar situations in the future. The company did not say when the call took place or which measures it adopted, according to Digit.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who was on the call","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The OpenAI participants were Sasha Baker, who leads national security policy at the company and previously held a senior Defense Department post; Caroline Zier, OpenAI's lead for strategic initiatives, who also worked at the Defense Department; and Ben Crampton, who leads the company's European national security work and previously worked for the European Union and the United Nations, The Intercept reported.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Baker and Zier said during the call that they had met Umerov before. The impersonator appears to have kept his camera off. Vladimir Kuznetsov, one of the two pranksters, told The Intercept that the duo first reached a senior Ukrainian official in San Francisco while posing as Umerov, and that this official believed he was setting up a meeting with OpenAI.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the officials discussed","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The fake official asked about OpenAI's possible military support for Ukraine, including offensive capabilities. Crampton said the company wanted as deep a relationship with Ukraine as possible but might not reach that goal right away. He also described a general reluctance among many senior people at OpenAI about offensive military uses, and said offense and defense cannot always be told apart, according to accounts of the recording.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The officials mentioned Daybreak Blue, an OpenAI model that finds and fixes computer vulnerabilities, and a developing partnership with Ukraine's Ministry of Defense. Baker said OpenAI had been in contact with the Pentagon about helping Ukraine. When the caller asked whether OpenAI could help counter Elon Musk's influence, Baker said the company probably could not help with Musk.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Business Today, citing The Intercept, noted that OpenAI has an ongoing $200 million contract with the U.S. Department of War to supply AI applications for military users.","sources":[{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who Vovan and Lexus are","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Vovan and Lexus are the pseudonyms of Vladimir Kuznetsov and Alexei Stolyarov, according to Digit. They have made prank calls to public figures since 2011, including Elton John and the late Senator John McCain. Their pranks often line up with Russian foreign policy, and they have been accused of working with the Russian government, which they deny. The Ukrainian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to The Intercept's request for comment.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The episode shows how much weight a familiar name and title can carry in a remote meeting. The call reached OpenAI through a real Ukrainian official, and two of the three participants believed they already knew the person on the other end. For an AI company that now works with defense customers, conversations about military uses carry far higher stakes than an ordinary sales call, and a caller with the camera off is a gap that formal identity checks can close without relying on recognition.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal to watch is whether OpenAI or other AI labs describe the identity checks they now require before national security conversations, and whether Ukrainian officials explain how the introduction to OpenAI was arranged.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: AI just gave Geralt's voice actor his old voice back
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Jacek Rozenek, the Polish voice of Geralt, had a stroke in 2019 that left him unable to speak. He came back to voice acting in 2022 after hours of training a day. His voice had changed. For the new expansion, Songs of the Past, Rozenek recorded every line himself. CD Projekt Red gave AI voice firm Respeecher all his old Witcher 3 lines to build a model, which made the new lines sound like him 12 years ago. Rozenek agreed to it. CD Projekt Red says its contracts require consent for any AI work and calls this a special case. Sources: Video Games Chronicle, GamesRadar+, Nintendo Life.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Geralt of Rivia, the white haired hero of The Witcher 3, in a scene from the game.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"CD Projekt Red used AI to restore Geralt's Polish voice after the actor's stroke","dek":"Jacek Rozenek recorded new lines for The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past himself, and a Respeecher model trained on his original performance brought them closer to how he sounded in the original game.","summary":"CD Projekt Red worked with the AI voice company Respeecher to adjust the Polish voice of Geralt in the upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past, after actor Jacek Rozenek's voice changed following a 2019 stroke. CD Projekt Red used an AI model from Respeecher, trained on Jacek Rozenek's original Witcher 3 recordings, to adjust the new Polish Geralt lines he recorded for Songs of the Past. Video Games Chronicle reported that the stroke left Rozenek unable to speak and that he returned to voice acting in 2022 after training for hours a day.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the AI was used","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Rozenek recorded the new lines for the expansion himself, in the usual way. The studio then sent the lines he had recorded for the base game of The Witcher 3 to Respeecher, a Ukrainian company that builds AI voice models. Respeecher trained a model on that original performance and used it to retouch the new recordings so they sit closer to the voice players heard in the base game.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"},{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to GamesRadar+, the new lines clashed with the original dialogue without that step. Mikołaj Szwed, a localization producer at CD Projekt Red, said in the interview that the studio delivered to Respeecher all of the lines Rozenek had recorded for The Witcher 3. Respeecher's Dmytry Vasylets described the brief as making the actor's voice sound alive, rich and young, as it did in the original game.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Rozenek said the goal was for the voice to be as close as possible to his voice from 12 years earlier, and he said he has great trust in the people who make the game. Both outlets reported that he consented to the use of AI on his performance. The interview was first published by Game File.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"},{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A case the studio calls special","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CD Projekt Red says its contracts require consent for any AI work on a performance, and that it turned to AI here only because of Rozenek's health situation. Szwed called it a special case and said he sees it as a way to use AI ethically, with consent, to do something good. The studio has worked with Respeecher before, on a Cyberpunk 2077 character whose actor had died, GamesRadar+ reported.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"},{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The English version of Geralt, voiced by Doug Cockle, did not need any AI retouching for the expansion, according to GamesRadar+. Nintendo Life reported that Songs of the Past is due next year, in 2027.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"},{"name":"Nintendo Life","url":"https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2026/11/witcher-3s-new-expansion-pairs-geralts-polish-voice-actor-with-ai-but-its-a-special-case"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Most arguments about AI voices in games turn on copying a performer without permission. This case is built differently: the actor still performs every line, the model is trained only on his own earlier work for the same character, and he signed off on it. That combination of consent, the same performer and a narrow purpose is likely to be cited as a reference point in future arguments over where AI voice tools belong in game production.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next test is how players react when Songs of the Past ships in 2027, and whether other studios adopt the same consent based approach for veteran actors whose voices have changed with age or illness.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: United Airlines just banned AI assistants from booking your flights, even through travel agencies
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: United says it will stop unauthorized, third-party AI agents from booking flights for travelers, on its site and app and through travel agencies. AI tools can still show United's flights and fares. They just cannot finish the purchase. United says giving your login to an AI assistant can expose sensitive information, and the bot could buy tickets, change your account or spend MileagePlus miles. Check-in is an issue too: federal rules make travelers confirm their bags hold no banned items. Sources: CBS News, Air Data News.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A United Airlines Boeing 737 MAX passenger jet.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"United Airlines bans unauthorized AI agents from booking flights for travelers","dek":"The airline says personal AI assistants could expose account data, make unwanted purchases or spend MileagePlus miles, and it will block them on its own channels and through travel agencies.","summary":"United Airlines said on November 11, 2026, that it will prohibit unauthorized third-party AI agents from booking flights on travelers' behalf. The restriction covers United's website and app as well as travel agencies and aggregators, while AI tools may still display United's flights and fares.","seo_title":"United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights","seo_description":"United will block unauthorized AI agents from booking its flights on its site, its app and through travel agencies, citing security and federal rules.","answer_summary":"Unauthorized AI agents such as personal AI assistants can no longer complete United Airlines bookings for travelers, either on United's own platforms or through travel agencies. They can still show United flights and fares.","tags":["United Airlines","AI agents","Travel","Meta","OpenAI"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"United Airlines said on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that it will ban unauthorized third-party AI agents and assistants from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers, according to CBS News. The airline is updating its booking, ticketing and distribution policies to put the rule into effect, Air Data News reported.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The restriction applies to United's own digital platforms and also to indirect channels, meaning travel agencies and ticket aggregators. According to Air Data News, the policy does not stop AI assistants from showing United's flights and fares; it stops them from completing reservations through the airline's systems without authorization. United did not announce a specific timetable for enforcement.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CBS News cited Meta's Muse and OpenAI's dots as examples of the consumer AI agents that have started to book travel and handle other tasks for their users.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The reasons United gave","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"United's main argument is security. The airline said that sharing account credentials with personal third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and that actions taken by these tools can lead to purchases, account changes or use of MileagePlus miles that the customer did not intend, according to CBS News and Air Data News.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The airline also pointed to federal rules. At check-in, passengers must confirm that their luggage contains no prohibited items, and United said letting an agent handle that step without the traveler's direct confirmation could conflict with those requirements. Air Data News reported that United plans to update its Digital Trust Center to explain the change and to help customers affected by unintended actions taken by AI assistants.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Reservations completed by such tools before November 11 will be honored, according to Travel Weekly as cited by Air Data News. The airline said it will keep evaluating how third-party AI tools interact with its services, which leaves room for authorizing specific platforms later.","sources":[{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Control of the customer relationship","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"United chief executive Scott Kirby said at an event in Chicago on November 10 that he did not want to create another intermediary between the airline and its customers, The Wall Street Journal reported, as cited by Air Data News. Henry Harteveldt of Atmosphere Research Group told CBS News that the policy suggests United wants to keep control of the booking process, and that it likely also wants to avoid the costs of a surge in flight searches run by AI bots.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Other carriers are taking a different approach. Delta Air Lines has indicated that properly authenticated AI assistants can make reservations, with additional safeguards for sensitive transactions, according to Air Data News. Southwest Airlines has made its flight inventory available to ChatGPT users. Harteveldt told CBS News that United fares can still be booked through Kayak, Hopper and Google Flights.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The decision draws a clear line between AI tools that help travelers search and AI tools that act inside a customer's account. United is leaving the first kind alone and closing the door on the second unless it has approved the platform, which keeps the airline in charge of the final sale and of the data that comes with it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal is whether United authorizes any specific AI platform to book on its systems, and whether other large carriers follow its approach or Delta's.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Runway AI to make videos, and what the free plan really gets you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Free accounts get 125 credits once. They never expire but never refresh. Gen-4.5 video needs the Standard plan or higher. Gen-4.5 costs 12 credits a second, so 5 seconds is 60 credits. Gen-4 Turbo costs 5 a second. Runway suggests testing there first. Camera shot, subject, action, place, then light and style. Sources: Runway Help Center: How do credits work, Runway Help Center: Gen-4.5, Runway Help Center: Text to Video prompting guide, Runway Help Center: Creating with Gen-4, Runway Help Center: Standard plan, Runway: Introducing Runway Gen-4.5, eesel AI: Runway AI pricing in 2026.
