item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Higgsfield AI, and what you get for free","dek":"No free trial, a small free tier and credits that vanish on re-rolls: how to make your first video without wasting them.","summary":"Higgsfield lets you generate images and video with many models in one place, but its free tier offers only a few models and no credits. This guide covers the free tier, your first video step by step, and how credits, refunds and Unlimited access work.","seo_title":"How to use Higgsfield AI (and what you get for free)","seo_description":"How to use Higgsfield AI step by step: what the free tier includes, how to make your first video, two prompts to copy, and how credits and Unlimited work.","answer_summary":"To use Higgsfield AI, sign in at higgsfield.ai, open AI Video, pick a model, describe one shot and check the credit cost on the Generate button. The free tier has no credits and only a small set of models, and there is no free trial.","tags":["Higgsfield","AI video","Kling","Veo","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Higgsfield AI comes down to two things: picking the right model for each shot, and watching your credits. Higgsfield is a web platform that puts many image and video models in one place, including Kling, Veo, Seedance, Wan and MiniMax for video, and Nano Banana, Soul, FLUX, GPT Image and Seedream for images.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield: AI video generator","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/ai-video"},{"name":"Higgsfield: About","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/about"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short answer on price: you can use Higgsfield without paying, but only a small set of models, and no credits come with it. Higgsfield's own help center says there is no free trial. Everything below tells you what you can do for free, how to make your first video, and how not to burn credits by accident.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do Higgsfield plans work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/plans-and-subscriptions/how-do-higgsfield-plans-work"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you get on Higgsfield for free","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Higgsfield says you can generate on the free tier with a limited set of models and upgrade later. Paid plans add a monthly credit allowance, access to more models and the ability to run several generations at once. Mid and top plans also include Unlimited access to selected models, which means generations on those models cost no credits for a set period.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do Higgsfield plans work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/plans-and-subscriptions/how-do-higgsfield-plans-work"},{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: Unlimited models","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/what-are-unlimited-models-and-which-plans-include-them"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some plans also include a one-time pool of free generations on specific models. Higgsfield names Soul 2.0 and Soul Cinema as examples. These free generations do not renew, and each plan's exact pool is listed under Unlimited & Free Gens on its card on the Pricing page.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/how-credits-work"},{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: Unlimited models","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/what-are-unlimited-models-and-which-plans-include-them"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A third-party guide from Layer3Labs, updated November 9, 2026, says free output carries a watermark and treats the free tier as a demo rather than a way to work. The Higgsfield help pages used for this guide do not mention a watermark, so check your own export before you post anything.","sources":[{"name":"Layer3Labs: How to use Higgsfield","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-higgsfield"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first Higgsfield video","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the video workspace","text":"Sign in at higgsfield.ai and open AI Video. The Create Video Now button takes you into the video workspace with a model already selected.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Pick a model","text":"Choose a model from the list. The video page shows Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.0, Wan 2.7, Kling o1, MiniMax H3, Veo 3.1 and Kling 2.6. On the free tier you only see the small set of models Higgsfield allows there.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the shot","text":"Type a description of the shot into the prompt box and set the length. Describe one shot, not a whole story: who or what is in frame, what moves, where the camera is, and the light.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A simple product shot","text":"Slow push-in on a [product] standing on a wet stone table at night, soft rain in the background, warm light from one side, shallow depth of field, 8 seconds.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A person in motion","text":"Handheld tracking shot of a [person description] walking through a busy street market at sunset, camera follows from behind, then circles to the front as they stop and look up.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check the cost, then generate","text":"Look at the Generate button before you click. Higgsfield shows the exact credit cost there before you confirm. If you ask for 2, 3 or 4 results at once, each one is charged separately, and the total appears on the same button.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Use references when you need control","text":"The video page lists first and last frame references, editing a video you upload, and motion control from a reference video. Cinema Studio adds a choice of camera body, lens and focal length, and lets you stack up to three camera movements.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Draft on a cheaper model and run only the final shot on a premium one. Layer3Labs suggests drafting on Kling or Seedance and finishing on Veo 3.1, and planning two to three attempts for each important shot.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How Higgsfield credits work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Credits pay for images, videos, re-rolls and upscaling. Browsing costs nothing. The cost depends on the model, the resolution and the length, which is why the Generate button is the only number to trust.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/how-credits-work"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Subscription credits reset every billing cycle, and unused ones expire at renewal. Credit Packs and Auto-Refill credits expire 90 days after purchase. Higgsfield spends your subscription credits first, then the others in order of expiry, soonest first.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/how-credits-work"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Failed generations usually return their credits within a few minutes, though Higgsfield says some models may not refund. To check, open your avatar, then Manage Account, then Usage. The log shows every deduction and refund with the model and the time.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/how-credits-work"},{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: What uses my credits","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/what-uses-my-credits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One trap: Unlimited and free generations only work on the higgsfield.ai website. Generations through MCP, the CLI, Canvas, Supercomputer or other automated tools always cost credits, even on a model that is unlimited on the site.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/how-credits-work"},{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: Unlimited models","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/what-are-unlimited-models-and-which-plans-include-them"},{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: What uses my credits","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/credits/what-uses-my-credits"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If your plan covers a model with Unlimited access, the generation panel shows an Unlimited toggle. Turn it on to stop spending credits. Turn it off and you pay credits, but the job runs in the faster priority queue.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you pay for Higgsfield","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Higgsfield's paid plans cost less per month when billed yearly. Upgrades apply right away with a prorated charge. Refunds are available within 7 days of the first purchase if no credits were used, with a service fee of up to 6%, and renewals are not refundable. Prices are on the Pricing page, not in the help center.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do Higgsfield plans work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/plans-and-subscriptions/how-do-higgsfield-plans-work"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Where Higgsfield falls short: credits go fast once you start re-rolling, and Layer3Labs warns that colors, logos and labels can drift between takes, so a character or product may not look the same from clip to clip. Higgsfield is strongest as a single place to try many video models side by side, and weakest as a cheap way to produce a lot of finished footage.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep your source photos and the prompts that worked in a document outside Higgsfield. When you need a new version of the same shot later, you can start from the exact settings instead of guessing.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use n8n for free: build your first AI agent, step by step
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The self-hosted Community edition is free. With Node.js 20.19 to 24 installed, run npx n8n. Then open localhost:5678 in your browser. Docker works too. Go to aistudio.google.com/app/apikey and click Create API key in new project. In n8n, open the Gemini model node, pick Create New Credential, paste the key, save. Sources: n8n Docs: Choose your n8n, n8n Docs: Install with npm, n8n Docs: Install with Docker, n8n: Build your first AI agent (template), n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent, Techsy: n8n AI agents tutorial.
item.category: n8n: Build your first AI agent (template)
n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent

nf:hero.nf:alt: n8n's illustration for its guide to building a first AI agent.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use n8n for free: build your first AI agent, step by step","dek":"Run the free Community edition, connect a free Google AI key and test an agent that calls real tools.","summary":"n8n's self-hosted Community edition is free and runs with one command. Its official starter template turns a free Google AI API key into a chat agent that uses tools and remembers follow-up questions.","seo_title":"How to use n8n for free: your first AI agent, step by step","seo_description":"Run n8n free on your computer, add a free Gemini API key and build a chat AI agent with tools and memory. Commands, steps and a system message to copy.","answer_summary":"To use n8n for free, self-host the Community edition (run npx n8n with Node.js 20.19 to 24, or use Docker), open localhost:5678, then add an AI Agent with a Google Gemini model using a free API key from Google AI Studio.","tags":["n8n","AI agents","Automation","Gemini","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use n8n for free comes down to one choice: host it yourself. n8n's self-hosted Community edition is free and, in the company's words, comes with almost the complete feature set. n8n Cloud, the hosted version, offers a 14 day trial with Pro features and then moves to the paid Starter, Pro or Enterprise plans.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Docs: Choose your n8n","url":"https://docs.n8n.io/choose-n8n/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Here is the payoff. In about five steps you get an AI agent that answers in a chat window, decides on its own when to call a tool, and remembers the last few messages. All of it runs on n8n's official starter template and a free Google AI API key.","sources":[{"name":"n8n: Build your first AI agent (template)","url":"https://n8n.io/workflows/6270-build-your-first-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Cloud or self-hosted: which n8n to pick","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n's own comparison says self-hosting needs technical expertise for installation and configuration, and it recommends n8n Cloud to people who do not have that expertise. If you are comfortable typing a command in a terminal, the free edition is enough for this guide. If you register your email in the free edition, n8n unlocks a few extras: folders, debug in editor and custom execution data.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Docs: Choose your n8n","url":"https://docs.n8n.io/choose-n8n/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One more cost to know about: the AI model is billed separately from n8n. A tutorial from Techsy notes that the self-hosted Community edition has no execution limits, but any OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini usage is charged by that provider. The Gemini key in this guide is free to create, which makes it the cheapest way to start.","sources":[{"name":"Techsy: n8n AI agents tutorial","url":"https://techsy.io/blog/n8n-ai-agents-tutorial"},{"name":"n8n: Build your first AI agent (template)","url":"https://n8n.io/workflows/6270-build-your-first-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Step by step: your first n8n AI agent","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Install and start n8n","text":"Install Node.js, version 20.19 to 24.x according to n8n's docs. Then open a terminal and run npx n8n to try it without installing anything, or npm install n8n -g followed by n8n start to keep it. Open http://localhost:5678 in your browser. n8n's docs say npm installs are deprecated starting with n8n 3.0, so if you plan to keep using it, the Docker route is the safer long-term setup.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Or start it with Docker","text":"With Docker Desktop installed, create a volume with docker volume create n8n_data, then run the n8nio/n8n image with port 5678 open and that volume mounted to /home/node/.n8n, as the install page shows. Set GENERIC_TIMEZONE to your time zone so scheduled workflows run at the right hour. n8n's docs now point to Docker Compose as the recommended method for a lasting setup.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Get a free Google AI API key","text":"Go to aistudio.google.com/app/apikey, click Create API key in new project and copy the key. n8n's starter template says this free key is the only thing you need to bring.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Load the starter agent and add the key","text":"Open the Build your first AI agent template from n8n's template library. On the canvas, open the node named Connect your model (Google Gemini), choose Create New Credential in the Credential dropdown, paste the key into the API Key field and click Save. The template already wires a Chat Trigger to an AI Agent node, plus a Simple Memory node for follow-up questions and two tools: Get Weather and Get News, which reads an RSS feed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Open the chat and test it","text":"Go to the Example Chat node and click Open Chat in its panel. Ask for the weather in Paris, then ask for the latest tech news. A weather answer shows the Get Weather tool works; a list of headlines shows Get News works. Ask a follow-up question about the same city to check that memory is doing its job.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build it yourself instead of using the template","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n's blog walks through the same pieces by hand. Click the plus button on an empty canvas and add a Chat Trigger. Add an AI Agent node and connect the trigger to it. In the agent, choose Connected Chat Trigger Node as the source of the user message. Add a chat model node, such as Google Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic, create its credential and connect it to the agent's Chat Model input. Tools go into the agent's Tool input.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent","url":"https://blog.n8n.io/how-to-build-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The agent's behavior lives in the System Message, under Options in the AI Agent node. n8n's guide suggests stating the task, explaining when and how to use each tool, and adding constraints. Rename each tool node so its name matches the name you use in the System Message.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent","url":"https://blog.n8n.io/how-to-build-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A starter System Message","text":"You are a research assistant.
When the user asks about the weather, call the [weather tool name] tool.
When the user asks for news, call the [news tool name] tool and return the 3 most relevant headlines with one line each.
If no tool fits the question, say you cannot check that. Never guess.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"After every test, open the execution in n8n and look at the AI Agent node's input and output. n8n's guide recommends this to see which tools the agent actually called. If it skipped a tool, the fix is usually a clearer System Message or a better description on the tool.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where n8n agents struggle","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Techsy tutorial reports that agents get confused once they have more than about five to seven tools, that they can fail without an obvious error, and that n8n gives less control over agent design than code frameworks such as LangGraph or CrewAI.","sources":[{"name":"Techsy: n8n AI agents tutorial","url":"https://techsy.io/blog/n8n-ai-agents-tutorial"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"n8n is a workflow tool first, and it shows. The practical answer is the same as with any agent: one narrow job, a few tools, and a test run before you trust it with anything real.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep your first agent read-only. Weather, news and summaries cannot do damage. Add tools that send email or write to a database only after you have watched a few executions and the agent calls the right tool every time.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use CapCut AI: captions, scripts and clips in minutes
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On desktop: import your video, open the Text tab, click Auto captions, pick the language and click Create. The captions land on the timeline, ready to edit. Read every line. Accents, noise and names trip the AI up. On the web, the Styles tab has looks like Glow, or let Style captions with AI pick one. Sources: CapCut: How to add subtitles in CapCut, CapCut: AI Clip Maker, CapCut: Script to video maker, CapCut Help Center: Standard vs Pro, CapCut Help Center: new subscription pricing, Descript.
item.category: CapCut: How to add subtitles in CapCut
CapCut Help Center: Standard vs Pro
CapCut Help Center: new subscription pricing

nf:hero.nf:alt: CapCut promotional image for adding subtitles to a video.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use CapCut AI: auto captions, AI video maker and clipper","dek":"Step by step instructions for the three CapCut AI tools people use most, and what each one needs from your plan.","summary":"CapCut's AI tools can add captions to a video, turn a script into a first draft and cut a long video into short clips. CapCut's help center lists auto captions among the Pro plan's AI tools, so check your plan before you start.","seo_title":"How to use CapCut AI: captions, video maker and clipper","seo_description":"How to use CapCut AI step by step: auto captions on desktop, web and phone, script to video, the AI Clip Maker for shorts, and what needs Pro.","answer_summary":"To use CapCut AI captions on desktop, import a video, open the Text tab, click Auto captions, pick the language and click Create. Script to video and the AI Clip Maker work from CapCut's tools pages, and CapCut lists auto captions as a Pro feature.","tags":["CapCut","AI video","Auto captions","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use CapCut AI, start with three tools. Auto captions writes subtitles from the speech in your video. Script to video writes a script from your idea and builds a first draft from stock footage. The AI Clip Maker finds the best moments in a long video and cuts them into short vertical clips. All three come from CapCut's own instructions below.","sources":[{"name":"CapCut: How to add subtitles in CapCut","url":"https://www.capcut.com/resource/how-to-add-subtitle-in-capcut"},{"name":"CapCut: AI Clip Maker","url":"https://capcut.com/tools/long-video-to-shorts"},{"name":"CapCut: Script to video maker","url":"https://www.capcut.com/tools/script-to-video-maker"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One thing first: money. CapCut's help center lists auto captions, AI avatars and AI generated content among the advanced AI tools of its Pro plan, while the cheaper Standard plan gets basics like noise reduction. Descript, which sells a competing editor, reports that CapCut moved auto captions behind a paid tier in a 2025 pricing change. CapCut says Pro now comes with 1,200 AI credits and 1TB of cloud storage, and that prices depend on your region and platform, so check the subscription page in the app before you plan around it.","sources":[{"name":"CapCut Help Center: Standard vs Pro","url":"https://www.capcut.com/help/capcut-standard-vs-pro"},{"name":"CapCut Help Center: new subscription pricing","url":"https://www.capcut.com/help/new-capcut-subscription-pricing"},{"name":"Descript","url":"https://descript.com/blog/article/capcut-captions-arent-free-anymore-heres-a-better-option"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to add auto captions in CapCut","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. On desktop: import your video","text":"Open CapCut on your computer and start a new project. In the left sidebar, open the Import tab under Media and click Import, or drag your video into the workspace.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Create the captions","text":"Open the Text tab at the top and click Auto captions. In the pop up, choose the language spoken in the video and click Create. The captions appear on the timeline as separate text clips.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Edit and style them","text":"Use the right sidebar. Captions is where you fix the words. Text, Animation and Tracking control the font, size, layout and movement. When you are happy, click Export in the top right corner, set resolution, frame rate and format, and click Export again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. On the web: use AI captions","text":"On the CapCut web start page, find the You may want to try section and click AI captions. Upload a video from your computer or your CapCut cloud space. CapCut says the video has to be shorter than 20 minutes. The text shows up in the Subtitles tab, where you can edit, delete or add lines. The Styles tab has looks such as Glow, Trending and Aesthetic, or you can click Style captions with AI and let it choose. Then click Export, or Edit more to open the full editor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. On your phone: tap Auto captions","text":"In the mobile app, tap Auto captions on the main screen, pick a video or audio file and tap Add. Choose the language and a template style, then tap Generate. Tap Edit captions to fix the text and change fonts and animations, then tap Done and export or share.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Read every caption before you post. CapCut itself says accents, background noise and specialist words can need manual fixes, and names are the usual casualty. If your language is not offered, you can still type subtitles with the text tools and line them up by hand.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to turn a script into a video","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Script to video","text":"Sign in to CapCut and open the Script to video tool in your browser. Click Narration for a voice led script, or Commercial if you are selling a product or service, and describe what the video is about.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Pick a script","text":"The AI writer gives you five scripts. Pick the one closest to what you want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt: a short narration idea","text":"A 45 second video for small business owners about three simple ways to answer customer emails faster. Friendly, plain words, one tip per scene, end with a short call to action.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Generate and replace","text":"Click Generate video. CapCut builds a first draft from stock footage. Open it in the multi track editor to swap clips for your own, adjust captions, transitions and the voiceover, and set the shape of the video. Then click Export, name the project, choose resolution, frame rate and format, and download it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Be realistic about this one. A draft made of stock footage looks like a draft made of stock footage. It is a fast way to get timing and structure, and a poor way to get something that feels like yours. Replace at least the opening shots with your own material.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to cut a long video into shorts with the AI Clip Maker","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload the long video","text":"Upload from your computer, CapCut cloud, Google Drive or Dropbox, and keep the page open until the upload finishes. CapCut suggests the tool for video podcasts, lessons, commentary and speeches, where people talk on camera.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Let it find the highlights","text":"The AI Clip Maker picks the strongest moments and cuts them into short clips. CapCut says it can also crop a wide 16:9 video to vertical 9:16 while tracking the speaker, and add captions. Before you export, you can change clip length and apply templates.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Check, edit, export","text":"Click Preview to watch each clip. Click Edit more to trim or fix one in the editor. Click Export to save it or share it straight to social media.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The AI picks moments from speech, so a clip can start mid thought or end before the punchline. Watch the first and last three seconds of every clip and trim by hand. Those six seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What CapCut AI is good at, and what it is not","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"CapCut AI is good at the boring parts of short video: getting words on screen, finding the clip worth posting and turning a wide video into a vertical one. It is weaker at judgment. It does not know which name it misheard, which joke landed or whether stock footage fits your brand. Use it to get to a first version fast, then spend your own time on the opening seconds and the captions, because that is where viewers decide.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use DeepSeek safely: the settings to change and what never to type
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: DeepSeek's privacy policy says it stores what it collects on servers in China. That includes your prompts, uploaded files and chat history. Type nothing you would not want stored there. On the web, open Settings, then Data, and switch off the option to improve the model for everyone. In the app, Kaspersky found the same switch under Settings, then Data controls. Sources: DeepSeek Privacy Policy, DeepSeek API Docs: DeepSeek V4 Preview Release, Kaspersky, DeleteMe, The Hacker News, Wikipedia: DeepSeek (chatbot).
item.category: DeepSeek API Docs: DeepSeek V4 Preview Release

nf:hero.nf:alt: How to use DeepSeek safely: the settings to change and what never to type

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use DeepSeek safely: settings to change and what to keep private","dek":"DeepSeek is free and capable, and its privacy policy says your chats are stored in China. Here is how to use it with less risk, step by step.","summary":"DeepSeek's web chat and apps are free, and the company's privacy policy says prompts, files and chat history are stored on servers in China and may be used to train its models. You can switch off training on your chats, delete shared links and chats, and keep personal details out of what you type.","seo_title":"How to use DeepSeek safely: privacy settings, step by step","seo_description":"How to use DeepSeek safely: turn off model training, delete shared links and chats, delete your account, and what never to type into it.","answer_summary":"Use DeepSeek for general questions only, never for personal, financial or work secrets. On the web, open Settings, then Data, switch off the option to improve the model for everyone, delete shared links you do not need and clear old chats.","tags":["DeepSeek","AI privacy","AI guides","Chatbots"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Learning how to use DeepSeek safely starts with one line in its privacy policy: the company says it stores the information it collects on secure servers located in the People's Republic of China. That covers what you type, the files you upload, your feedback and your chat history, plus account details and device information such as your IP address and device model.","sources":[{"name":"DeepSeek Privacy Policy","url":"https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy-2025-02-14.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The upside is real. The DeepSeek chatbot is free on the web and in its iOS and Android apps, and the company released its V4 models on April 24, 2026, with a context window of one million tokens that it says is now the default across its official services. So the goal here is not to scare you off. It is to set up DeepSeek so you share as little as possible, and to know what never to type into it.","sources":[{"name":"DeepSeek API Docs: DeepSeek V4 Preview Release","url":"https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260424/"},{"name":"Wikipedia: DeepSeek (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_(chatbot)"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What DeepSeek does with your data","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The privacy policy lists training and improving DeepSeek's technology, including its machine learning models, among the uses of the information it collects. Account data, including your inputs, is kept while your account is active, and the policy says some information can be kept longer to meet legal obligations or legitimate business interests.","sources":[{"name":"DeepSeek Privacy Policy","url":"https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy-2025-02-14.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kaspersky adds two points worth knowing. As a company based in China, DeepSeek may be required to hand data to Chinese authorities. And because chats can end up in training data, Kaspersky warns that a model can sometimes repeat training data to other users, which is why it advises keeping sensitive information out entirely.","sources":[{"name":"Kaspersky","url":"https://www.kaspersky.com/blog/deepseek-privacy-and-security/54643/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Governments have reacted. On October 20, 2026, the Federal Register published a Department of Homeland Security order that tells federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products from their systems and stop buying them, including third party products developed using DeepSeek. According to The Hacker News, the order does not restrict companies or the public. Earlier, Italy's data protection authority ordered DeepSeek blocked in January 2025, and Australia, Canada and South Korea barred it from government devices.","sources":[{"name":"The Hacker News","url":"https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/us-orders-deepseek-removed-from-federal.html"},{"name":"Wikipedia: DeepSeek (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_(chatbot)"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use DeepSeek safely: the settings to change","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign up with email, not a social login","text":"Kaspersky recommends creating your account with an email address and a strong password you use nowhere else, rather than signing in with Google. At the time of its review, DeepSeek offered no two factor authentication or passkeys, so the password is your only lock.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Turn off training on your chats","text":"On the web, sign in at chat.deepseek.com, open the sidebar, click the three dots next to your name and choose Settings. Open Data and switch off the option to improve the model for everyone. Kaspersky found the same switch in the mobile app under Settings, then Data controls. This only covers future chats: Kaspersky says data already used for training needs an email to privacy@deepseek.com.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Delete shared links you do not need","text":"Anyone who has a shared chat link can read that chat. In Settings, open Data and click Manage next to Shared links. Click the bin icon next to each link you want gone and confirm with Delete.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Clear old chats","text":"To remove one chat, hover over it in the sidebar, click its three dots and choose Delete. To remove everything, go to Settings, then Data, and click Delete all next to Delete all chats. Kaspersky notes that this removes chats from your account, not necessarily from DeepSeek's servers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Export, then delete the account if you are done","text":"If you want a copy first, use Settings, then Data, then Export. DeleteMe says the download link expires after seven days, and Kaspersky says JSON exports are available only on the web. Then open Settings, then Profile, click Delete next to Delete account, type DELETE MY ACCOUNT and confirm. DeepSeek's policy says a deleted account cannot be reactivated or recovered.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What never to type into DeepSeek","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Treat every message as something stored on a server you do not control. Keep out passwords and login codes, ID and account numbers, health details, client or employer documents, private photos, and anything about other people that they did not agree to share.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If your job involves a government agency or a federal contract, check your employer's rules before you open DeepSeek on a work device. The DHS order covers federal civilian agencies and, through a contract clause, the contractors working for them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"DeepSeek works best for tasks where nothing is private: explaining a concept, drafting a generic email, checking code that contains no secrets, or summarizing a public article. When you need help with something personal, remove the identifying details first. The prompt below lets you keep the structure of a text while the real names and numbers stay with you.","sources":[{"name":"Kaspersky","url":"https://www.kaspersky.com/blog/deepseek-privacy-and-security/54643/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt: rewrite a text with the private details removed","text":"The text below uses placeholders like [NAME], [COMPANY], [CITY] and [AMOUNT] instead of real details.
Keep every placeholder exactly as it is, in the same place.
Rewrite the text so it is clear, polite and under 150 words.

Text:
[paste your text with placeholders here]","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Once you get the answer back, swap the real names and numbers in yourself. It takes a minute, and the private part never leaves your computer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The most private option: run DeepSeek on your own computer","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"DeepSeek publishes the weights of its models under the MIT License, while the web and mobile apps are proprietary. That means you can run a version of the model locally, where your chats never reach the company's servers. Kaspersky suggests LM Studio, which works offline, and says smaller models in the 7B to 13B range suit a laptop with 16 to 32 GB of RAM. The trade off, according to Kaspersky: a local model cannot look up current information online.","sources":[{"name":"Kaspersky","url":"https://www.kaspersky.com/blog/deepseek-privacy-and-security/54643/"},{"name":"Wikipedia: DeepSeek (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_(chatbot)"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Running it locally does not remove every issue. Reports collected on Wikipedia's DeepSeek page say locally hosted versions still sometimes give answers consistent with Chinese Communist Party narratives, and the hosted chatbot limits answers on topics such as the Tiananmen Square massacre and Taiwan's political status.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: DeepSeek (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_(chatbot)"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"DeepSeek is a strong free model, and for public, low stakes questions it does the job. The problem is not the quality of the answers but where the conversation lives afterward. Switch off training, clear your shared links, keep personal and work details out, and use a local model or a different assistant when the subject is private.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to build your first Zapier AI agent for free, step by step
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at agents.zapier.com. Take the tour, or use the + icon in the sidebar and pick New agent. Describe the job in plain English or start from a template. Choose what starts the agent: on demand, on a schedule, from a Zap or from another app. Example: a new lead arrives, the agent sums it up and emails sales. Open Insert tools, then Add tool. Add data sources like Google Drive or Notion, and actions like a Gmail draft. Sources: Zapier: Zapier Agents guide, Zapier Help Center: How is Zapier Agents usage measured?, Zapier Agents pricing, Zapier: Zapier Agents overview, XRAY Tech.
item.category: Zapier Help Center: How is Zapier Agents usage measured?

nf:hero.nf:alt: Zapier logo artwork on a light yellow background.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Zapier AI agents: how to build your first one, with examples","dek":"Zapier Agents runs a job you describe in plain English across your apps. Here is how to set one up, what the free plan covers and where agents still go wrong.","summary":"Zapier Agents lets you build an AI agent from plain-language instructions, a trigger, data sources and app actions. The free plan includes 400 activities a month, and tests count toward that limit.","seo_title":"Zapier AI agents: how to build your first one (free plan)","seo_description":"Build your first Zapier AI agent: trigger, tools, instructions and testing, step by step. Plus free plan limits, what counts as an activity and a prompt to copy","answer_summary":"Sign in at agents.zapier.com, click New agent, describe the job in plain English, pick a trigger, add data sources and actions under Insert tools, then test it in the right panel and click Save. The free plan allows 400 activities a month.","tags":["Zapier","AI agents","Automation","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier AI agents are assistants you set up with plain-language instructions. Each one can start on a trigger, read from data sources such as Google Drive or Notion, search the web and run actions in the apps Zapier connects to. Zapier says the product has moved out of beta into general availability, and anyone with a Zapier account can try it for free at agents.zapier.com.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents guide","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/"},{"name":"Zapier Agents pricing","url":"https://zapier.com/l/agents-pricing"},{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents overview","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: one agent, one narrow job, a small set of tools, and a test run before you let it work alone. Below is the setup step by step, the limits of the free plan and a starter prompt you can copy.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents guide","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Zapier AI agents cost and what counts as an activity","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier measures agent usage in activities, not in the tasks used by regular Zaps. The Free plan includes 400 activities a month with up to 10 per run. Pro includes 1,500 a month with up to 40 per run and costs $33.33 a month billed annually ($400 a year). Enterprise has a custom limit and adds agent sharing across the company.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier Help Center: How is Zapier Agents usage measured?","url":"https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/26559132765325"},{"name":"Zapier Agents pricing","url":"https://zapier.com/l/agents-pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One activity is one thing the agent does: using a trigger, answering from a knowledge source, running an action, browsing or scraping a page, running a web search, or receiving a message through the Chrome extension. On the Free plan, test runs count toward your 400. On paid plans they do not.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier Help Center: How is Zapier Agents usage measured?","url":"https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/26559132765325"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When you reach the limit, agents stop running actions, searches, triggers and knowledge lookups until your billing date resets the count, though you can still chat with them. Zapier emails you at 80 percent and again at 100 percent. If one run hits the per-run cap, the agent asks for your input before it continues.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier Help Center: How is Zapier Agents usage measured?","url":"https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/26559132765325"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to build your first Zapier agent","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start a new agent","text":"Go to agents.zapier.com and sign in. If you have no agents yet, click Take a tour, then Create my first agent. If you already have some, hover over the + icon in the left sidebar and click New agent.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe the job or pick a template","text":"Write what the agent should do in plain English, or choose one of the ready-made templates on the left. Click Create agent to let the prompt assistant tidy up your instructions, or Skip this step to keep your own wording.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Connect the apps you named","text":"If your instructions mention apps, Zapier asks you to connect those accounts. You can do it now from the dropdowns or skip it and come back later.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Choose a trigger","text":"Pick what starts the agent: on demand, on a set schedule, from a Zap or from another app. Zapier's own example is a new Facebook Lead Ads lead that the agent summarizes and emails to the sales team through Gmail.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Add data sources and actions","text":"Open the Insert tools tab and click Add tool. Choose an app as a data source, for example a Google Sheets file or a Notion page, or choose an action, for example creating a Gmail draft. You can also pick Call an agent to hand part of the work to another agent. Inside the Instructions field, typing a slash lets you insert an action or data.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Test it and save","text":"Run a test in the panel on the right, read what the agent did, adjust the instructions and test again. When it behaves, click Save. Use Share in the top right if a teammate should see or edit it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Check the activity log","text":"Click All activity in the left panel to see each run. Anything under Needs action is waiting for you: the agent needs more information, you told it to pause at a decision point, or a connection broke.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A starter prompt to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt: an inbox triage agent that only drafts","text":"You are my inbox assistant.
When a new email arrives:
1. Label it as urgent, normal or spam.
2. For urgent emails, write a short, polite reply draft in my voice.
3. For spam, do nothing.
Rules: never send an email yourself. Only create drafts. If you are not sure what the sender wants, write "Needs a human" at the top of the draft.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Zapier suggests writing instructions as if for a new team member with no context: give a role, put the steps in order, say how long and in what tone the output should be, and wrap long background in tags like <context>. Showing one example of the output you want also helps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Examples of Zapier agents worth trying","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier's template library has close to 100 agents. Its examples include lead enrichment that researches a lead, updates the CRM and drafts outreach; customer support that routes tickets using help docs; email management that drafts replies and archives spam; meeting prep that builds agendas in Google Docs; and expense tracking that logs invoices from QuickBooks or Stripe into Google Sheets.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents guide","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/"},{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents overview","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Zapier agents fall short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier itself says to use a regular Zap when you need precision and an agent when roughly 80 percent accuracy is acceptable and speed matters more. It recommends starting with low-stakes tasks, requiring approval before important actions and keeping risky actions, such as deleting data, inside a single agent.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents guide","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/"},{"name":"Zapier: Zapier Agents overview","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In hands-on testing, XRAY Tech found that fields left for the agent to fill in can change from run to run, and suggested fixing key values, such as the Slack recipient of a message, so the agent cannot choose them. It also found that template actions still need to be configured by hand.","sources":[{"name":"XRAY Tech","url":"https://www.xray.tech/post/ai-agents-zapier"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"On the Free plan, keep tests short. A test that browses the web and runs three actions can use several of your 400 monthly activities at once.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest pitch for Zapier Agents is a smart helper for repetitive, forgiving work: sorting, summarizing and drafting. Anything that sends, pays or deletes is better left as a draft that a person approves, at least until you have watched the activity log for a while.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Nano Banana in Gemini for free: 5 prompts that work
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images, Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor, Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement, Engadget, Tom's Guide.
item.category: Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images
Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor

nf:hero.nf:alt: A Google Pixel phone with the Gemini app open on its screen.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images","dek":"Nano Banana 2 is the image model inside the free Gemini app. Here is how to make a picture, edit your own photo and get better results with prompts you can copy.","summary":"Nano Banana 2 is Google's default image model in the Gemini app and the free choice for creating and editing pictures. Paid Google AI plans add Nano Banana Pro and higher limits.","seo_title":"How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images","seo_description":"How to use Nano Banana in Gemini for free: make images, edit your own photos, merge pictures, download them, plus 6 prompts to copy and the limits to know.","answer_summary":"Go to gemini.google.com, open the sidebar, choose Images and type a prompt that starts with a verb. To edit a photo, upload it and describe the change. Nano Banana 2 is the free default model.","tags":["Gemini","Nano Banana","Google","AI images","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use Gemini Nano Banana for free, the short answer is that you already have it. Nano Banana 2 is the default image model in the Gemini app, and Google's product page describes it as the free model for making and editing images. Google introduced it on February 26, 2026, built on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, and said it replaced Nano Banana Pro across the Fast, Thinking and Pro modes in the app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"},{"name":"Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement","url":"https://dev.to/googleai/nano-banana-2-combining-pro-capabilities-with-lightning-fast-speed-4fm1"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/googles-nano-banana-2-is-a-faster-version-of-nano-banana-pro-160000695.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It does two jobs. It creates new pictures from a text prompt, and it edits pictures you upload: change a background, swap an object, add something, or combine several photos into one. Google lists better text inside images, consistent characters across images and edits to one part of a photo as its main strengths.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"},{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You need a Google account signed in to Gemini. Google's help page says image editing is not available to users under 18, and the feature is limited to the countries and languages where the Gemini app works. Work and school accounts can have different rules or no access at all.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan has a daily limit. Google does not publish the exact number on its help page; it only says that limits apply and that paid Google AI plans get higher ones. Paid subscribers can also redo an image with Nano Banana Pro, the slower model meant for images that need more detail and more precise control.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"},{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first image with Nano Banana","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Gemini","text":"Go to gemini.google.com on a computer, or open the Gemini app on your phone, and sign in.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Images","text":"On the web, click Open Sidebar, then Images. You can pick one of the ready-made templates or type your own prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the prompt","text":"Start with a verb such as create, draw or generate. Then say the style, the subject, what the subject is doing and where. One clear sentence beats a list of keywords.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Download it","text":"Hover over the finished image and click Download full size. You can also click More under the image and choose Export to Docs if you want to keep working on it in a document.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The model you pick in Gemini decides which image model runs. According to Google's help page, Flash-Lite uses Nano Banana 2 Lite, which is quick but not made for several reference images or repeated edits. Flash and Pro use Nano Banana 2. So for editing work, switch away from Flash-Lite before you ask for the image.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to edit your own photo","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload the picture","text":"Start a chat in Gemini and add your photo with the upload button. You can add several pictures at once if you want Gemini to combine them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe only the change","text":"Say what should stay the same and what should change. Be concrete: which object, which side of the picture, which color.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Keep editing in the same chat","text":"Ask for one fix at a time. For an image you made earlier, open Library in the sidebar, click the image, click Chat under it and type the next change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Tom's Guide reported in December 2025 that the Gemini app lets you draw or circle on an uploaded photo to mark the spot you want changed, with or without a text prompt. Google's help page does not describe this tool, so if you do not see it, describe the spot in words instead.","sources":[{"name":"Tom's Guide","url":"https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/ai-image-video/nano-banana-now-lets-you-draw-prompts-directly-on-your-photos-sam-altman-is-going-to-hate-this"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gemini Nano Banana prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean first image","text":"Create a photorealistic image of [subject] [doing what] in [place], [time of day] light, shot from [angle].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Fix one part of a photo","text":"Keep everything in this photo exactly the same, but replace [the thing to change] with [the new thing]. Do not change the faces.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Combine photos","text":"Put the person from the first image and the [pet or object] from the second image together in the setting from the third image. Natural lighting, same style as the third image.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Text that reads right","text":"Design a [poster, invitation or card] that says \"[exact words]\" in large letters, with \"[smaller line]\" below it. Style: [watercolor, retro, minimal]. Background: [color].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Borrow a style","text":"Apply the colors, texture and mood of the second image to the subject in the first image. Keep the subject's shape and face unchanged.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: A new format","text":"Turn this image into a [9:16 vertical, 16:9 wide or square] version. Extend the background naturally and keep the subject centered.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google's own page lists changing the mood, lighting, camera angle or focus of a photo, and adjusting a picture to a different aspect ratio, as things the model handles. Those make good first experiments because the result is easy to judge.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Nano Banana needs help","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Google's help page itself points to the weak spots: the Lite model is not built for several references or repeated edits, and the free plan has a daily cap. In practice that means short, specific requests work best. Split a big edit into steps, tell the model what to keep as well as what to change, and when a result is close, ask for one fix instead of starting over so you do not spend your daily images.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every image is marked as AI-made. Google says each picture carries an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible watermark, and that you can upload an image to the Gemini app and ask whether Google AI made it. Google may also remove images whose prompts break its terms or its prohibited use policy.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you pay for a Google AI plan and an image needs finer detail or cleaner text, click More at the bottom right of the image and choose Redo with Pro. Free users stay on Nano Banana 2.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nano Banana 2 is not only in the Gemini app. Google said it is also the default in AI Mode and Lens in Search and in its Flow creative studio, where it costs zero credits, and Engadget noted it can keep the look of up to five characters consistent in one workflow.","sources":[{"name":"Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement","url":"https://dev.to/googleai/nano-banana-2-combining-pro-capabilities-with-lightning-fast-speed-4fm1"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/googles-nano-banana-2-is-a-faster-version-of-nano-banana-pro-160000695.html"}]}]}

item.title: ChatGPT image prompts that actually work: 5 tricks for better pictures and edits
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5, OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6, RuntimeWire, DataCamp.
item.category: OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6

nf:hero.nf:alt: ChatGPT image prompts that actually work: 5 tricks for better pictures and edits

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"ChatGPT Images: how to write image prompts and edit pictures that come out right","dek":"ChatGPT can now change one part of a picture and leave the rest alone. Here is how to prompt it, edit with it and turn images into GIFs.","summary":"ChatGPT Images 2.5 and 2.6 make targeted edits, follow rough sketches and can turn a picture into an animated GIF. The best results come from saying what must stay the same, changing one thing per request and marking unknown details as placeholders.","seo_title":"ChatGPT Images: prompts and editing tips that work","seo_description":"How to write ChatGPT image prompts, make targeted edits, use @Sketch and templates, and turn pictures into GIFs with Images 2.6. Prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Describe the image you want, then edit in small steps: say what must stay the same and change one thing per request. Type @Sketch to draw a layout, and use a picture or prompt to make a GIF.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","AI images","Prompts","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"ChatGPT makes and edits pictures right inside a chat. Since Images 2.5 arrived on September 8, 2026, OpenAI says edits change only what you ask for and keep the rest of the image intact, and earlier edits tend to stick across a long conversation. Images 2.5 rolled out to all ChatGPT tiers on desktop, mobile and web.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Images 2.6 followed on November 4, 2026. It adds animated GIFs and reference images you save once and reuse, and it is available across all subscription tiers on desktop, mobile and web, according to OpenAI's announcement and RuntimeWire.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6","url":"https://community.openai.com/t/images-upgraded-introducing-chatgpt-images-2-6/1412901"},{"name":"RuntimeWire","url":"https://runtimewire.com/article/openai-chatgpt-images-2-6-gifs-flare-sunburst-api"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version of this guide: describe the picture, then fix it in small steps. Say what must stay the same, change one thing per message, and use a sketch when words are not enough. The prompts below are ready to copy.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a clear first prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Write the subject first, then the setting, then the style and light. You do not need a long paragraph. A clear sentence or two beats a list of twenty adjectives, because every extra word is one more thing the model has to balance.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean first image","text":"A close-up photo of a ceramic coffee mug on a wooden kitchen table, morning sunlight from a window on the left, soft shadows, calm and warm.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's own example for Images 2.5 shows the style it handles well: concrete details about what a person wears and what surrounds them. Its sample prompt for a 1980s portrait begins with a smiling man with curly hair in a teal, navy and pink windbreaker and a gold chain, then adds the lights and a boombox.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Edit in small steps","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Editing is where the tool is strongest. DataCamp's hands-on test found that local edits, such as a new background, a changed line of text or one swapped object, work best, and that the rest of the picture holds up when the change is small and targeted. Moving several objects at once or re-posing a person can break consistency and leave artifacts outside the edited area.","sources":[{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload your photo or start from a generated image","text":"Add the picture to the chat, or make one with a first prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Name what must not change","text":"If a face, a logo or a product shape matters, say so in the same message as the edit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Keep the person, change the scene","text":"Change only the background to a quiet beach at sunset. Keep my face, hairstyle, clothes and pose exactly the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for one change per message","text":"Treat each follow-up as its own small request. If the date on a poster is wrong, ask to change that date, not to redo the whole poster.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: One fix at a time","text":"Change the date on the poster to [NEW DATE]. Do not change anything else.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can also point at the exact spot. OpenAI says Images 2.5 lets you place comments directly on an image for focused edits, so the model knows which area you mean without a long description.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use @Sketch and templates","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Type @Sketch in ChatGPT to draw directly in the chat and use the drawing as a guide. OpenAI says adding a style description helps. DataCamp found a sketch most useful for spatial details, such as where two characters stand, that are awkward to put into words. You do not need to draw well.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Sketch to finished picture","text":"@Sketch Turn my drawing into a children's book illustration: a small fox on the left, a big tree on the right, soft pastel colors.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Templates give you a starting format such as Poster or Merch. You then add the content, the design elements and the style, OpenAI says. They are good for repeat formats, though DataCamp notes they leave less room for open-ended ideas.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A poster with placeholders","text":"Poster for a neighborhood yard sale. Friendly, bright colors, hand-drawn feel.
Title: Yard Sale
Date: [DATE]
Address: [ADDRESS]
Leave space at the bottom for a small map.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Mark anything you do not know yet with brackets, like [DATE]. DataCamp's tests suggest giving the event details and the mood, then marking unknowns as placeholders, so you can fill them in later with a one-line edit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Reuse faces and make GIFs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"With Images 2.6 you can save reference images of yourself, your pets and recurring characters and reuse them without uploading them again, OpenAI says. You can also turn a prompt or an image into an animated GIF, then adjust the speed and edit individual frames before you share it.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6","url":"https://community.openai.com/t/images-upgraded-introducing-chatgpt-images-2-6/1412901"},{"name":"RuntimeWire","url":"https://runtimewire.com/article/openai-chatgpt-images-2-6-gifs-flare-sunburst-api"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: A reaction GIF","text":"Make a short looping GIF of my saved cat character waking up, stretching and yawning. Simple, clean background.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it still gets wrong","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Text is still a weak spot, especially small or dense type. Hair edges in portrait edits can look rough, and results can still have a recognizable AI look, according to DataCamp's review. Every image carries C2PA metadata and an invisible watermark that marks it as made with OpenAI tools, the company says.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If a long edit starts drifting, do not keep stacking fixes. Go back to the last good version, restate what must stay the same, and make the next change on its own.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Midjourney prompts that actually work: 5 rules from its own docs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics, Midjourney Docs: Parameter List, Midjourney Docs: Models, Midjourney Docs: Getting Started Guide, Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha, Evolink: Midjourney V8.1 prompt guide.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","dek":"Midjourney rewards short, precise prompts and a few settings placed at the end. Here is what its own documentation recommends, with prompts to copy.","summary":"Midjourney's documentation says short, simple prompts usually produce the best images, with exact numbers, precise words and only the details you care about. Settings such as aspect ratio go at the end of the prompt, and the --no parameter removes things you do not want.","seo_title":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","seo_description":"Write better Midjourney prompts: keep them short, use exact numbers, pick the details that matter, put parameters at the end and remove things with --no.","answer_summary":"Write a short description of the image you want with precise words and exact numbers, add only the details that matter (subject, medium, setting, lighting, color, mood, composition), then put parameters like --ar 16:9 at the end.","tags":["Midjourney","AI images","Prompts","Image generation","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney turns a written description into images. You type a prompt into the Imagine bar on the Create page at midjourney.com, press Enter, and it makes a set of four images. You need a paid plan before you can make your first image, according to Midjourney's Getting Started Guide.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Getting Started Guide","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/hc/en-us/articles/33329261836941-Getting-Started-Guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version of this guide: write less than you think, choose exact words, say how many of something you want, describe what should be in the picture rather than what should not, and put settings at the very end. Everything below comes from Midjourney's own documentation, plus notes from people who test new versions.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a short prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Prompt Basics page is blunt about length. Short, simple prompts usually produce the best images. It suggests thinking of a prompt as a quick snapshot of the idea, and it warns that long lists and detailed instructions can confuse the process. A prompt can be as small as one word. With fewer details you get more variety; with more details you get more control.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs give an example. A long, chatty request for blooming California poppies in bright orange, drawn with colored pencils, becomes one plain line.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The short version","text":"Colored pencil illustration of bright orange California poppies","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose exact words and numbers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Word choice matters. The docs recommend specific synonyms over generic ones, such as huge or enormous instead of big. Numbers matter even more. A plural like cats leaves the count up to Midjourney. Three cats, or a collective noun like a flock of birds, makes the result predictable.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Say how many","text":"Three cats asleep on a sunny windowsill, soft morning light","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Add only the details you care about","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When certain parts of the image matter to you, name them. Midjourney's docs list seven areas to think about: subject (a person, animal, object or place), medium (photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle), environment (indoors, underwater, in the city), lighting (soft, overcast, studio, neon), color (vibrant, muted, pastel, black and white), mood (calm, playful, gloomy, energetic) and composition (portrait, headshot, closeup, bird's-eye view).","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You do not need all seven. Pick the two or three that decide whether the image works for you, and let Midjourney's default style handle the rest.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A detailed photo","text":"Closeup photo of [subject] [doing something] in [place], [lighting] light, [color] colors, [mood] mood","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Put parameters at the end","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Parameters are settings you type after the description. Midjourney's parameter list says they go at the end of the prompt, with a space before the two dashes and no commas or periods inside them. The most useful ones for beginners are --ar to change the shape of the image, --s (stylize) to control how much of Midjourney's own artistic style is applied, --chaos to get more varied results, and --raw for more control over the output.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For the current V8.1 model, a third-party prompt guide from Evolink lists the defaults: square 1:1 images, stylize at 100 on a scale of 0 to 1000, and chaos at 0 on a scale of 0 to 100. Stylize sets how strongly Midjourney's default look is applied, so lower values give a plainer result.","sources":[{"name":"Evolink: Midjourney V8.1 prompt guide","url":"https://evolink.ai/docs/en/api-manual/image-series/midjourney/midjourney-v8-1-prompt-guide"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A wide image with a bit more style","text":"Watercolor painting of a lighthouse on a cliff at sunset --ar 16:9 --s 250","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use --ar 4:5 or --ar 9:16 for images meant for a phone screen, and --ar 16:9 for slides and desktop wallpapers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Say what you want, not what you do not want","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is the mistake most people make. If you write a party with no cake, the docs warn, you may still get a cake, because mentioning a thing can pull it into the image. Describe the scene you want instead. When you really need to remove something, use the --no parameter, which Midjourney's parameter list describes as the way to exclude elements from an image.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Remove an object","text":"Minimal living room with a gray sofa and tall windows --no plants","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Pick the right model","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Models page lists V6, V6.1, V7 and V8.1, plus Niji 7 for anime and illustration. You can choose one for a single image by adding --v and the number at the end, for example --v 8.1, or set a default in the settings panel. V8.1 renders standard jobs several times faster than earlier versions, holds on to small details and can make 2K images with --hd. It does not support some older features, including Character Reference and Omni Reference.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Testers report that newer models want clearer direction. Heather Cooper, who writes the Visually AI newsletter, found that V8 rewards more detail than V7 did, and she recommends switching to --raw for controlled or photorealistic results. Midjourney's docs say the same about Raw: it removes default styling for stronger prompt adherence.","sources":[{"name":"Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha","url":"https://heatherbcooper.substack.com/p/midjourney-v8-is-live-on-alpha-heres"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write the core line","text":"Describe the subject and the medium in one short sentence, such as a photo of a red bicycle against a white wall.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add two or three details","text":"Choose the lighting, mood or composition that matters most to you. Stop there.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add parameters","text":"Set the shape with --ar, and add --raw if the result looks too stylized.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Change one thing at a time","text":"If the image is not right, change a single word or setting and run it again, so you know what made the difference.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Text inside the image","text":"Vintage travel poster for a mountain town with the words \"Visit Alpine Falls\" --v 8.1","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For words inside an image, put the exact text in quotation marks. Cooper reports that V8 renders quoted text with higher accuracy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Midjourney is good at mood, lighting and style, and a short prompt often gives a more striking result than a long one. It is weaker when you need exact control over many objects at once, and results still vary from run to run. Treat the first set of four images as a draft, keep the version you like, and refine from there.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: GitHub Copilot is free in VS Code. 5 steps to make it write, explain and fix your code
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In VS Code, hover over the Copilot icon in the Status Bar, pick Use AI Features and sign in with GitHub. No plan yet? Signing in puts you on Copilot Free: 2,000 completions a month plus AI credits. Sources: GitHub Docs: Plans for GitHub Copilot, GitHub Docs: Quickstart for GitHub Copilot in your IDE, VS Code Docs: Set up GitHub Copilot, VS Code Docs: Inline suggestions from GitHub Copilot, VS Code Docs: GitHub Copilot cheat sheet, VS Code Docs: Complete your first task with an agent, VS Code Docs: Custom instructions, Fast.io: How to use GitHub Copilot.
