item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"GitHub Copilot in VS Code: how to set up the free plan and use it every day","dek":"Copilot Free gives you code suggestions, a chat that knows your files and an agent that can build small features. Here is how to set it up and use each part well.","summary":"GitHub Copilot Free works in VS Code after a GitHub sign-in, with 2,000 completions a month and an allowance of AI credits. Tab accepts suggestions, Ctrl+Alt+I opens chat, and Agent mode edits files and runs commands with your approval.","seo_title":"GitHub Copilot in VS Code: free plan setup and daily use","seo_description":"Set up GitHub Copilot Free in VS Code, accept suggestions with Tab, ask questions in chat, give Agent mode a task and add project instructions with /init.","answer_summary":"Open VS Code, hover over the Copilot icon in the Status Bar, select Use AI Features and sign in with GitHub. Without a paid plan you get Copilot Free with 2,000 completions a month and an allowance of AI credits.","tags":["GitHub Copilot","VS Code","GitHub","Microsoft","AI coding","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"GitHub Copilot is an AI coding assistant that works inside your code editor. In VS Code it does three jobs: it suggests code as you type, it answers questions about your code in a chat, and in Agent mode it takes a task, edits files and runs commands with your approval. GitHub says it also works in Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Eclipse and Xcode.","sources":[{"name":"GitHub Docs: Quickstart for GitHub Copilot in your IDE","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/quickstart-for-using-github-copilot-in-your-ide"},{"name":"VS Code Docs: GitHub Copilot cheat sheet","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/copilot-vscode-features"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: sign in to VS Code with GitHub, press Tab to accept suggestions, open chat and ask what a file does, then give Agent one small task and review every change. This guide follows the order of the official GitHub and VS Code quickstarts and covers the free plan's limits.","sources":[{"name":"GitHub Docs: Quickstart for GitHub Copilot in your IDE","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/quickstart-for-using-github-copilot-in-your-ide"},{"name":"VS Code Docs: Set up GitHub Copilot","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/setup"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Copilot Free costs nothing. GitHub's plans page says it is limited to 2,000 code completions a month and includes an allowance of GitHub AI credits, which chat and agents use. Free users get models through automatic model selection only, so you cannot pick a specific model.","sources":[{"name":"GitHub Docs: Plans for GitHub Copilot","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid plans add more credits and more model choice. Copilot Pro is $10 a month with 1,500 monthly AI credits, Pro+ is $39 a month and Max is $100 a month. Verified students get a separate free plan called Copilot Student, and GitHub says verified teachers and maintainers of popular open source projects may get Pro for free.","sources":[{"name":"GitHub Docs: Plans for GitHub Copilot","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One practical detail from an independent guide by Fast.io: on paid plans, code completions do not use AI credits, while chat, agents and command line sessions do. The same guide lists 50 chat requests a month for Copilot Free, a number GitHub's own plans page now describes only as a credit allowance.","sources":[{"name":"Fast.io: How to use GitHub Copilot","url":"https://fast.io/resources/how-to-use-github-copilot/"},{"name":"GitHub Docs: Plans for GitHub Copilot","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Set it up in VS Code","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Install VS Code and open a project","text":"Download VS Code if you do not have it, then open a folder with File > Open Folder. If VS Code asks whether you trust the folder, trust it only if you know where the code came from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Sign in with GitHub","text":"Hover over the Copilot icon in the Status Bar at the bottom of the window and select Use AI Features, then choose a sign-in method. You can also pick Sign in to use Copilot from the Copilot menu in the Status Bar, or run GitHub Copilot: Sign in from the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows and Linux, Shift+Command+P on a Mac).","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If your GitHub account has no Copilot plan, signing in enrolls it in Copilot Free with a monthly allowance of inline suggestions and AI credits. The VS Code docs note that telemetry is on in the free version, and that you can turn it off with the telemetry.telemetryLevel setting.","sources":[{"name":"VS Code Docs: Set up GitHub Copilot","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/setup"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Let it finish your code","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Type and press Tab","text":"Open a code file and start typing. Copilot shows a suggestion in dimmed ghost text, sometimes the rest of the line and sometimes a whole block. Press Tab to accept it or Escape to dismiss it. If several options exist, hover over the suggestion to flip between them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GitHub's quickstart uses a simple test: create a JavaScript file and type function calculateDaysBetweenDates(begin, end) {. Copilot suggests the body of the function in gray. The VS Code docs also describe next edit suggestions: after you change one thing, such as a function's parameters, Copilot suggests the related edits elsewhere in the file.","sources":[{"name":"GitHub Docs: Quickstart for GitHub Copilot in your IDE","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/quickstart-for-using-github-copilot-in-your-ide"},{"name":"VS Code Docs: Inline suggestions from GitHub Copilot","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editing/ai-powered-suggestions"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Write a comment that says what you want before you write the code, for example a class for a student with a name, an ID and methods to add and remove courses. Copilot uses the comment as its instructions.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ask questions in chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Open Chat","text":"Press Ctrl+Alt+I on Windows and Linux or Control+Command+I on a Mac. Chat can see the file you have open, so you do not need to paste code. For a quick question about a few lines, Ctrl+I (Command+I on a Mac) opens inline chat right in the editor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Get the big picture","text":"what does this file do?","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Understand one line","text":"explain this line","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For the second prompt, select a line of code first. The cheat sheet lists three modes in chat: Ask explains code without changing it, Plan researches a change before anything is built, and Agent does the work. Slash commands such as /explain, /fix and /tests explain code, suggest fixes and generate tests.","sources":[{"name":"GitHub Docs: Quickstart for GitHub Copilot in your IDE","url":"https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/quickstart-for-using-github-copilot-in-your-ide"},{"name":"VS Code Docs: GitHub Copilot cheat sheet","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/copilot-vscode-features"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Give Agent a real task","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Switch to Agent","text":"In the chat box, select Agent, describe the task and press Enter. The VS Code agents quickstart recommends the Auto model and Manual permissions, so the agent asks for your approval before it runs tools or reaches outside your project. It can still edit files inside your project folder.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Build something small (from the VS Code quickstart)","text":"Create a task list web app in a single index.html file with embedded CSS and JavaScript. Let me add, complete, and delete tasks. Save the tasks in local storage so they persist after a page reload. Use no external libraries.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Make it test its own work","text":"Open index.html in the integrated browser and validate the app.
Add a task, mark it complete, and delete it. Then add another task,
reload the page, and verify that the task persists. If any step fails,
fix the issue and repeat the complete flow.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can stop the agent at any time with the Stop button or send a new prompt to steer it. To undo its file changes, hover over an earlier request and select Restore Checkpoint. The docs warn that this does not reverse terminal commands, network requests or deployments.","sources":[{"name":"VS Code Docs: Complete your first task with an agent","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Review the diff before you commit. The VS Code docs say the agent's own check helps find problems but does not replace your review, so click through the app yourself too.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Teach it your project's rules","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Copilot reads an instructions file in your project and follows it in every chat. For Copilot in VS Code that file is .github/copilot-instructions.md or AGENTS.md, written in plain Markdown. Typing /init in chat makes Copilot analyze your codebase and draft the instructions for you.","sources":[{"name":"VS Code Docs: Custom instructions","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions"},{"name":"VS Code Docs: GitHub Copilot cheat sheet","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/copilot-vscode-features"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Add a house rule","text":"Add this to the project instructions: always run the tests before you tell me a task is done, and never add a new dependency without asking me first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When you are ready to commit, the sparkle button in the Source Control box writes a commit message from your staged changes.","sources":[{"name":"VS Code Docs: GitHub Copilot cheat sheet","url":"https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/copilot-vscode-features"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Copilot is only as good as the context it gets. Suggestions get worse when the relevant files are not open, and quality varies by programming language. Its code can be wrong or insecure, so treat it like code from a stranger: read it, run the tests and check anything that touches passwords or user data. On the free plan, the monthly limits also mean you should save chat and Agent for the jobs where they help most.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Fast.io's guide also lists the usual reasons Copilot goes quiet: you are not signed in, the language is turned off, the free limits are used up, or an organization's policy blocks it.","sources":[{"name":"Fast.io: How to use GitHub Copilot","url":"https://fast.io/resources/how-to-use-github-copilot/"}]}]}

item.title: Claude Code edits your files and runs commands while you just describe what you want. 5 steps to start
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Type cd and your folder's path, then claude. The first time, your browser opens so you can log in. You need a paid Claude plan or a Console account. The free plan does not include it. Press Shift+Tab to change how much Claude can do without asking you first. Ask it to commit your changes with a clear message, so every step can be undone with Git. Also works in VS Code, JetBrains, the desktop app and the web. Sources: Claude Code Docs: Quickstart, Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup, Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project, Anthropic: Claude Code, Bannerbear.
item.category: Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project

nf:hero.nf:alt: Headshot portrait of a smiling man.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Claude Code: how to install it and start coding with an AI agent","dek":"Anthropic's coding agent edits files and runs commands from a plain English request. Here is how to set it up, the first prompts to try and where it goes wrong.","summary":"Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding agent for the terminal, editors, the desktop and the web. It needs a paid Claude plan or a Console account, installs with one command and works best with small, specific tasks and a CLAUDE.md file.","seo_title":"Claude Code for beginners: install it and start in 5 steps","seo_description":"How to install Claude Code, log in, write your first prompts, set up CLAUDE.md with /init and keep control with permissions and Git.","answer_summary":"Install Claude Code with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash (or the PowerShell command on Windows), run claude in a project folder, log in with a paid Claude plan or Console account, and start by asking it to explain the project.","tags":["Claude Code","Anthropic","Claude","AI coding","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent. You describe what you want in plain English, and it reads your project, edits files and runs commands to get it done. It runs in the terminal and also in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, a desktop app and the web.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Anthropic: Claude Code","url":"https://claude.com/product/claude-code"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: install it with one command, open it inside a project folder, ask it to explain the code before it changes anything, then give it one small task and read what it did. This guide follows the order of Anthropic's own quickstart, with the parts beginners trip over.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need first","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan or a Claude Console account with API credits. Anthropic's setup page is clear that the free claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code. Companies can also run it through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"},{"name":"Bannerbear","url":"https://www.bannerbear.com/blog/how-to-install-claude-code-terminal-ide-web-desktop-setup/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It runs on macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 (version 1809) or later, and common Linux versions such as Ubuntu 20.04 and Debian 10, with at least 4 GB of RAM and an internet connection. You also need a project to work on. A copy of something you do not mind changing is ideal for a first try.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you have never used a terminal, Anthropic's docs point to a separate terminal guide, and there is also a desktop app that lets you use Claude Code without the terminal at all.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Install and log in","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Run the installer","text":"On a Mac, on Linux or in WSL, open a terminal and paste: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash. In Windows PowerShell, use: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex. The installer shows no progress while it downloads, so give it a minute. Homebrew (brew install --cask claude-code) and WinGet (winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode) work too, but those copies do not update themselves.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Check that it worked","text":"Open a new terminal window and type claude --version. It should print a version number followed by (Claude Code). If your terminal says the command is not found, the install folder is not on your PATH yet, and the docs have a troubleshooting page for exactly that. For a deeper check, claude doctor prints install health and settings problems without starting a session.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Start a session in your project","text":"Move into your project with cd and the folder's path, then type claude. The first time, Claude Code opens your browser so you can log in with your Claude account or Console account. Your login is saved, so you only do this once. Inside a session, /help lists the commands and /resume brings back an earlier conversation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Native installs update themselves in the background. Homebrew, WinGet and Linux package manager installs need a manual upgrade, and claude update applies an update right away on a native install.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Advanced setup","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Your first prompts","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to the quickstart, Claude Code reads project files as it needs them, so you do not have to paste code or add context by hand. That makes a question the best first move: you learn the project, and you see how Claude works before it touches anything.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Get a tour","text":"what does this project do? explain the folder structure and where the main entry point is","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Make one small change","text":"add a hello world function to the main file","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When Claude wants to change a file, it shows you the change. If it asks for approval, you pick Yes. Anthropic's product page says Claude Code asks for permission before it changes files or runs commands, and the docs say Shift+Tab switches the permission mode, which sets what it may do without asking.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Anthropic: Claude Code","url":"https://claude.com/product/claude-code"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Fix a real bug, specifically","text":"fix the login bug where users see a blank screen after entering wrong credentials","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Be specific. The docs contrast \"fix the bug\" with a request that names the bug and what the user sees. The second one gets far better results.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Break a big job into steps","text":"1. create a new database table for user profiles\n2. create an API endpoint to get and update user profiles\n3. build a webpage that allows users to see and edit their information","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Make it remember your project","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every session starts with a fresh memory. A file called CLAUDE.md fixes that: Claude loads it at the start of every session. Type /init and Claude analyzes your code and writes a first version with build commands, test instructions and the conventions it finds. If the file already exists, /init suggests improvements instead of overwriting it.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic recommends keeping each CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, because longer files use more context and get followed less reliably. A project file lives at ./CLAUDE.md and can be shared with your team through Git. Personal rules for every project go in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. You can also ask Claude to save a rule for you.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Save a rule for good","text":"add this to CLAUDE.md: always run the tests before you tell me a task is done","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code also keeps its own notes, called auto memory, based on your corrections. If you say something like \"always use pnpm, not npm\", it saves that. The /memory command shows these files and lets you edit or turn auto memory off.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: How Claude remembers your project","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Git as your undo button","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Code handles Git in plain English. You can ask what files you changed, ask it to commit with a descriptive message, create a branch or show the last five commits. Committing after each small task means every change can be undone.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Commit before you ask for anything big. If the result is wrong, you can go back in one step instead of untangling the edits by hand.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Claude Code acts on your real files and runs real commands, which is the point and also the risk. Approving changes without reading them is the fastest way to break a project. A vague request gets a vague result, and a long, messy CLAUDE.md gets ignored more often. Small tasks, specific prompts and a commit after each step keep the agent useful and your project safe.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If the terminal is not for you, the same agent runs as an extension in VS Code, in JetBrains IDEs, in the desktop app and on the web at claude.ai/code, where you connect a GitHub repository instead of a local folder.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart"},{"name":"Bannerbear","url":"https://www.bannerbear.com/blog/how-to-install-claude-code-terminal-ide-web-desktop-setup/"}]}]}

item.title: You can now code with AI by just typing what you want. 5 Cursor prompts to start
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Cursor Docs: Quickstart, Cursor Docs: Agent overview, Cursor Docs: Plan Mode, Cursor Docs: Rules, Cursor Help: Tab, Jetadmin, Sam on AI, The Neuron.

nf:hero.nf:alt: You can now code with AI by just typing what you want. 5 Cursor prompts to start

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Cursor for beginners: how to start coding with an AI agent, plus 5 prompts to copy","dek":"Cursor's agent can explain a project, edit files and run commands. Here is a safe order to learn it in, and where it goes wrong.","summary":"Cursor is an AI code editor with an agent that reads, edits and tests your project, plus Tab autocomplete and rules. Beginners get the best results by asking for an explanation first, making one small change, reviewing the diff and using Plan Mode for bigger work.","seo_title":"Cursor for beginners: a practical guide with 5 prompts","seo_description":"How to start with Cursor's AI agent: Agent, Tab, Plan Mode and rules explained, with five copy and paste prompts and its real weak spots.","answer_summary":"To start with Cursor, open a small project, ask the agent to explain the codebase, let it make one small change, review the diff and run your checks. Use Plan Mode for anything that touches many files.","tags":["Cursor","AI coding","AI guides","Prompts","Coding agents"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Cursor is an AI code editor. You open a folder, and an AI agent can read the project, explain it, edit files and run terminal commands for you. Next to the agent sits Tab, an autocomplete that suggests the next lines as you type. Cursor runs on macOS 12 and later, Windows 10 and later, and Linux, according to its quickstart.","sources":[{"name":"Cursor Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/get-started/quickstart"},{"name":"Cursor Docs: Agent overview","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version for beginners: let the agent explain before it edits, start with one small change, read every diff, and switch to Plan Mode for anything bigger. That order matches the quickstart Cursor gives new users, and it is the fastest way to learn the tool without breaking your project.","sources":[{"name":"Cursor Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/get-started/quickstart"},{"name":"Cursor Docs: Plan Mode","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/agent/plan-mode"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Download Cursor from cursor.com/downloads, open the app and sign in. Then pick a folder for a small first task. A personal project, a practice repo or a copy of something you do not mind changing is ideal.","sources":[{"name":"Cursor Docs: Quickstart","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/get-started/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Cursor has a free Hobby plan with limited Tab completions and limited agent requests, plus paid plans for heavier use, according to a September 2026 pricing breakdown by Jetadmin. The free plan is fine for learning. Long working sessions can hit its limits.","sources":[{"name":"Jetadmin","url":"https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/cursor-pricing-explained-plans-credit-system-and-real-costs-in-2026/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Git from day one. Cursor saves checkpoints before big agent edits, but its docs say those checkpoints are stored locally and are not a replacement for version control.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The three parts of Cursor","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent is the main one. You open it in the side pane with Cmd+I on a Mac or Ctrl+I on Windows and Linux. It can search your code and the web, read files and images, edit files, run shell commands and ask you clarifying questions, according to Cursor's docs.","sources":[{"name":"Cursor Docs: Agent overview","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Tab is the autocomplete. Suggestions show up as gray text ahead of your cursor. Press Tab to accept, Cmd+Right Arrow (Ctrl+Right Arrow on Windows and Linux) to accept one word at a time, and Escape or simply keep typing to reject. After you accept, pressing Tab again jumps to the next spot Cursor expects you to edit.","sources":[{"name":"Cursor Help: Tab","url":"https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/tab.md"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Rules are standing instructions. Project rules live as .mdc files in a .cursor/rules folder inside your project. Cursor also reads a plain AGENTS.md file in the project root. User rules, which apply to all your projects, are set under Customize, then Rules.","sources":[{"name":"Cursor Docs: Rules","url":"https://cursor.com/docs/rules"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"5 prompts to start with","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Get a map before you touch anything","text":"Ask the agent to explain the project first","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Explain the codebase","text":"Explain this codebase. Point me to the main entry points, key modules, and anything I should read before making changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Why it works","text":"This is the first prompt in Cursor's own quickstart. The agent searches the repo and summarizes how the pieces fit together. Read the answer and open the files it names. You will understand your own project faster, and your later prompts will be more precise.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Make one small, safe change","text":"Let the agent suggest, and you choose. Low risk changes like fixing copy or a small layout bug are the right size for a first try.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Three safe improvements","text":"Suggest three small, safe improvements in this codebase. Explain the tradeoffs and wait for me to choose one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Review the diff and run your checks","text":"After the agent edits, the diff view shows exactly what changed. Then have it run the checks your project already has: tests, the type checker, the linter or a local build.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Verify the change","text":"Run this project's existing checks: tests, type checker, linter and build.
Fix anything that fails because of your change.
Then list every file you changed and why, in plain English.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Use Plan Mode for anything bigger","text":"Press Shift+Tab in the agent input, or use the mode picker, to switch to Plan Mode. The agent researches the code, asks clarifying questions and writes an implementation plan. You can edit the plan before it builds anything. Cursor recommends it for features with several possible approaches, changes across many files, and requirements that are still fuzzy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Plan before you build","text":"I want to add [feature, in one or two sentences].
Ask me any questions you need first.
Then write a step by step plan, list the files you will touch, and wait for my approval before writing code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Teach Cursor your preferences once","text":"Type /create-rule in the agent and describe what you want. Cursor generates the rule file and saves it in .cursor/rules. Good first rules are about style and communication, not about the code itself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A beginner friendly rule","text":"/create-rule Always explain changes in plain English for a beginner. Keep each change small. Never delete files or add new dependencies without asking me first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Cursor falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The agent can be confidently wrong, and the bigger the task, the more ways it can drift. That is why Plan Mode exists. Cursor's own advice when a planned build goes wrong is to revert the changes, make the plan more specific and run it again, which it says is usually faster than patching a run with follow up prompts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Plain .md files in .cursor/rules are ignored, because project rules need the .mdc format with frontmatter. If a rule seems to do nothing, check the file type first. Checkpoints only restore files, not your conversation, and they live on your machine.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Cursor is also moving toward building whole apps, not only editing code. Its cloud agents can now build and publish web apps with hosting, an optional Postgres database and Cursor sign-in, on paid plans with cloud agents turned on, according to Sam on AI's November 6, 2026 brief and The Neuron.","sources":[{"name":"Sam on AI","url":"https://samonai.substack.com/p/ai-brief-november-6-2026"},{"name":"The Neuron","url":"https://www.theneuron.ai/digest/everything-that-happened-in-ai-today-friday-november-6-2026/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start every new task in a fresh chat. Old conversations carry old assumptions, and a clean start with one clear goal gets better results than a long thread.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Elon Musk's Grok does way more than answer X posts. 5 things to try
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: xAI: Welcome to Grok, xAI: Grok FAQ, X Help Center: About Grok, xAI: Skills in web, iOS, and Android, ToolChase, DataNorth AI.
item.category: xAI: Skills in web, iOS, and Android

nf:hero.nf:alt: Elon Musk smiling on stage in a dark suit.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Grok: what it is good at, where it falls short, and 5 things to try","dek":"xAI's assistant is more than a reply button on X. Here is what it does well, what it gets wrong, and prompts you can copy.","summary":"Grok searches X and the web in real time, reads large batches of files and can return Word files, slide decks and spreadsheets through built-in Skills. Its main weakness is accuracy: xAI and X both warn that it can state wrong information with confidence.","seo_title":"Grok guide: what it does well, where it fails, 5 prompts","seo_description":"How to use Grok for live X search, file analysis, Skills and Imagine, with copy and paste prompts and an honest look at its weak spots.","answer_summary":"Grok is best for questions about what is happening right now on X and the web, for reading many files at once, and for producing documents with its built-in Skills. Double-check its facts, because it can repeat rumors and make confident mistakes.","tags":["Grok","xAI","AI guides","Prompts","X"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Grok is the AI assistant from xAI. You can use it at grok.com, in the iOS and Android apps, and inside X, where it sits behind the Grok icon in the navigation bar. It is free to start; the paid SuperGrok plan raises your limits, and on X it comes with Premium and Premium+.","sources":[{"name":"xAI: Welcome to Grok","url":"https://docs.x.ai/grok/overview"},{"name":"X Help Center: About Grok","url":"https://help.x.com/en/using-x/about-grok"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: Grok is strongest when the question is about what is happening right now. It can decide on its own to search public X posts and run live web searches, so its answers can include the latest information. The same feature is its biggest weakness, because a post on X can be a rumor.","sources":[{"name":"X Help Center: About Grok","url":"https://help.x.com/en/using-x/about-grok"},{"name":"DataNorth AI","url":"https://datanorth.ai/blog/the-complete-guide-to-grok-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Grok can do","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to xAI's documentation, the core features are chat, Grok Imagine for images and video, voice conversations, file uploads for analysis and summaries, and connectors that let Grok reach your email, files and calendar inside a chat. Connectors listed by xAI include Google Drive, Gmail and Google Calendar, Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams and Salesforce.","sources":[{"name":"xAI: Welcome to Grok","url":"https://docs.x.ai/grok/overview"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"File uploads are generous. On the web you can attach about 100 files to a single message, on Android up to 20. Most files can be up to 150 MB. Grok reads PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, XLSX, PPTX, JSON, Markdown and code files, common image formats, audio such as MP3 and WAV, and MP4 and MOV video. xAI notes that images embedded in non-PDF files may not be read, and that transcription quality varies.","sources":[{"name":"xAI: Grok FAQ","url":"https://docs.x.ai/grok/faq"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Skills launched on May 18, 2026. Every account gets five built-in Skills made by xAI: Word documents, presentations, spreadsheets, PDFs and a Skill Creator. You can also save your own. xAI says Skills work at grok.com and in the iOS and Android apps.","sources":[{"name":"xAI: Skills in web, iOS, and Android","url":"https://x.ai/news/grok-skills"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"5 things to try","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Ask what X is saying about a topic","text":"This is the one thing Grok does that most assistants do not do natively. Ask for a time window and ask it to separate facts from rumors, then open the posts it links.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Live check on a topic","text":"Search X and the web for what people are saying about [topic] in the last 24 hours.
Separate confirmed facts from rumors.
Link the posts and articles you used.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Read a pile of files at once","text":"Click or tap the plus icon next to the message box, or drag files in on the web. Because you can attach many files, ask for the things a person would miss when reading them one by one: contradictions, repeated numbers, deadlines.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Summary across files","text":"Read these files and give me a one page summary.
List the key numbers, every deadline, and anything that contradicts itself across files.
Say which file each point comes from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for a real file back","text":"With the built-in Skills, Grok can create and edit a .docx file, build a slide deck, make a formatted spreadsheet and create or merge PDFs. Paste your notes and say what file you want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Notes into a deck","text":"Turn my notes below into a 6 slide presentation.
Slide 1 is a title slide. Then one key point per slide, with no more than 3 bullets each.
[paste notes]","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Save a format as a Skill","text":"Once you have fixed a format you like, ask Grok to save what it learned as a Skill. xAI says you can also build a Skill by describing it in a chat or by uploading a file. Your own version of a built-in Skill takes priority over xAI's.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Save it once","text":"Save the format we just used as a skill called [Weekly report].
Use it every time I ask for a weekly report.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Make an image or a short clip","text":"Grok Imagine creates images and video from a text prompt. Every image and video gets a Grok watermark, and xAI says removing it breaks its Acceptable Use Policy. On paid plans, image and video generation draw from your weekly usage, and video costs the most.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A simple photo","text":"A photo of [subject] on a wooden kitchen table, soft morning window light, shot from above.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Grok falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"X's own help page calls Grok an early version that can confidently give incorrect information, missummarize or miss context, and tells you to verify its answers and avoid sharing personal or sensitive information. DataNorth AI points out that grounding answers in live X posts means Grok can repeat rumors with the same confidence as established facts.","sources":[{"name":"X Help Center: About Grok","url":"https://help.x.com/en/using-x/about-grok"},{"name":"DataNorth AI","url":"https://datanorth.ai/blog/the-complete-guide-to-grok-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Image generation has limits too. ToolChase's guide says Imagine is weaker at hands, dense text inside images and specific brand likenesses, and that standard video clips run about six seconds.","sources":[{"name":"ToolChase","url":"https://toolchase.com/blog/how-to-use-grok/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid plans share one weekly usage pool across all Grok products. You can see what you have used under Settings, then Usage. When you hit the limit, paid features pause until the reset unless you buy Extra Usage Credits, which start at $5 on the web and cost more per action than your plan allowance.","sources":[{"name":"xAI: Grok FAQ","url":"https://docs.x.ai/grok/faq"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Your data","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On X, your public data and your Grok conversations may be shared with xAI to train its models. To opt out, go to Settings, then Privacy and safety, then Data sharing and personalization, then Grok and Third-party Collaborators, and turn data sharing off. You can still use Grok after that. Thumbs up and down feedback may still be used for training.","sources":[{"name":"X Help Center: About Grok","url":"https://help.x.com/en/using-x/about-grok"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Grok for the first draft of anything time sensitive, then check every claim against the links it gives you. If it gives no link, treat the claim as unverified.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Grok is a good second assistant rather than a first one for most people. If you live on X or need to know what is being said in the last few hours, it has an edge. For careful research or anything you will publish, its own makers tell you to double-check it, and that advice is worth taking.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: The Copilot button on your PC does way more than chat. Here are 5 tricks to try
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Microsoft Copilot: what it does in Windows, Edge and Office, and how to use it","dek":"How to open Copilot, search your own files, share your screen with Vision, compare Edge tabs, and use it in Word and Excel, with five prompts to copy.","summary":"Microsoft Copilot is built into Windows 11, Edge and the Microsoft 365 apps, and each version does something different. Here is how to open each one, which parts are free, which need a Microsoft 365 plan, and where it falls short.","seo_title":"Microsoft Copilot Guide: Windows, Edge, Word and Excel","seo_description":"How to use Microsoft Copilot in Windows, Edge, Word and Excel: shortcuts, file search, Vision, tab comparison, plans and five prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Press Windows key + C to open Copilot on Windows, click the Copilot icon in Edge to compare open tabs for free, and use the Copilot button in Word or Excel with a Microsoft 365 Personal, Family or Premium plan.","tags":["Microsoft Copilot","Windows 11","Microsoft Edge","Microsoft 365","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Microsoft Copilot is not one product. It is the AI assistant in Windows, the sidebar in Microsoft Edge, and a chat pane inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. Some of it is free with a Microsoft account, and some of it needs a paid Microsoft 365 plan. This guide covers what each version does, how to open it, and five prompts worth trying, based on Microsoft's own support pages.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Welcome to Copilot on Windows","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/windows/welcome-to-copilot-on-windows-675708af-8c16-4675-afeb-85a5a476ccb0"},{"name":"Microsoft Edge: Copilot in Edge","url":"https://explore.microsoft.com/edge/copilot-mode"},{"name":"Microsoft: Microsoft 365 Copilot for individuals","url":"https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/solutions/individuals"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Copilot on Windows","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Windows 11, Copilot is an app. Microsoft says new Windows 11 PCs should already have it, and if yours does not, you can get it from the Microsoft Store. You can sign in with a personal Microsoft account or a work or school account. A personal account adds chat history, image creation, longer conversations and voice.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Welcome to Copilot on Windows","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/windows/welcome-to-copilot-on-windows-675708af-8c16-4675-afeb-85a5a476ccb0"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open it","text":"Press the Copilot key if your keyboard has one, or press Windows key + C. You can also open it from the taskbar or the Start menu. Microsoft lets you choose whether the shortcut opens the full app or a smaller quick view, under Account, then Settings, then Copilot Keyboard Shortcuts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Turn on voice if you want it","text":"Copilot can listen for the wake word \"Hey, Copilot\". It is off until you turn it on. Windows Central notes you can interrupt Copilot while it is talking and pick a different voice.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Copilot needs an internet connection. Windows Central points out that it runs on models in Microsoft's cloud, not on your PC.","sources":[{"name":"Windows Central","url":"https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-get-started-with-microsoft-copilot-on-windows-11"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Search and read your own files","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Copilot on Windows can find files on your PC, open them and answer questions about them, including files synced from OneDrive. It reads .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .txt, .pdf and .json files. Two switches control this: File Search and File Read, under Account and then Settings in the Copilot app.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Welcome to Copilot on Windows","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/windows/welcome-to-copilot-on-windows-675708af-8c16-4675-afeb-85a5a476ccb0"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Give it access, then ask in plain words","text":"Turn on File Search and File Read. Then describe the file the way you remember it: the topic, roughly when you saved it, what kind of file it was. You do not need the exact file name.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Find a file and pull out what matters","text":"Find the PDF I saved about [topic] and give me the 3 main points, plus any dates or deadlines in it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you only want to ask about part of the screen, use the Copilot composer: select the plus button, then Take a Screenshot, mark the area and ask your question.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Copilot Vision: help with what is on your screen","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Copilot Vision lets Copilot see an app or browser window you share, or your phone camera in the Copilot mobile app, and answer questions about it. It only works during a voice conversation. On a PC, start voice chat with the Copilot key or Windows key + C, then select the screen share arrow. To end it, select Stop sharing. The voice chat keeps going.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Using Copilot Vision with Microsoft Copilot","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Vision can explain what you are looking at and highlight parts of the screen. It cannot click, type, scroll or do anything for you. Each Vision session also starts fresh, so Copilot does not remember the screens you shared earlier. For a personal account, Microsoft's support page lists a Microsoft 365 Personal, Family or Premium subscription as a requirement.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Using Copilot Vision with Microsoft Copilot","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Get unstuck in an app","text":"I'm stuck in this app. Walk me through how to [task], one step at a time, and point to what I should click.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep the app you are asking about on screen and do not switch windows quickly. Microsoft says that gives better answers. Windows Central's tester found Vision not very accurate, so treat it as a guide, not an authority.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Copilot in Microsoft Edge","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In Edge, Copilot lives in a side pane. Click the Copilot icon in the top right of the browser window to open it. Microsoft says Copilot in Edge is free, and a Microsoft 365 subscription raises the usage limits.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Edge: Copilot in Edge","url":"https://explore.microsoft.com/edge/copilot-mode"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Its most useful trick is reading across your open tabs. It can compare information from several pages, summarize a page, and summarize a YouTube video with key takeaways. Engadget reported in May 2026 that Microsoft retired the separate Copilot Mode because these features are now built into Edge itself, on desktop and mobile.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Edge: Copilot in Edge","url":"https://explore.microsoft.com/edge/copilot-mode"},{"name":"Engadget via AITopics","url":"https://aitopics.org/doc/news:13A93855"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Open the pages first, then ask","text":"Open two or more tabs on the same subject, such as three laptops, three hotels or three articles about the same story. Then ask Copilot to compare them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Compare your tabs","text":"Compare the open tabs and make a table of [product] options by price, [feature 1] and [feature 2]. Tell me which one fits [my need].","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Edge also has Journeys, which groups related pages, searches and chats so you can come back to a project later with one click. It is switched on from the new tab page. Microsoft says memory and similar features are optional and can be turned off.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Edge: Copilot in Edge","url":"https://explore.microsoft.com/edge/copilot-mode"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Journeys stores page titles, web addresses, searches and chats to group your history. Windows Central flags that as a privacy question. Turn it off if you share the computer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Copilot in Word and Excel","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Copilot inside the Office apps needs a paid plan. On Microsoft's plans page, Microsoft 365 Personal costs $9.99 a month and Family $12.99 a month, with Premium at $19.99 for heavier use. On the Family plan, the AI features are only for the subscription owner, not the other members.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft: Microsoft 365 Copilot for individuals","url":"https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/solutions/individuals"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In Word, select the Copilot button in the corner of a document to open the chat pane. Copilot can draft from a prompt or notes, rewrite selected text, change the tone, summarize the document and answer questions about it. Choose Chat only when you want answers without any edits to the file. Microsoft notes that Copilot supports fewer languages than Word itself.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Welcome to Copilot in Word","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/welcome-to-copilot-in-word"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Check a document before you send it","text":"Summarize this document in five bullets. Then list the decisions still needed before it is ready to share.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In Excel, select the Copilot icon in the lower right corner. It has three modes. Allow editing lets it change the workbook directly. Plan shows the steps it will take so you can confirm first. Chat only analyzes the data and answers questions without touching the file. It can write formulas, build charts and PivotTables, sort and filter, and point out trends and outliers.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Get started with Copilot in Excel","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/office/d7110502-0334-4b4f-a175-a73abdfc118a"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Find the story in a spreadsheet","text":"Look at this data and tell me the 3 biggest trends and any outliers. Then make a chart of [column] by month.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Plan mode the first few times. You see what Copilot intends to change before it touches your numbers. Microsoft's plans page also says Copilot in Excel needs AutoSave, which means the file has to be saved to OneDrive.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Excel's full editing mode works on Windows, Mac and the web. On iPhone and Android, Copilot in Excel is chat first, according to Microsoft's support page.","sources":[{"name":"Microsoft Support: Get started with Copilot in Excel","url":"https://support.microsoft.com/office/d7110502-0334-4b4f-a175-a73abdfc118a"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Copilot falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Copilot is spread across too many places, and the free and paid versions do different things. That is the main source of confusion. Usage limits on every plan exist, but Microsoft does not publish exact numbers on its plans page. Vision can show you where to click but will not do the work. And like every AI assistant, Copilot makes mistakes, so check any number or summary before you rely on it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The best place to start is the free part: Windows key + C for questions about your files, and the Edge side pane for comparing tabs. If those save you time every week, the paid Office features are worth a trial.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: NotebookLM has a new name. 4 prompts turn your notes into a podcast, quiz and study guide
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook, Google Workspace Updates, Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook, Gemini Notebook Help: Add or discover new sources, Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview, Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Flashcards or Quizzes, Layer3Labs.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM): how to turn your documents into notes, quizzes and audio","dek":"How to set up a notebook, ask questions about your own files, and use Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and reports, with prompts to copy.","summary":"Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026, but it still works the same way: you add your own sources and it answers and builds study material from them. Here is how to use each part, step by step, and where it falls short.","seo_title":"Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) Guide: Notes, Quizzes, Audio","seo_description":"How to use Gemini Notebook, formerly NotebookLM: add sources, ask cited questions, make Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and study guides.","answer_summary":"Create a notebook, add your sources (PDFs, Docs, slides, audio, links or YouTube videos), ask questions in the chat, then use the Studio panel to generate Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes, reports and more from those sources.","tags":["Gemini Notebook","NotebookLM","Google","Studying","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM, Google's research and study tool. Google announced the rename on July 16, 2026, and said the product stays a standalone research tool. The idea has not changed: you give it your own material, such as lecture notes, PDFs or a recorded talk, and it answers questions and builds study aids from that material instead of from the open web. This guide covers how to set up a notebook, how to ask good questions, and how to use Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and reports.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Google Workspace Updates","url":"https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/notebooklm-now-gemini-notebook.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If you used NotebookLM before, nothing breaks. Google's Workspace team said automatic redirects keep existing shared notebooks and links working, and the new name and logo appear across the product over several weeks. On mobile you may need to update the app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Workspace Updates","url":"https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/notebooklm-now-gemini-notebook.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Set up your first notebook","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create a notebook","text":"Open Gemini Notebook in your browser and select Create new notebook. In the window that opens, choose Upload a source. Use one notebook per subject or project. Each notebook is separate, and Gemini Notebook cannot pull information from several notebooks at once, so a notebook for your biology class will not know what is in your history notebook.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add the right sources","text":"Select Add sources on the left. Gemini Notebook accepts PDFs, Google Docs, Google Slides, Google Sheets, Word, PowerPoint, TXT, Markdown, CSV and ePub files, images, audio files such as MP3 and WAV, pasted text, web links, public YouTube videos and Gemini chats. Each source can hold up to 500,000 words, or 200 MB for an uploaded file, and free users can add up to 50 sources per notebook. Sources from Google Drive sync automatically, but footnotes and comments in those files are not imported.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"No material yet: type a question into the search box in the Sources panel and pick Web or Drive. Gemini Notebook shows results you can import. Turn on Deep Research for a longer search that takes a few minutes; Google says that option is only for users over 18.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ask questions about your own files","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Once sources are in, the chat panel shows a summary of them and suggested questions. Answers draw on the notebook's sources and include citations that link back to the passage they came from, according to Layer3Labs' walkthrough. You can also switch individual sources off in the Sources panel to narrow what an answer uses.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Find what matters for the test","text":"Using only my sources, explain [topic] in plain words. Then list the 5 facts I am most likely to be tested on, and point to where each one appears.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Spot the gaps","text":"Compare what [source 1] and [source 2] say about [topic]. List where they agree, where they disagree, and anything one covers that the other leaves out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Click the citations on anything you plan to quote or memorize. The answer is only as good as the passage behind it, and checking takes seconds.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Turn your notes into a podcast","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Audio Overviews live in the Studio panel. Google's help center lists four formats: Deep Dive, the default, where two hosts discuss your sources; The Brief, one speaker giving the key points in under two minutes; The Critique, two hosts giving feedback on something like an essay; and The Debate, two hosts arguing different sides. You can choose Shorter, Default or Longer, though Longer works in English only. More than 80 languages are supported.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Generate an Audio Overview with a focus","text":"In Studio, open Audio Overview, pick a format and length, and add a prompt that says what to focus on and how expert the listener is. It generates in the background, which can take a couple of minutes, so you can keep working. You can download the audio when it is done.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A beginner's audio lesson","text":"Focus only on [chapter or topic]. Explain it for a beginner, use one everyday example per idea, and end with the 3 points I must remember.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is also an Interactive mode. When you create a new Audio Overview with it switched on, you can select Join while listening and ask the hosts a question by voice; they answer from your sources and then carry on. Google says it is English only, works only on newly generated overviews, and may have delays or audio glitches.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Quiz yourself with flashcards and quizzes","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Customize before you generate","text":"In Studio, select Flashcards or Quizzes to generate right away, or click the pencil icon first to customize. You can set the difficulty to easy, medium or hard, choose fewer, standard or more items, and add a prompt about the topic, audience or style.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Questions that test understanding","text":"Make questions only about [topic]. Mix definitions with questions that ask me to apply an idea to a new example. Skip anything not in my sources.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"While you study, the Explain button gives the reasoning behind a card or an answer. On flashcards you mark each card Got it! or Missed it!, and Gemini Notebook saves your progress. At the end you can practice again with the same cards, all cards, or only the ones you missed. Flashcards can be downloaded as a CSV file.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Flashcards or Quizzes","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16958963"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build study guides and reports","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Studio panel also makes notes, Video Overviews, mind maps, data tables, slide decks, infographics and reports. Report types include a study guide, a briefing document, an FAQ or a custom report, and a report can be exported to Google Docs from its three dot menu. Edits you make in the exported Doc do not sync back to the notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A one page study guide","text":"Create a one page study guide on [topic]: key terms with short definitions, a timeline of the main events, and 5 practice questions with answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gemini Notebook is only as good as what you put in. If your sources are thin or wrong, its answers and quizzes will be too, and it will not tell you what your notes are missing unless you ask. Google itself warns that Audio Overviews are AI generated and can contain inaccuracies, so treat them as a way to review, not as the final word. It also cannot combine notebooks, and the mobile app may not support every feature. For a quick fact check against the open web, a search tool is still the better fit; for learning a specific set of material well, this is the tool to use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free accounts get the core features. Google's paid AI plans raise the limits on notebooks, sources and daily generations, and some newer features, such as code that runs inside a notebook to analyze data, started with Google AI Ultra users before a wider rollout.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]}]}

item.title: You're using Perplexity like Google. 4 habits turn it into a real research assistant
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?, Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?, Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?, Fast Company, Dupple, Fello AI.
item.category: Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?
Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?

nf:hero.nf:alt: A young woman holding a laptop at a library table covered in stacks of books, with the Perplexity logo on the wall.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Perplexity: how to research with sources you can actually check","dek":"How to ask better questions, choose where Perplexity searches, verify its citations, and use Research mode and Projects for bigger jobs.","summary":"Perplexity searches the web and answers with numbered citations, but the answer is only as good as the question and the sources behind it. Here is how to set up each step, which features need a paid plan, and where Perplexity falls short.","seo_title":"Perplexity Guide: How to Research With Sources","seo_description":"How to use Perplexity for research: narrow questions, the sources menu, checking citations, Research mode and Projects, with copy and paste prompts.","answer_summary":"Ask a specific question, choose the right sources (Web, Academic, Social or Finance), click the numbered citations to check each claim, and select Research in the mode selector when you need a full cited report.","tags":["Perplexity","AI search","Research","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity is an AI search engine. You type a question, it searches the web in real time, and it writes an answer with numbered footnotes that link to the pages it used. That last part is what makes it useful for research: you can check every claim. The catch is that most people read the answer and never open a single source. This guide covers how to ask, how to pick sources, how to check the citations, and when to use Research mode and Projects.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a narrow question","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity handles plain, conversational questions, but specific questions get better answers. Fast Company gives a simple example: a query for the latest breakthroughs in EV battery recycling methods works better than just typing EV batteries. Answers also keep context inside a thread, so you can ask a follow up without repeating the whole question.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Name the topic, the time frame and the output","text":"Say what you want to know, which period it covers, and what shape the answer should take: a list, a comparison, a short summary. If dates matter, ask for the date of each source so you can see how fresh the information is.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: What changed recently","text":"What changed in [topic] between [month, year] and today? Use only sources published in that period, list the 3 most important changes, and give the date of each source.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Keep digging in the same thread","text":"Ask your follow ups as replies in the same thread instead of starting a new search. Perplexity keeps the earlier questions in context, so you can go from a broad overview to one specific detail in a few steps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose where it searches","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The search box has a sources menu that sets where Perplexity looks. Web is the default and covers news, current events and popular sites. Academic leans on scientific papers, scholarly articles and research journals. Social pulls in discussions and firsthand experiences from people, and Finance focuses on market data, company reports and investment news, according to Fast Company.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Switch to Academic for health, science and research questions","text":"When the question is about evidence, not opinion, set the sources to Academic before you search. Then ask Perplexity to separate strong findings from early ones.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: What the studies say","text":"Summarize what peer reviewed studies say about [question]. Separate strong evidence from early or small studies, and say where the studies disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Social when you want real experiences, like how owners feel about a product after a year. Treat those answers as opinions, not facts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Check the citations","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Each answer has numbered citations, and clicking one opens the original page. Dupple's guide warns that the AI can still get things wrong and recommends clicking through to verify claims, especially statistics. Fast Company makes the same point: the citations exist so you can read the summary in its original context.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Ask which source supports which claim","text":"After a long answer, ask Perplexity to map each claim to its source. Then open the sources for the claims you plan to use, and read the sentence yourself. If a number is not on the page, do not use it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Show your work","text":"For each claim in your last answer, tell me which numbered source supports it. Flag any claim that no source directly supports.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Research mode for the big questions","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Research mode is Perplexity's deeper option. According to its help center, it runs many searches, reads a large number of sources and reasons through them to write a full report. You turn it on by selecting Research from the mode selector in the search box, on the web, the mobile apps and the Mac app. Most tasks finish in under 3 minutes, but some take 4 to 5 minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10738684-what-is-research-mode"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free users get limited access to Research mode and Pro subscribers get extended access. Limits reset on a rolling basis, not on a fixed date. You cannot pick the model in Research mode; Perplexity chooses it. When the report is done, you can export it as a PDF or a document, or turn it into a Perplexity Page to share.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10738684-what-is-research-mode"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A full report","text":"Write a research report on [topic] for [who it is for]. Cover [point 1], [point 2] and [point 3], end with a short list of open questions, and cite a source for every number.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For quick everyday questions, the faster standard search is enough. Perplexity describes Pro Search as the deeper option for complex questions: it may ask you follow up questions to refine what you want, and free accounts get a limited number of Pro Searches.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Keep long research in a Project","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Projects are the new name for what Perplexity used to call Spaces; the company renamed them on July 30, 2026, according to Fello AI. A Project keeps searches, files, instructions and connected tools in one place, so you can return to the same research over time.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352961-what-are-projects"},{"name":"Fello AI","url":"https://felloai.com/perplexity-spaces/"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Create a Project","text":"Open the Projects section in the left sidebar and select New project. Give it a title of up to 50 characters. You can add a description, an icon and a color.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Add instructions and files","text":"In the Project settings, add instructions of up to 8,000 characters. They apply to every query you run in that Project, so this is where you put your preferred format or the kinds of sources you trust. Then upload files or whole folders.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The help center lists the same file limits on every plan: up to 10,000 files and 5 GB per Project, with each file up to 100 MB. On personal accounts a Project is visible only to people you give access to, and you can add up to 5 contributors.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352961-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Perplexity falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity is a research shortcut, not a replacement for reading. A summary can flatten a nuance, mix up two sources, or attach a number to the wrong page. The citations make those mistakes easy to catch, but only if you open them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is also not the best tool for every search. Dupple notes that Google is still better for going straight to a specific website or finding a local business. Several features, including more Pro Searches and file uploads, are tied to the paid Pro plan, which both Fast Company and Dupple list at $20 a month.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you share anything Perplexity wrote, open at least the sources behind the numbers. If you cannot find the claim on the page, leave it out.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Most people use Gemini like a search box. These 4 features make it work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A Gem is Gemini with your instructions saved. On gemini.google.com click Explore Gems, then New Gem. It is free on every plan. You make it on the web, then use it on your phone too. Preview it on the right before you click Save. Click Add files under the chat box, then Upload or Add from Drive. Up to 10 files per prompt. Sources: Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems, Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files, Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app, Zapier: Gemini Gems, Zapier: Gemini connected apps, Chrome Story.
