item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Gemini: a practical guide to Gems, file uploads and Gmail and Drive","dek":"How to build a Gem that remembers your instructions, what Gemini can do with your files, and how to let it search your own Google Workspace.","summary":"Gems, file uploads and the Google Workspace connection are the three Gemini features that matter most for everyday work. Here is how to set up each one, the current limits, and where each one falls short.","seo_title":"Gemini Guide: Gems, File Uploads, Gmail and Drive","seo_description":"How to create Gemini Gems, write instructions, upload files and connect Gmail, Drive and Calendar, with copy and paste prompts and the current limits.","answer_summary":"Create a Gem on gemini.google.com with Explore Gems and New Gem, upload files with the Add files button (up to 10 per prompt), and connect Google Workspace so you can ask about your Gmail, Drive, Docs and Calendar.","tags":["Gemini","Google","Gemini Gems","Google Workspace","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Most people open Gemini, type a question and close the tab. Three features change that: Gems, which save your instructions so you stop repeating them, file uploads, which let Gemini read your documents, videos and code, and the Google Workspace connection, which lets it search your own Gmail, Drive, Docs and Calendar. All three are documented in Google's Gemini Apps Help pages. This guide covers how to set up each one, the limits Google lists, and where each one falls short.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15235603"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gems: set your instructions once","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A Gem is a saved version of Gemini with your own instructions about goals, behavior and output format. Zapier compares Gems to custom GPTs in ChatGPT: you set them up once and reuse them every time. Chrome Story reports that Gems are free on every Gemini plan, including the free tier, so you do not need Google AI Pro or Ultra to make one.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15235603"},{"name":"Zapier: Gemini Gems","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/gemini-gems/"},{"name":"Chrome Story","url":"https://chromestory.com/2026/07/create-gem-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the Gem builder","text":"Go to gemini.google.com on a computer and sign in. In the panel on the left, click Explore Gems, then New Gem. Gems can only be created and edited in the web app. Once saved, they also show up in the Gemini mobile app, where you can chat with them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Name it and write the instructions","text":"Give the Gem a short name you will recognize in a list, such as Email editor or Trip planner. Then write the instructions. Google suggests covering up to four things: the persona (the role the Gem plays), the task (what it should do), the context (background, as much as you can give) and the format (how the answer should look). You do not need all four.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A starting template for any Gem","text":"You are my [role, for example email editor].
Your task is to [what you want done every time].
Context: [who I am, who the audience is, anything it should always know].
Format: [for example bullet points, under 150 words, plain language].
If anything in my request is unclear, ask me one question before you answer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If writing instructions feels like work, type one or two sentences about your goal into the instructions box and use the Use Gemini to re-write instructions option. It expands your draft into fuller instructions. Read the result and cut anything you did not mean before you save.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add knowledge files","text":"Under Knowledge, click Add files, then choose Upload files for something on your computer or Drive for a file in Google Drive. A style guide, a price list or a set of past examples works well here. If you do not want the Gem to cite these files in its answers, select Disable knowledge citations.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Preview, then save","text":"Type a test request in the preview panel on the right. The preview does not save anything, so adjust the instructions until the answers look right, then click Save. To change a Gem later, open your Gems list and click the pencil icon next to it. The three dot menu has Make a copy, which also works on Google's premade Gems.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A writing editor Gem","text":"You are a careful editor for [my newsletter / my work emails].
When I paste a draft, fix grammar and spelling, cut filler words and keep my voice.
Do not add new facts or change numbers.
Return the edited text first, then a short list of the three biggest changes you made.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gems have real limits. According to Zapier, they cannot be used with Gemini Live, they do not take actions outside the chat window, and they cannot use connected apps. So a Gem is best for repeated writing, editing and planning tasks, not for anything that needs your inbox or calendar.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: what Gemini can read","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini web app, click the Add files button below the text box. Upload takes a file from your device and Add from Drive takes one from Google Drive. Under More Uploads you can also import a code folder or a GitHub repository. According to Google, most file types are supported and you can add up to 10 files in the same prompt. Videos can be up to 2 GB each and most other files up to 100 MB.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Length limits depend on the plan. Google says the total video length is up to 5 minutes, or up to 1 hour with Google AI Pro or Ultra, and the total audio length is up to 10 minutes, or up to 3 hours on those plans. One code folder or GitHub repository can be added per chat, with up to 5,000 files and 100 MB. Upload limits are rolling, so if you hit one, you may have to wait before uploading more.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Get the useful part of a long PDF","text":"Read the attached file.
1. Summarize it in five bullet points.
2. List every deadline, date and number that I need to act on, with the page it appears on.
3. Tell me what is missing or unclear.
Only use what is in the file. If something is not in it, say so.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google warns that very large uploads can lead to answers that miss details or connections across the content. If you need precise answers, upload fewer files at once and ask about one document at a time. If Gemini clearly misreads a file, upload it again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gmail, Drive and Calendar: ask about your own stuff","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Google Workspace app connects Gemini to your Gmail, Docs and Drive for summaries and lookups, to Google Tasks and Google Keep for reminders, notes and lists, and to Google Calendar for events. To point Gemini at one service, type @ and pick it from the list. Google says to use keywords from the content rather than pasting a link to an email or a document.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Connect Google Workspace","text":"Sign in to Gemini with the same account you use for Gmail and Drive. Keep Activity must be on, or Gemini cannot connect. In Gmail, the setting Smart features in other Google products also has to be on; after you turn it on, reload Gemini. Work and school accounts need the administrator to allow the connection first. To disconnect later, use the Connected Apps settings page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Clear your inbox backlog","text":"@Gmail Find emails from the last 7 days that ask me to reply, decide or send something.
For each one, give me the sender, what they need and by when.
Sort them by deadline, soonest first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Prepare for a meeting","text":"@Google Calendar What is my next meeting with [name]?
@Drive Find the latest documents that mention [project].
Give me a five line briefing: what the meeting is about, what changed since we last met, and two questions I should ask.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The limits matter here. Google lists them plainly: Gemini cannot see comments or images inside Docs and Gmail, or pictures and videos in Drive. It cannot create folders or move files in Drive, cannot count items in Drive or Gmail, and cannot report your storage. In a new chat, name the service in your first prompt; follow up questions in the same chat do not need it. Zapier adds that the list of connected apps and their availability varies by country.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"},{"name":"Zapier: Gemini connected apps","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/gemini-connected-apps/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The Workspace connection is the most useful of the three for busy people, and also the one that needs the most checking. Google itself notes that Gemini can hallucinate or give outdated information here, so open the emails and files it cites before you act on a summary.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where to start","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start with one Gem for the task you repeat most, such as editing emails. Use uploads when you have one long document to understand. Turn on the Workspace connection when you spend too long searching your own inbox, and always check the sources it shows.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Stop pasting the same files into Claude. 3 features that do the work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A project is a workspace with its own chats, files and instructions. Free accounts can make up to five. Add your reference files once and every chat in that project can use them. Start chats from inside the project, not the main sidebar. Click + in the chat box, then Add files or photos. PDFs, Word files, CSVs, spreadsheets and images all work. Sources: Claude Help Center: What are projects, Claude Help Center: RAG for projects, Claude Help Center: Uploading files, Claude Help Center: Artifacts, Claude: Artifacts, Ascendient Learning, Maginative, Developers Digest, Kevin Stratvert.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Claude Projects, file uploads and artifacts: a practical guide","dek":"How to set up a Claude project, write instructions that stick, get the most from uploaded files and turn answers into documents and tools.","summary":"Projects, file uploads and artifacts are the three Claude features that matter most for everyday work. Here is how to set up each one, what the limits are and where each one falls short.","seo_title":"Claude Projects, Files and Artifacts: A Practical Guide","seo_description":"How to set up Claude Projects, write project instructions, upload PDFs and spreadsheets, and create artifacts, with copy and paste prompts and current limits.","answer_summary":"Create a project, add instructions and reference files once, start every chat from inside it, upload files with the + button in the chat box, and ask Claude for a document, deck or tool to get an artifact beside the chat.","tags":["Claude","Anthropic","Claude Projects","Artifacts","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you use Claude for the same kind of work every week, three features save the most time: Projects, file uploads and artifacts. Projects are self-contained workspaces with their own chat history and knowledge base, according to Anthropic's help center. File uploads let Claude read your PDFs, documents, spreadsheets and images. Artifacts are the documents, decks, dashboards and small tools Claude builds in a panel beside the conversation. This guide covers how to set up each one, the limits that apply and where each one falls short.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: What are projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects"},{"name":"Claude Help Center: Uploading files","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-uploading-files-to-claude"},{"name":"Claude Help Center: Artifacts","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Projects: set the context once","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic says Projects are available to every user, including free accounts, and that free users can create up to five projects. Each project has a knowledge base, where you add documents, text and code, and a set of instructions that shape how Claude answers inside it, such as a more formal tone or the point of view of a specific role.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: What are projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create the project","text":"Go to Projects and create a new one. Give it a name you will recognize later, like the client, the class or the report. According to Ascendient Learning, Claude does not read the project name or description; they are only there to help you stay organized.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Write the instructions","text":"Open the project's instructions and write the brief you would otherwise paste into every chat. Ascendient Learning notes the instructions are added at the start of every conversation in the project. Say who Claude is helping, who the audience is, the format you want, the tone and where the facts come from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Project instructions starter","text":"You are helping me with [project name]. The audience is [who will read the work].
Write in a [tone] tone. Keep answers under [length] unless I ask for more.
Use the files in this project as your main source. If something is not in the files, say so instead of guessing.
When I ask for a draft, give me one version first, then a short list of what you would change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add your reference files","text":"Upload the material the work depends on, such as a brief, a style guide, a plan or last quarter's numbers, to the project's files. Once they are there, every chat in the project can use them, so you do not upload the same document again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Start chats from inside the project","text":"Open the project and start a new chat there. Ascendient Learning points out that a chat started from the main sidebar has no project context, which is the most common reason people think their instructions are being ignored.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On paid plans (Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise), a project can hold more material than fits in Claude's context window. When the knowledge base gets close to that limit, Claude switches to retrieval mode, which Anthropic says can expand capacity by up to 10 times. It turns on automatically and the project shows an indicator when it is active. Anthropic recommends clear, descriptive file names and naming the document you mean in your question.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: RAG for projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11473015-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-for-projects"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Team and Enterprise plans, projects can be shared with colleagues, who can be given view or edit access. Free, Pro and Max accounts do not get project sharing, according to the help center.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: What are projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep one project per piece of work, not one giant project for everything. Smaller projects keep Claude focused on the right files and make the instructions easier to get right.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: what Claude can read","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude accepts PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX documents, plus JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images. Spreadsheets in XLSX format need the code execution and file creation setting turned on. To upload, click the + button in the lower left of the chat box and choose Add files or photos, or drag files into the window. You can also paste an image from your clipboard.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Uploading files","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-uploading-files-to-claude"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In a single chat, the limits are 500 MB per file, up to 20 files, images up to 8000 by 8000 pixels and PDFs up to 1,000 pages. For PDFs of 100 pages or fewer, Claude also analyzes charts, images and graphics. Longer PDFs are read as text only. Other document types are read for text only, so Claude will not see images embedded in a Word file. Files added to a project have a 30 MB limit per file.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Uploading files","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-uploading-files-to-claude"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Get the key points out of a long PDF","text":"Read the attached PDF. Give me:
1. A five-sentence summary.
2. Every date, deadline and number that matters, in a table with the page number for each.
3. Anything that looks unclear or contradictory.
Use the page numbers shown in my PDF viewer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"When you point Claude to a page, use the page number your PDF viewer shows, not the number printed on the page. Anthropic recommends this because the two often differ. If a file is too big, split it into sections.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Check a spreadsheet before you send it","text":"Look at the attached spreadsheet. Tell me which columns have missing values, which numbers look out of range compared with the rest of the column, and any totals that do not add up. Then suggest three charts that would explain this data to [audience].","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Artifacts: from answer to finished work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An artifact is a standalone piece of work, such as a document, a slide deck, a design, a dashboard or a small interactive tool, that opens in its own window beside the chat. Anthropic says Claude creates one when the content is substantial, self-contained and likely to be edited or reused. You can ask for one in the chat, pick Output in the message box, or start from the Artifacts tab, where everything you create is saved.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Artifacts","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them"},{"name":"Claude: Artifacts","url":"https://claude.com/features/artifacts"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Turn on the setting","text":"Artifacts need Cloud code execution and file creation. On Free, Pro and Max, it is under Settings, Capabilities. On Team and Enterprise, an owner turns it on in the organization settings.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Ask for the output, not just an answer","text":"Be specific about the format: a one-page document, a ten-slide deck or a simple calculator. Then ask for changes in the chat, or edit a template artifact directly, for example by typing in a doc or changing a slide.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Fix and share","text":"If an artifact shows an error, use Try fixing with Claude near the error. Artifacts start private, and you choose when to share them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic's help center lists Docs, Slides and Design templates as a beta for paid plans. Docs export to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, and Slides export to PowerPoint or PDF. Artifacts can also call Claude themselves, which lets them work as small apps, and each person who uses a shared one does so with their own account and plan limits.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Artifacts","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them"},{"name":"Developers Digest","url":"https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/claude-design-slides-and-docs"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Turn notes into a shareable document","text":"Turn my notes below into a one-page document for [audience]. Use a short title, three sections with headings, and a final list of next steps with an owner for each. Keep it under 400 words.

[paste your notes]","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where these features fall short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Projects only help if you start chats inside them, and the five-project cap on free accounts fills up fast. Non-PDF documents lose their images, and long PDFs lose their charts, so a chart buried in a Word file or on page 300 of a report will be missed. Artifacts are good for drafts and simple tools, but they still need a human check before anything goes out. Treat a published artifact from someone you do not know with the same caution as a file from an unknown sender, which is what Anthropic advises.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Stop using ChatGPT like a search box. 4 features that make it work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open Projects in the left menu, name it, then add files, instructions or old chats. Everything inside carries over to every new chat in that project, so you stop repeating yourself. Plus gets 20 files per project, Pro 40. Say it plainly: "Remember that I'm vegetarian when you suggest recipes." Saved memories stay even if you delete the chat. Ask ChatGPT to forget something, or manage it all in Settings. Sources: OpenAI Academy: Projects, OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ, OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ, OpenAI Academy: Working with files, Unite.AI, DataCamp.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"ChatGPT for everyday work: how to use Projects, memory and file uploads","dek":"Set up Projects, control what ChatGPT remembers, use Temporary Chat and get real work out of your PDFs and spreadsheets.","summary":"Projects, memory, Temporary Chat and file uploads turn ChatGPT into a work tool. Here is how to set up each one, with copy and paste prompts and the limits that apply on each plan.","seo_title":"ChatGPT Projects, Memory and File Uploads: A Practical Guide","seo_description":"How to set up ChatGPT Projects, manage memory, use Temporary Chat and upload files, with copy and paste prompts and current limits.","answer_summary":"Create a project from the left menu, add instructions and files, tell ChatGPT what to remember in plain words, use Temporary Chat for one-off questions, and attach files from the tools menu with a specific request.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","ChatGPT Projects","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Four ChatGPT features do most of the heavy lifting for everyday work: Projects, memory, Temporary Chat and file uploads. Projects keep the files, instructions and chats for one piece of work together. Memory lets ChatGPT keep details you want it to know. Temporary Chat keeps a conversation out of all of that. File uploads let it read your PDFs, documents, spreadsheets and images. This guide shows how to set up each one and when to skip it.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Projects","url":"https://openai.com/academy/projects"},{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"},{"name":"OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545-file-uploads-faq"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Projects: one place for one job","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI describes a project as a dedicated space for a body of work. Each project holds its own files and instructions, and they apply to every chat inside it, so you do not have to upload the same document or repeat the same background in each new conversation.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Projects","url":"https://openai.com/academy/projects"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create the project","text":"Open Projects from the left-hand menu, create a new project and give it a name you will recognize later, such as the client, the class or the trip.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add instructions","text":"Write the guidance you would otherwise paste into every chat: who you are, who the work is for, the tone you want, and what to avoid. Project instructions apply to the chats in that project and take priority over your general custom instructions there, according to Unite.AI.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add files","text":"Upload the reference material the project depends on, like a brief, a style guide or last quarter's numbers. OpenAI's file FAQ lists project limits of 20 files on Plus and 40 files on Pro, Team, Education and Business plans.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Move old chats in","text":"If you already have conversations about the same work, move them into the project. DataCamp notes you can drag a chat into a project or add it from the chat's menu.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some plans also offer project-only memory, which limits ChatGPT's context to conversations inside that same project. OpenAI says this helps keep projects separate. Unite.AI reported that the option is chosen when a project is created and cannot be switched on for an existing one, so decide before you start. On plans that support sharing, collaborators can work from the same files, instructions and history.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Projects","url":"https://openai.com/academy/projects"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/how-to-use-chatgpts-project-memory/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use a project for work that runs over days or weeks: research, a draft you revise in stages, recurring planning. For a quick, self-contained question, a normal chat is faster.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Write your project instructions","text":"You are helping me with [project name]. I am [your role], and the work is for [audience].
Always write in [tone] and keep answers under [length].
Use the files in this project as the main source. If something is not in the files, say so instead of guessing.
Before long answers, ask me one clarifying question if the request is unclear.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Memory: what ChatGPT keeps about you","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"ChatGPT has two kinds of memory, according to OpenAI's help center. Saved memories are details you ask it to keep, and they stay until you delete them, even if you delete the chat where they came up. Chat history lets ChatGPT draw on past conversations to learn your interests and preferences, and those details can change over time.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Save something on purpose","text":"Tell ChatGPT directly what to keep. A clear sentence with a reason works best, because it tells the model when the detail applies.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Save a useful memory","text":"Remember that I work in [industry] and write for [audience]. When I ask for emails or summaries, use plain American English and keep them under [number] words.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Check and clean it up","text":"Ask ChatGPT what it remembers about you. To remove a detail, ask it to forget it. OpenAI says a forgotten item can take a few days to stop being referenced, and the original conversation stays unless you delete it too.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Where the controls live depends on which memory system your account has. In the older system, saved memories are under Settings, then Personalization, where you can search them, delete single entries or delete all. OpenAI says a newer memory system is rolling out first to Plus and Pro users in the US, with its controls under Settings, then Memory. Turning off Reference saved memories also turns off Reference chat history. On Enterprise and Edu plans, workspace owners decide whether memory is on.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Audit your memory","text":"List everything you currently remember about me, grouped by topic. Mark anything that looks outdated or that you are unsure about, so I can tell you what to forget.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Temporary Chat: when you want a clean slate","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Temporary Chats do not appear in your chat history. In the new memory system, OpenAI says they also do not use your existing memories or create new ones. That makes them the right choice when you do not want a conversation to shape future answers.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Temporary Chat for a one-off question about a topic you do not want following you around, or to see how ChatGPT answers without your saved preferences. It is not a delete button for something you already said in a normal chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: let ChatGPT read the document","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Attach the file","text":"In a chat, open the tools menu and choose Add photos or files. OpenAI lists CSV, XLSX, PDF, DOCX, JPEG, PNG and TXT among the supported formats, and uploads work on the web and in the iOS and Android apps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Ask for something specific","text":"A file plus a vague request gets a vague answer. Say what you want back: a summary with risks, a table, a chart, or a rewrite. ChatGPT can also produce files you download, such as an updated spreadsheet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Pull the facts out of a PDF","text":"Read the attached PDF. Make a table with these columns: date, what happens, who owns it, and the page it comes from. Then list any deadlines in the next [number] days.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Make sense of a spreadsheet","text":"Look at the attached spreadsheet. Tell me in five bullet points what changed the most from [period] to [period], then make one chart that shows it. Explain any column you are not sure how to read.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The limits matter more than most people expect. OpenAI's file FAQ says free users get 3 file uploads per day, and everyone is limited to 80 files every 3 hours.
